## Common Pitfalls

- Don't truncate inputs when passing files or content to the API. If the content is too long to fit in the context window, notify the user and discuss options (chunking, summarization, etc.) rather than silently truncating.
- **Prefill removed (Fable 5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, and the 4.6/4.7/4.8 family):** Assistant message prefills (last-assistant-turn prefills) return a 400 error on Fable 5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, and Sonnet 4.6. Use structured outputs (`output_config.format`) or system prompt instructions to control response format instead. (One exception: the fallback-credit prefill claim — when redeeming a credit with `fallback_has_prefill_claim: true`, the server accepts the echoed assistant message; see the migration guide's refusal section.)
- **Confirm migration scope before editing:** When a user asks to migrate code to a newer Claude model without naming a specific file, directory, or file list, **ask which scope to apply first** — the entire working directory, a specific subdirectory, or a specific set of files. Do not start editing until the user confirms. Imperative phrasings like "migrate my codebase", "move my project to X", "upgrade to Sonnet 4.6", or bare "migrate to Opus 4.8" are **still ambiguous** — they tell you what to do but not where, so ask. Proceed without asking only when the prompt names an exact file, a specific directory, or an explicit file list ("migrate `app.py`", "migrate everything under `services/`", "update `a.py` and `b.py`"). See `shared/model-migration.md` Step 0.
- **`max_tokens` defaults:** Don't lowball `max_tokens` — hitting the cap truncates output mid-thought and requires a retry. For non-streaming requests, default to `~16000` (keeps responses under SDK HTTP timeouts). For streaming requests, default to `~64000` (timeouts aren't a concern, so give the model room). Only go lower when you have a hard reason: classification (`~256`), cost caps, deliberately short outputs, or **`max_tokens: 0`** for cache pre-warming (see `shared/prompt-caching.md` → Pre-warming).
- **Disabling thinking on Claude Opus 5 has two failure modes — prefer low/medium effort instead.** Only affects code that explicitly opts out; thinking is on by default, so watch for a disabled-thinking setting carried forward from Opus 4.8. With `thinking: {type: "disabled"}`, the model occasionally writes a tool call into its **visible text** instead of a `tool_use` block: the turn succeeds, the call never runs, no error is raised, and in an agentic loop that text pollutes later turns. It can also leak `<thinking>` tags into the response. Turning thinking on and lowering `effort` fixes both and still cuts cost. If a route must stay thinking-off: add *"You may say a brief sentence before using a tool"*, **delete** any don't-think/don't-reason rule (it makes tag leakage worse), and use a generic *"Do not include internal or system XML tags in your response"* rather than naming thinking tags. Details: `shared/model-migration.md` → Two failure modes when thinking is disabled.
- **128K output tokens:** Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6 support up to 128K `max_tokens`, but the SDKs require streaming for values that large to avoid HTTP timeouts. Use `.stream()` with `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()`.
- **Tool call JSON parsing (Fable 5, Opus 5, and the 4.6/4.7/4.8 family):** Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, and Sonnet 4.6 may produce different JSON string escaping in tool call `input` fields (e.g., Unicode or forward-slash escaping). Always parse tool inputs with `json.loads()` / `JSON.parse()` — never do raw string matching on the serialized input.
- **Structured outputs (all models):** Use `output_config: {format: {...}}` instead of the deprecated `output_format` parameter on `messages.create()`. This is a general API change, not 4.6-specific.
- **Don't reimplement SDK functionality:** The SDK provides high-level helpers — use them instead of building from scratch. Specifically: use `stream.finalMessage()` instead of wrapping `.on()` events in `new Promise()`; use typed exception classes (`Anthropic.RateLimitError`, etc.) instead of string-matching error messages; use SDK types (`Anthropic.MessageParam`, `Anthropic.Tool`, `Anthropic.Message`, etc.) instead of redefining equivalent interfaces.
- **Error handling — catch a chain, not one broad class.** A single `except APIStatusError` / `catch (AnthropicServiceException)` / `rescue APIError` loses the distinction between retryable (429, ≥500, network) and non-retryable (400/404) failures. Write a most-specific-first chain — e.g. `NotFoundError` → `RateLimitError` → `APIStatusError` → `APIConnectionError` (or the Go equivalent: `errors.As` into `*anthropic.Error` then `switch apierr.StatusCode { case 404: …; case 429: …; default: … }`). Per-language class names and namespaces are in `shared/error-codes.md`.
- **Don't research SDK types — write first.** If a type name isn't shown in the documentation included in this skill, write the code file from the namespace/package tables in the language-specific doc and let the compiler's error point you to the right name. Do not spend turns on WebFetch, SDK-repo clones, or compiling-and-running a separate reflection program to discover type names before writing — produce the source file first, then fix what the compiler reports. A quick `strings` / `jar tf` / `javap` against the installed SDK is acceptable for locating names (it returns in seconds), but don't escalate beyond that. A file with a wrong type name is recoverable; a session spent on discovery with no file written is not.
- **Bash and text editor tools are Anthropic-defined, schema-less.** Declare `{"type": "bash_20250124", "name": "bash"}` / `{"type": "text_editor_20250728", "name": "str_replace_based_edit_tool"}` — no `input_schema`. A custom tool with your own schema named `"bash"` is a different tool. Handler paths and security checks are in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` § Client-Side Tools.
- **Advisor tool model pairing.** The advisor tool's `model` must be at least as capable as the request's top-level `model` — e.g. executor `claude-sonnet-5` → advisor `claude-opus-4-8` or `claude-opus-4-7`. An invalid pair returns 400. Pairing table in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` § Advisor. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **Agent Skills ≠ Managed Agents.** To have Claude generate a `.pptx`/`.xlsx`/etc. via Agent Skills, call `client.beta.messages.create` with `container={"skills": [...]}`, the `code_execution_20260521` tool, and both `code-execution-2025-08-25` + `skills-2025-10-02` betas. Do not use `client.beta.agents` / `sessions` / `environments` here — those are the Managed Agents surface, not Agent Skills.
- **MCP connector needs both halves.** `mcp_servers=[{type:"url", url, name}]` alone is rejected as a validation error — also add `tools=[{type:"mcp_toolset", mcp_server_name:<same name>}]` with beta `mcp-client-2025-11-20`. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **`inference_geo` is a direct top-level request parameter** — `client.messages.create(..., inference_geo="us")` / `.inferenceGeo("us")`. Do not put it in `extra_body` / `putAdditionalBodyProperty`. (Messages API only — on Managed Agents, `inference_geo` instead nests inside the agent's `model` object, never top-level; see `shared/managed-agents-core.md` § Pinning inference geography.) Supported on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and later; availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`. `response.usage.inference_geo` reports where inference ran.
- **Fine-grained tool streaming is not a beta feature.** Set `eager_input_streaming: true` on the tool definition and call the regular `client.messages.stream(...)`. There is no beta header and no `client.beta.*` path.
- **Cache diagnostics is beta.** Use `client.beta.messages.*` with beta `cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07`. Pass `diagnostics: {previous_message_id: null}` on the first turn and `diagnostics: {previous_message_id: <previous response id>}` on subsequent turns; the result is on `response.diagnostics`. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **Memory tool type is `memory_20250818`.** Declare `{"type": "memory_20250818", "name": "memory"}`. Go uses the beta-namespace type `{OfMemoryTool20250818: &anthropic.BetaMemoryTool20250818Param{}}` on `client.Beta.Messages.New`; Python/TypeScript/Ruby/PHP/C# use the non-beta `client.messages.create`; Java has both a non-beta `MemoryTool20250818` and a beta tool-runner path. Python/TypeScript provide `BetaAbstractMemoryTool` / `betaMemoryTool` helpers for implementing the backend.
- **Use a model the feature actually supports.** Some features are restricted to specific model tiers — fast mode is Claude Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 only (and Claude API only), task budgets (Messages API only — Managed Agents session budgets have no model-tier restriction) are Claude Opus 5 / Fable 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.8 / 4.7 only, and the advisor tool requires a valid executor↔advisor pair. If the user's prompt names a model that the feature doesn't support, use a supported model instead and note the substitution in the output.
- **Don't define custom types for SDK data structures:** The SDK exports types for all API objects. Use `Anthropic.MessageParam` for messages, `Anthropic.Tool` for tool definitions, `Anthropic.ToolUseBlock` / `Anthropic.ToolResultBlockParam` for tool results, `Anthropic.Message` for responses. Defining your own `interface ChatMessage { role: string; content: unknown }` duplicates what the SDK already provides and loses type safety.
- **Report and document output:** For tasks that produce reports, documents, or visualizations, the code execution sandbox has `python-docx`, `python-pptx`, `matplotlib`, `pillow`, and `pypdf` pre-installed. Claude can generate formatted files (DOCX, PDF, charts) and return them via the Files API — consider this for "report" or "document" type requests instead of plain stdout text.
- **Server-tool errors don't raise.** Web search and web fetch errors return HTTP 200 with a `web_search_tool_result` / `web_fetch_tool_result` block whose `content` is a single error object (e.g. `{error_code: "max_uses_exceeded"}`) — not a raised exception. For web search, a success `content` is a *list*; an error `content` is an *object* — branch on that before indexing.
- **Code execution output block type:** `code_execution_20260521` returns `bash_code_execution_tool_result` (with `.content.stdout`), **not** the legacy bare `code_execution_tool_result`. Iterate `response.content` and match on the correct type.
- **Tool search: never defer everything.** The search tool itself must not have `defer_loading: true`, and at least one tool in `tools` must be non-deferred, or the API returns 400 `All tools have defer_loading set`.

# Claude API — Python

## Installation

```bash
pip install anthropic
```

## Client Initialization

```python
import anthropic

# Default — resolves credentials from the environment:
# ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, or an `ant auth login` profile.
# Prefer this for local dev; don't hardcode a key.
client = anthropic.Anthropic()

# Explicit API key (only when you must inject a specific key)
client = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key="your-api-key")

# Async client
async_client = anthropic.AsyncAnthropic()
```

---

## Client Configuration

### Per-request overrides

Use `with_options()` to override client settings for a single call without mutating the client:

```python
client.with_options(timeout=5.0, max_retries=5).messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
)
```

### Timeouts

Default request timeout is 10 minutes. Pass a float (seconds) or an `httpx.Timeout` for granular control. On timeout the SDK raises `anthropic.APITimeoutError` (and retries per `max_retries`).

```python
import httpx

client = anthropic.Anthropic(timeout=20.0)
client = anthropic.Anthropic(
    timeout=httpx.Timeout(60.0, read=5.0, write=10.0, connect=2.0),
)
```

### Retries

The SDK auto-retries connection errors, 408, 409, 429, and ≥500 with exponential backoff (default 2 retries). Set `max_retries` on the client or via `with_options()`; `max_retries=0` disables.

### Async performance (aiohttp backend)

For high-concurrency async workloads, install `anthropic[aiohttp]` and pass `DefaultAioHttpClient` instead of the default httpx backend:

```python
from anthropic import AsyncAnthropic, DefaultAioHttpClient

async with AsyncAnthropic(http_client=DefaultAioHttpClient()) as client:
    ...
```

### Custom HTTP client (proxy, base URL)

Use `DefaultHttpxClient` / `DefaultAsyncHttpxClient` — not raw `httpx.Client` — so the SDK's default timeouts and connection limits are preserved:

```python
from anthropic import Anthropic, DefaultHttpxClient

client = Anthropic(
    base_url="http://my.test.server.example.com:8083",  # or ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL env var
    http_client=DefaultHttpxClient(proxy="http://my.test.proxy.example.com"),
)
```

### Logging

Set `ANTHROPIC_LOG=debug` (or `info`) to enable SDK logging via the standard `logging` module.

---

## Basic Message Request

```python
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}
    ]
)
# response.content is a list of content block objects (TextBlock, ThinkingBlock,
# ToolUseBlock, ...). Check .type before accessing .text.
for block in response.content:
    if block.type == "text":
        print(block.text)
```

---

## System Prompts

```python
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    system="You are a helpful coding assistant. Always provide examples in Python.",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "How do I read a JSON file?"}]
)
```

### Mid-conversation system messages (model-gated)

For operator instructions that arrive mid-conversation (mode switches, injected state), append `{"role": "system", ...}` to `messages` instead of editing top-level `system` — this preserves the cached prefix and carries operator authority. Must follow a user message (or an `assistant` message ending in server-tool use), and must be either the last entry in `messages` or be followed by an `assistant` turn; cannot be `messages[0]`. Unsupported models return a 400 (`role 'system' is not supported on this model`). See `shared/prompt-caching.md` for when to use this vs. top-level `system`.

```python
response = client.messages.create(
    model=MODEL_ID,  # must support mid-conversation system messages
    max_tokens=16000,
    system=[{"type": "text", "text": STABLE_SYSTEM, "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}],
    messages=history + [
        {"role": "user", "content": user_message},
        {"role": "system", "content": "Terse mode enabled — keep responses under 40 words."},
    ],
)  # No beta header needed — use regular client.messages.create
```

---

## Vision (Images)

### Base64

```python
import base64

with open("image.png", "rb") as f:
    image_data = base64.standard_b64encode(f.read()).decode("utf-8")

response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    messages=[{
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {
                "type": "image",
                "source": {
                    "type": "base64",
                    "media_type": "image/png",
                    "data": image_data
                }
            },
            {"type": "text", "text": "What's in this image?"}
        ]
    }]
)
```

### URL

```python
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    messages=[{
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {
                "type": "image",
                "source": {
                    "type": "url",
                    "url": "https://example.com/image.png"
                }
            },
            {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image"}
        ]
    }]
)
```

## Prompt Caching

Cache large context to reduce costs (up to 90% savings). **Caching is a prefix match** — any byte change anywhere in the prefix invalidates everything after it. For placement patterns, architectural guidance (frozen system prompt, deterministic tool order, where to put volatile content), and the silent-invalidator audit checklist, read `shared/prompt-caching.md`.

### Automatic Caching (Recommended)

Use top-level `cache_control` to automatically cache the last cacheable block in the request — no need to annotate individual content blocks:

```python
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    cache_control={"type": "ephemeral"},  # auto-caches the last cacheable block
    system="You are an expert on this large document...",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the key points"}]
)
```

### Manual Cache Control

For fine-grained control, add `cache_control` to specific content blocks:

```python
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    system=[{
        "type": "text",
        "text": "You are an expert on this large document...",
        "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}  # default TTL is 5 minutes
    }],
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the key points"}]
)

# With explicit TTL (time-to-live)
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    system=[{
        "type": "text",
        "text": "You are an expert on this large document...",
        "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h"}  # 1 hour TTL
    }],
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the key points"}]
)
```

### Verifying Cache Hits

```python
print(response.usage.cache_creation_input_tokens)  # tokens written to cache (~1.25x cost)
print(response.usage.cache_read_input_tokens)      # tokens served from cache (~0.1x cost)
print(response.usage.input_tokens)                 # uncached tokens (full cost)
```

If `cache_read_input_tokens` is zero across repeated identical-prefix requests, a silent invalidator is at work — `datetime.now()` or a UUID in the system prompt, unsorted `json.dumps()`, or a varying tool set. See `shared/prompt-caching.md` for the full audit table.

---

## Extended Thinking

> **Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, and Sonnet 4.6:** Use adaptive thinking. `budget_tokens` is removed on Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Opus 4.8, and 4.7 (400 if sent); deprecated on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6.
> **Claude Opus 5:** thinking is on by default — omitting `thinking` runs adaptive (`{"type": "adaptive"}` is equivalent), unlike Opus 4.8/4.7 where omitting it meant no thinking. `{"type": "disabled"}` is accepted only at effort `high` or lower; pairing it with `xhigh`/`max` returns a 400.
> **Older models:** Use `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` (must be < `max_tokens`, min 1024).

```python
# Fable 5 / Claude Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 / 4.7 / 4.6: adaptive thinking (recommended)
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    thinking={"type": "adaptive", "display": "summarized"},  # display opt-in: default is omitted (empty thinking text) on Fable 5 / Mythos 5 / Claude Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 / 4.7
    output_config={"effort": "high"},  # low | medium | high | xhigh | max
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Solve this step by step..."}]
)

# Access thinking and response
for block in response.content:
    if block.type == "thinking":
        print(f"Thinking: {block.thinking}")
    elif block.type == "text":
        print(f"Response: {block.text}")
```

---

## Error Handling

```python
import anthropic

try:
    response = client.messages.create(...)
except anthropic.BadRequestError as e:
    print(f"Bad request: {e.message}")
except anthropic.AuthenticationError:
    print("Invalid API key")
except anthropic.PermissionDeniedError:
    print("API key lacks required permissions")
except anthropic.NotFoundError:
    print("Invalid model or endpoint")
except anthropic.RateLimitError as e:
    retry_after = int(e.response.headers.get("retry-after", "60"))
    print(f"Rate limited. Retry after {retry_after}s.")
except anthropic.APIStatusError as e:
    if e.status_code >= 500:
        print(f"Server error ({e.status_code}). Retry later.")
    else:
        print(f"API error: {e.message}")
except anthropic.APIConnectionError:
    print("Network error. Check internet connection.")
```

---

## Response Helpers

Every response object exposes `_request_id` (populated from the `request-id` header) — log it when reporting failures to Anthropic. Despite the underscore prefix, this property is public.

```python
message = client.messages.create(...)
print(message._request_id)       # req_018EeWyXxfu5pfWkrYcMdjWG
print(message.to_json())          # serialize the Pydantic model
print(message.to_dict())          # plain dict
```

To access raw headers or other response metadata, use `.with_raw_response`:

```python
raw = client.messages.with_raw_response.create(
    model="claude-opus-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
)
print(raw.headers.get("request-id"))
message = raw.parse()  # the Message object messages.create() would have returned
```

## Multi-Turn Conversations

The API is stateless — send the full conversation history each time.

```python
class ConversationManager:
    """Manage multi-turn conversations with the Claude API."""

    def __init__(self, client: anthropic.Anthropic, model: str, system: str = None):
        self.client = client
        self.model = model
        self.system = system
        self.messages = []

    def send(self, user_message: str, **kwargs) -> str:
        """Send a message and get a response."""
        self.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": user_message})

        response = self.client.messages.create(
            model=self.model,
            max_tokens=kwargs.get("max_tokens", 16000),
            system=self.system,
            messages=self.messages,
            **kwargs
        )

        assistant_message = next(
            (b.text for b in response.content if b.type == "text"), ""
        )
        self.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": assistant_message})

        return assistant_message

# Usage
conversation = ConversationManager(
    client=anthropic.Anthropic(),
    model="claude-opus-5",
    system="You are a helpful assistant."
)

response1 = conversation.send("My name is Alice.")
response2 = conversation.send("What's my name?")  # Claude remembers "Alice"
```

**Rules:**

- Consecutive same-role messages are allowed — the API combines them into a single turn
- First message must be `user`
- `role: "system"` messages are allowed mid-conversation on supporting models (no beta header needed) — see § Mid-conversation system messages above

---

### Compaction (long conversations)

> **Beta, Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, and Sonnet 4.6.** When conversations approach the 200K context window, compaction automatically summarizes earlier context server-side. The API returns a `compaction` block; you must pass it back on subsequent requests — append `response.content`, not just the text.

```python
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()
messages = []

def chat(user_message: str) -> str:
    messages.append({"role": "user", "content": user_message})

    response = client.beta.messages.create(
        betas=["compact-2026-01-12"],
        model="claude-opus-5",
        max_tokens=16000,
        messages=messages,
        context_management={
            "edits": [{"type": "compact_20260112"}]
        }
    )

    # Append full content — compaction blocks must be preserved
    messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response.content})

    return next(block.text for block in response.content if block.type == "text")

# Compaction triggers automatically when context grows large
print(chat("Help me build a Python web scraper"))
print(chat("Add support for JavaScript-rendered pages"))
print(chat("Now add rate limiting and error handling"))
```

---

## Stop Reasons

The `stop_reason` field in the response indicates why the model stopped generating:

| Value | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `end_turn` | Claude finished its response naturally |
| `max_tokens` | Hit the `max_tokens` limit — increase it or use streaming |
| `stop_sequence` | Hit a custom stop sequence |
| `tool_use` | Claude wants to call a tool — execute it and continue |
| `pause_turn` | Model paused and can be resumed (agentic flows) |
| `refusal` | Claude refused for safety reasons — check `stop_details` |

### Structured Stop Details

When `stop_reason` is `"refusal"`, the response includes a `stop_details` object with structured information about the refusal:

```python
if response.stop_reason == "refusal" and response.stop_details:
    print(f"Category: {response.stop_details.category}")   # e.g. "cyber", "bio", "reasoning_extraction", "frontier_llm", or None — see docs for the full set
    print(f"Explanation: {response.stop_details.explanation}")
```

### Refusal Fallbacks (Claude Fable 5) — opt in by default

Fallbacks are **opt-in**: without them a refused request simply stops. Include the server-side `fallbacks` parameter in `claude-fable-5` code by default — on a policy decline the API re-runs the same request on the fallback model inside the same call. A decline before any output isn't billed (a mid-stream decline bills the streamed partial); the rescue bills at the fallback model's own rates, with cache repricing applied automatically.

```python
response = client.beta.messages.create(
    model="claude-fable-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    betas=["server-side-fallback-2026-06-01"],
    fallbacks=[{"model": "claude-opus-4-8"}],
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "..."}],
)

# Switch points: one fallback block per model that ran and declined this turn
for block in response.content:
    if block.type == "fallback":
        print(f"{block.from_.model} declined; {block.to.model} continued")

# Served-by signal — covers sticky turns, which carry no fallback block.
# Pair with stop_reason: the fallback model can itself refuse.
fallback_ran = any(
    entry.type == "fallback_message" for entry in response.usage.iterations or []
)
if fallback_ran and response.stop_reason != "refusal":
    print(f"Served by {response.model}")
```

A `stop_reason: "refusal"` on the final response means the whole chain refused. The header must be exactly `server-side-fallback-2026-06-01` **for this array form**; the newer `fallbacks: "default"` scalar form uses `server-side-fallback-2026-07-01` instead (see `shared/model-migration.md` → Migrating to Claude Opus 5 → New API features), and pairing either header with the other form returns a 400. The parameter is rejected on the Batches API and unavailable on Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry — register the client-side `BetaRefusalFallbackMiddleware` on the client there instead. Full semantics (sticky routing, billing, streaming, echoing fallback turns back): `shared/model-migration.md` → Migrating to Claude Fable 5 → `refusal` stop reason.

## Cost Optimization Strategies

### 1. Use Prompt Caching for Repeated Context

```python
# Automatic caching (simplest — caches the last cacheable block)
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    cache_control={"type": "ephemeral"},
    system=large_document_text,  # e.g., 50KB of context
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the key points"}]
)

# First request: full cost
# Subsequent requests: ~90% cheaper for cached portion
```

### 2. Choose the Right Model

```python
# Default to Opus for most tasks
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5",  # $5.00/$25.00 per 1M tokens
    max_tokens=16000,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain quantum computing"}]
)

# Use Sonnet for high-volume production workloads
standard_response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-5",  # $3.00/$15.00 per 1M tokens
    max_tokens=16000,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize this document"}]
)

# Use Haiku only for simple, speed-critical tasks
simple_response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-haiku-4-5",  # $1.00/$5.00 per 1M tokens
    max_tokens=256,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Classify this as positive or negative"}]
)
```

### 3. Use Token Counting Before Requests

```python
count_response = client.messages.count_tokens(
    model="claude-opus-5",
    messages=messages,
    system=system
)

estimated_input_cost = count_response.input_tokens * 0.000005  # $5/1M tokens
print(f"Estimated input cost: ${estimated_input_cost:.4f}")
```

## Retry with Exponential Backoff

> **Note:** The Anthropic SDK automatically retries rate limit (429) and server errors (5xx) with exponential backoff. You can configure this with `max_retries` (default: 2). Only implement custom retry logic if you need behavior beyond what the SDK provides.

```python
import time
import random
import anthropic

def call_with_retry(
    client: anthropic.Anthropic,
    max_retries: int = 5,
    base_delay: float = 1.0,
    max_delay: float = 60.0,
    **kwargs
):
    """Call the API with exponential backoff retry."""
    last_exception = None

    for attempt in range(max_retries):
        try:
            return client.messages.create(**kwargs)
        except anthropic.RateLimitError as e:
            last_exception = e
        except anthropic.APIStatusError as e:
            if e.status_code >= 500:
                last_exception = e
            else:
                raise  # Client errors (4xx except 429) should not be retried

        delay = min(base_delay * (2 ** attempt) + random.uniform(0, 1), max_delay)
        print(f"Retry {attempt + 1}/{max_retries} after {delay:.1f}s")
        time.sleep(delay)

    raise last_exception
```
</doc>

```text
1	# claude-hud statusline shows the raw model id (`claude-opus-5[1m]`) instead of a friendly name
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
4	- The claude-hud statusline shows the literal pinned model string —
5	  `claude-opus-5[1m]`, `claude-opus-4-8[1m]` — with the `[1m]` suffix visible,
6	  instead of a readable name like `Opus 5 (1M context)`
7	- **The same dotfiles config renders differently on two machines** — friendly
8	  name on one host, raw id on another, with identical
9	  `.claude/settings.local.json` and identical chezmoi-managed claude-hud config
10	- No error anywhere; `claude --version` works, the statusline renders fine
11	  otherwise, and the model itself works (requests succeed)
12	- Possibly alongside: context percentage in the HUD climbing ~5× faster than
13	  expected, or exceeding 100%
14	
15	**First seen**: 2026-07
16	**Affects**: claude-hud (any version — the fallback is by design), Claude Code
17	older than ~2.1.220, any model id carrying the Claude Code-only `[1m]` suffix
18	**Status**: not a bug in claude-hud or the pin — fixed by upgrading Claude Code
19	on the lagging host
20	
21	## Symptom
22	
23	Two machines, same chezmoi-managed dotfiles, same project pin
24	(`ANTHROPIC_MODEL = "claude-opus-5[1m]"` in `.claude/settings.local.json`):
25	
26	| Host | Claude Code | statusline shows |
27	|---|---|---|
28	| macOS | 2.1.220 | `Opus 5 (1M context)` |
29	| Ubuntu | 2.1.207 | `claude-opus-5[1m]` |
30	
31	## Root cause
32	
33	The friendly name is **not** computed by claude-hud — it comes from the
34	`model.display_name` field that **Claude Code** puts in the statusline JSON it
35	pipes to the statusline command. claude-hud's `getModelName()`
36	(`~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-hud/claude-hud/<ver>/src/stdin.ts`) is:
37	
38	```ts
39	const displayName = stdin.model?.display_name?.trim();
40	if (displayName) return displayName;          // "Opus 5 (1M context)"
41	const modelId = stdin.model?.id?.trim();
42	if (!modelId) return 'Unknown';
43	return normalizeBedrockModelLabel(modelId) ?? modelId;   // "claude-opus-5[1m]"
44	```
45	
46	So **seeing the raw id means `display_name` was absent or empty** — the raw id
47	is the fallback branch, not a formatting choice.
48	
49	Why it's absent: `[1m]` is a Claude Code-only suffix, not a real API model id.
50	Claude Code has to strip it and match the remainder against its built-in model
51	table to produce a display name (and to size the context window). A Claude Code
52	old enough to predate the model in that table matches nothing, so it emits no
53	`display_name` — and claude-hud falls back.
54	
55	This is the same table-matching mechanism behind the older "dotted ids cause the
56	`[Opus 4] retired` warning and a >100% context HUD" gotcha in
57	[`docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md`](../docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md) —
58	different trigger (stale binary vs wrong id shape), identical failure path.
59	
60	## Why it can be more than cosmetic
61	
62	claude-hud reads the context window size **straight from Claude Code** — it does
63	not infer it from the model id:
64	
65	```ts
66	const size = stdin.context_window?.context_window_size;
67	```
68	
69	If the same unrecognized-model condition also makes Claude Code assume a 200k
70	window for a model that actually serves 1M, the HUD's context percentage runs
71	~5× high and compaction triggers on the wrong budget. Treat a raw-id statusline
72	as a signal to check the context percentage too, not just a cosmetic annoyance.
73	
74	## Fix
75	
76	Upgrade Claude Code on the lagging host:
77	
78	```sh
79	ssh <host> 'claude update'
80	# or, through this repo's upgrade path (justfile → cat_agents → `claude update`)
81	just upgrade-agents
82	```
83	
84	## Why `chezmoi apply` / `fleet-apply` does not fix it
85	
86	By design — see AGENTS.md → "Install vs upgrade is split on purpose". `chezmoi
87	apply` and ansible are install-only (`state: present`, `creates:`), so a host
88	that already has *some* `claude` binary is never bumped by an apply. Version
89	drift across the fleet accumulates silently until something like this surfaces
90	it, and `just upgrade-*` has to be run **on each host** — `fleet-apply` does not
91	broadcast upgrades.
92	
93	Consequence for debugging: "same config, different behavior across machines" is
94	much more often a **binary version skew** than a config-drift problem in this
95	repo. Check `claude --version` (or the equivalent) on both hosts before
96	diffing configs.
97	
98	`claude` is not on the non-interactive SSH PATH on Linux — a bare
99	`ssh host 'claude --version'` returns `claude: not on PATH` even though it is
100	installed at `~/.local/bin/claude`. Augment PATH, or use `fleet exec`, which
101	carries the PATH prelude for exactly this reason (see
102	[`docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`](../docs/tools/fleet-exec.md)).
103	
104	## Related
105	
106	- [`claude-hud-usage-statusline-stale`](claude-hud-usage-statusline-stale.md)
107	- claude-hud's config is chezmoi-managed — live edits get reverted on apply; see
108	  [`docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`](../docs/tools/agent-overlays.md)
109
```

80	```
81	
82	- **native** — Claude Code's own `cost.total_cost_usd` on stdin. This is the
83	  normal path for a subscription session.
84	- **estimate** — derived from `sessionTokens`, so it *does* inherit the
85	  main-thread blind spot above. Only used when stdin carries no cost.
86	
87	Claude Code's accumulator adds every request unconditionally:
88	
89	```js
90	if (e.totalCost += r, e.requestCount++, t.attributionAgent)
91	    zUo(e.byAgent, t.attributionSkill ?? t.attributionAgent, r)
92	```
93	
94	`attributionAgent` only drives a per-agent breakdown; it does not gate the
95	total. So **`Cost` includes subagents and workflows, `Tokens` does not.** When
96	the two disagree, `Cost` is the complete one.
97	
98	### Verified, not inferred
99	
100	A controlled run pins both halves down at once. Force the main thread onto
101	haiku and the subagent onto sonnet, then read `--output-format json`:
102	
103	```console
104	$ claude -p --output-format json --model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 \
105	    'Use the Agent tool with subagent_type "general-purpose" and model "sonnet" …'
106	```
107	
108	```text
109	total_cost_usd                        0.13825985
110	  claude-haiku-4-5  (main thread)     0.06095585
111	  claude-sonnet-5[1m] (subagent)      0.077304
112	                                      ──────────
113	  sum                                 0.13825985   exact match
114	```
115	
116	The subagent is 56% of the bill and is unambiguously counted. Meanwhile the
117	transcripts show the reverse:
118	
119	```text
120	MAIN transcript  (the only file claude-hud reads)
121	   models = ['claude-haiku-4-5-20251001']
122	<session-id>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl  (never read)
123	   models = ['claude-sonnet-5']
124	```
125	
126	The subagent's model never appears in the main transcript, but does appear in
127	`modelUsage` and in the cost. One experiment, both claims.
128	
129	> Naively summing `usage` over the main transcript gives ~1.7× the figure in
130	> `modelUsage`, because Claude Code dual-logs the same API response 2–3 times.
131	> claude-hud dedupes by `message.id` (see the comment in `src/transcript.ts`);
132	> ad-hoc scripts must do the same or they will overcount.
133	
134	## Cache: input-side only, and the countdown is a snapshot
135	
136	### There is no output cache
137	
138	Anthropic prompt caching applies to the **input prefix** only. The four usage
139	fields:
140	
141	| Field | Meaning | Rough price |
142	|---|---|---|
143	| `input_tokens` | fresh input, not served from cache | 1× |
144	| `cache_creation_input_tokens` | prefix **written** to cache | 1.25× |
145	| `cache_read_input_tokens` | prefix **read** from cache | **0.1×** |
146	| `output_tokens` | generated tokens | output rate |
147	
148	This is why the breakdown above shows `in=92k` against `cache_read=98.30M`:
149	after the first request almost the entire prefix (system prompt, tool
150	definitions, history) hits cache, and only the newest delta is fresh.
151	
152	Output is never cached as output — but this turn's output becomes part of next
153	turn's input prefix, and *then* becomes cacheable. That is the only route by
154	which generated text enters the cache.
155	
156	### The countdown freezes when idle — by design, not a bug
157	
158	`showPromptCache` renders a plain arithmetic expression, evaluated at render
159	time (`src/render/lines/prompt-cache.ts`):
160	
161	```js
162	const remainingMs = (lastAssistantResponseAt.getTime() + ttlSeconds * 1000) - now;
163	```
164	
165	There is no timer inside claude-hud. The value only changes when **Claude Code
166	re-invokes the statusline command**, which it does on state change (debounced
167	300 ms), never on a wall clock. So:
168	
169	- **During an active turn** it tends to sit near `5m 0s`, because
170	  `lastAssistantResponseAt` advances with every assistant message and an agent
171	  turn produces one every few seconds. It is genuinely resetting, not stuck.
172	- **Once the turn ends** nothing triggers a re-render, so the last computed
173	  string stays frozen on screen.
174	
175	The countdown is live — invoking the command by hand on a fixed transcript
176	shows `5m 0s → 4m 56s → 4m 52s` across three calls four seconds apart. The
177	practical limitation is the inverse of what you want: it cannot show you a
178	nearly-expired cache while you sit idle, which is precisely when that would be
179	useful. Treat it as "how fresh was the cache at the last render".
180	
181	Why it matters in money: letting the TTL lapse means the prefix is re-billed as
182	`cache_creation` (1.25×) instead of `cache_read` (0.1×) — a 12.5× swing on the
183	prefix. `promptCacheTtlSeconds` defaults to 300 and should match the TTL your
184	requests actually use.
185	
186	## First-line truncation follows a fixed order
187	
188	Segments render in this native order, and the line is cut at terminal width:
189	
190	```text
191	model, project, advisor, sessionName, version, extra, duration, cost, speed, auth
192	```
193	
194	`cost` is 8th of 10, so it is among the first things to disappear — you get
195	`Cost $…` while a random session slug survives. Do not fix this by switching
196	elements off; reorder instead. `orderFirstLineParts` emits listed segments in
197	your order and **appends every unlisted key after them**, so a partial list
198	works and whatever lands last is what truncation eats:
199	
200	```json
201	"projectLineOrder": [
202	  "model", "project", "duration", "cost",
203	  "extra", "advisor", "speed", "auth",
204	  "sessionName", "version"
205	]
206	```
207	
208	`modelFormat: "compact"` additionally drops the `(1M context)` suffix, which the
209	Context line already reports as `218k/1.0M`.
210	
211	## `sessionName` is a random slug unless you name the session
212	
213	`magical-noodling-horizon` and friends are a fallback, not an identifier:
214	
215	```js
216	result.sessionName = customTitle ?? latestSlug;
217	```
218	
219	`customTitle` comes from `claude -n <name>` / `--name <name>`, described by the
220	CLI as *"Set a display name for this session (shown in the prompt box, /resume
221	picker, and terminal title)"*. Without it you get an auto-generated slug.
222	
223	It is **unrelated to the session UUID** that `--resume` keys on. It is purely a
224	human-readable label for the `/resume` picker and the terminal title — useless
225	noise until you start launching named sessions, at which point it becomes the
226	fastest way to find a session again.
227

```text
1	# Codex warns "Model metadata for `gpt-5.6-sol` not found" after using the Copilot gateway
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): `Model metadata for gpt-5.6-sol not found`; `Defaulting to fallback metadata; this can degrade performance and cause issues.`; the model still answers successfully; `codex debug models --bundled` contains the model but normal `codex debug models` does not; `~/.codex/models_cache.json` contains only Copilot adapter models such as `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`
4	**First seen**: 2026-08
5	**Affects**: Codex CLI 0.147.0 with a custom `copilot-api` provider; observed with `@jeffreycao/copilot-api` 2.1.0
6	**Status**: fixed locally in `codex-copilot` with a versioned bundled `model_catalog_json` override plus live gateway token limits
7	
8	## Symptom
9	
10	```
11	⚠ Model metadata for `gpt-5.6-sol` not found. Defaulting to fallback metadata; this can degrade performance and cause issues.
12	```
13	
14	The warning is misleading as a model-availability signal: the same session can
15	send `POST /responses` with `model: gpt-5.6-sol` and receive HTTP 200 responses.
16	
17	Reproduction:
18	
19	1. Start the Copilot gateway and run `codex-copilot` with `gpt-5.6-sol`.
20	2. Let Codex refresh `/models?client_version=0.147.0` through the custom provider.
21	3. Observe that `~/.codex/models_cache.json` has only a small adapter subset.
22	4. Start another session and observe the fallback-metadata warning.
23	
24	Useful comparison:
25	
26	```sh
27	codex debug models --bundled | jq -r '.models[].slug' | grep gpt-5.6-sol
28	codex debug models           | jq -r '.models[].slug' | grep gpt-5.6-sol
29	```
30	
31	The first command finds Sol while the second can return nothing.
32	
33	## Root cause
34	
35	Codex uses one global `~/.codex/models_cache.json`; the cache is not namespaced
36	by `model_provider`. A custom-provider model refresh can therefore replace the
37	first-party catalog with the subset Codex derives from the Copilot gateway.
38	
39	In the observed case the gateway's raw `/models` response contained 17 entries,
40	including `gpt-5.6-sol`, but Codex persisted only three Gemini adapter records.
41	That provider-global cache then took precedence over the model metadata bundled
42	inside the same Codex 0.147.0 binary.
43	
44	Deleting `~/.codex/models_cache.json` appears to fix the next launch but is not
45	durable: another custom-provider refresh can recreate the degraded cache.
46	
47	## Workaround
48	
49	`codex-copilot` generates the installed binary's bundled catalog once per Codex
50	version:
51	
52	```sh
53	codex debug models --bundled \
54	  > ~/.cache/copilot-proxy/codex-models/codex-cli_0.147.0.json
55	```
56	
57	It then prepends this per-process override:
58	
59	```toml
60	model_catalog_json = "~/.cache/copilot-proxy/codex-models/codex-cli_0.147.0.json"
61	```
62	
63	The launcher also passes the selected model's live
64	`model_context_window` and `model_auto_compact_token_limit` from the gateway,
65	because bundled limits can lag Copilot's entitlement-specific long-context
66	values. Explicit user `-c` arguments remain later in argv and still win.
67	
68	## Prevention
69	
70	- Keep `_copilot_codex_catalog_file` version-keyed and validate `.models` before
71	  atomically replacing its cache file.
72	- Do not "fix" this by deleting `~/.codex/models_cache.json` on every launch;
73	  plain Codex owns that cache and other providers may need it.
74	- Keep the live token-limit injection paired with the bundled catalog override.
75	- Regression coverage lives in `tests/unit/copilot_proxy.bats`.
76	
77	## Related
78	
79	- `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh`
80	- `docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md`
81	- `pitfalls/copilot-api-caches-degraded-model-list-at-startup.md`
82	- Codex configuration reference: <https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference>
83
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# copilot-api caches a degraded / geo-filtered model list at startup → every Claude request 400s
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
4	- Claude Code against the Copilot proxy dies instantly with
5	  `API Error: 400 {"error":{"message":"The requested model is not supported.","code":"model_not_supported",...}}`
6	- Startup banner lists **no `claude-*` ids** — only `gpt-*`, `gemini-*`, embeddings
7	- `curl` through Clash/Verge still sees Claude in `/models`, but the running
8	  `copilot-api` process does not
9	- OpenCode's GitHub Copilot provider shows the same Claude-less list
10	- It "used to work" under Clash for Windows **TUN / Mixin** (all TCP captured),
11	  and broke after switching to System Proxy only (Clash Verge without TUN)
12	
13	**First seen**: 2026-07
14	**Affects**: `@jeffreycao/copilot-api`, OpenCode native GitHub Copilot, any Node
15	  client that ignores the macOS System Proxy on a GFW host
16	**Status**: upstream geo-filters Anthropic models by egress; mitigated locally by
17	  `COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY=auto` → `--proxy-env` + `HTTPS_PROXY` on start, plus
18	  `copilot-proxy doctor` direct-vs-via-proxy A/B
19	
20	## Root causes (two look identical)
21	
22	### A. Egress geo-filter (most common after leaving TUN)
23	
24	Same token, same enterprise account:
25	
26	| Path | Claude count |
27	|---|---:|
28	| Direct / CN egress (`curl --noproxy '*'`) | 0 |
29	| Via overseas Clash node (e.g. SG VLESS) | 8 |
30	
31	Node/`copilot-api`/`OpenCode` do **not** read macOS System Proxy. With only
32	System Proxy on (no TUN), they fetch the direct catalog and cache 0 Claude for
33	the process lifetime. `curl` still shows Claude because it honors System Proxy —
34	which is why `doctor` used to mis-label this as "org entitlement".
35	
36	### B. Flaky node / truncated response
37	
38	A single degraded Clash hop during the one-shot `/models` fetch caches a short
39	list. Restart after the node is healthy.
40	
41	## Fix
42	
43	```bash
44	proxy-status                 # should show Verge/mihomo port (e.g. 7897)
45	copilot-proxy restart        # auto attaches --proxy-env when a local proxy is up
46	copilot-proxy doctor         # expect: upstream via proxy has claude; served has claude
47	
48	# non-GFW machine / force direct:
49	COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY=never copilot-proxy restart
50	
51	# force a port:
52	COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897 copilot-proxy restart
53	```
54	
55	OpenCode: launch with `HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897` (or enable TUN).
56	
57	## Related
58	
59	- Shell: `~/.config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh`, `50_networking.sh` (`proxy-status`)
60	- Docs: `docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md`
61
```
</details></tool-use>

 `./pitfalls/copilot-proxy-openai-model-silent-stall.md`

```text
1	# OpenAI models via `copilot-proxy` sit at `0 tok` for minutes, then need Esc + "continue"
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
4	- Claude Code on a `gpt-*` / `gemini-*` model through the proxy shows no output
5	  at all for minutes — FleetView / the Task line reads `gpt-5.6-sol[1m] · 0 tok`
6	  while the timer keeps climbing
7	- Nothing wrong appears anywhere: `copilot-proxy status` is healthy,
8	  `copilot-proxy logs` shows `--> POST /v1/messages?beta=true 200`, no 4xx/5xx
9	- Occasionally the session never recovers and the only way out is Esc
10	  (`[Request interrupted by user]`) followed by typing `continue`
11	- Sometimes it surfaces instead as
12	  `API Error: Connection lost mid-response. The response above may be incomplete.`
13	  or `API Error: Connection closed mid-response.`
14	- `copilot-proxy logs` has `<-- POST /v1/messages?beta=true` lines with **no**
15	  matching `--> POST` line (count them: `grep -c '^<-- POST'` vs `grep -c '^--> POST'`)
16	
17	**First seen**: 2026-08
18	**Affects**: `@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0` behind
19	`dot_config/shell/copilot-throttle-shim.js`, any OpenAI/Gemini reasoning model;
20	worse on GFW hosts where the backend runs with `--proxy-env` through
21	Clash/mihomo, and worse again under multi-agent workloads
22	**Status**: mitigated locally (shim keepalive + stall watchdog, 2026-08);
23	upstream copilot-api still emits no `ping` events
24	
25	## Symptom
26	
27	Two different things wear the same face, and separating them is most of the fix.
28	
29	### Not a stall: `0 tok` is a display artifact
30	
31	FleetView fills an agent's token counter in only when that agent **finishes**.
32	Six agents sitting at `0 tok · 14m15s` while a seventh shows `104.7k tok` are
33	all working; the transcript proves it:
34	
35	```console
36	$ python3 -c '...' ~/.claude/projects/<proj>/<sess>/subagents/workflows/<wf>/agent-<id>.jsonl
37	{'user': 80, 'attachment': 1, 'assistant': 135} 2026-08-19T03:30:16Z → 2026-08-19T03:41:46Z
38	usage: input_tokens=3, output_tokens=1234, cache_read_input_tokens=95439
39	```
40	
41	Check there before blaming the proxy. (`input_tokens: 3` is also normal for this
42	gateway — the real prompt size lands in `cache_read_input_tokens`.)
43	
44	### The real stall: a socket with nothing on it
45	
46	The failure is that **nothing is transmitted at all** while an OpenAI reasoning
47	model thinks, so any idle timer in the path is free to reap the connection.
48	Measured against `:4141` with `gpt-5.6-sol`:
49	
50	```console
51	$ bun hdr.js                      # fetch, then read the body chunk by chunk
52	headers at 8.11s status 200 ct text/event-stream
53	first body chunk at 8.12s
54	chunks 598 maxgap 8.28s total 32.91s
55	```
56	
57	The response **headers** are withheld for the whole think time — copilot-api
58	does not open the SSE stream early — so the entire wait happens inside one
59	`fetch()` with zero bytes on either socket. The backend's own log agrees; note
60	that its `-->` duration is time-to-headers, not stream duration (a 91s request
61	is logged as `16s`):
62	
63	```console
64	$ grep -aoE '[0-9]+s$' "$TMPDIR/copilot-api-4141.log" | ...
65	n=1395  p50=7s  p90=20s  p99=46s  max=89s
66	```
67	
68	And a real Anthropic stream covers exactly this with periodic `ping` events,
69	which copilot-api never sends:
70	
71	```console
72	events {'message_start':1, 'content_block_start':10, 'content_block_delta':1407,
73	        'content_block_stop':10, 'message_delta':1, 'message_stop':1}
74	```
75	
76	No `ping`. Mid-stream is silent too — reasoning blocks are separated by
77	multi-second gaps (8.28s above, longer under load).
78	
79	## Root cause
80	
81	Three independent contributors, all of which have to be addressed:
82	
83	1. **copilot-api withholds headers until the first token and emits no `ping`.**
84	   The client socket is silent for the model's entire think time.
85	2. **Queueing adds to that silence.** The shim's semaphore (`COPILOT_SHIM_MAX`,
86	   default 4) makes request 5+ wait with *literally* zero traffic. Six review
87	   agents plus a parent session exceed the cap immediately:
88	
89	   ```text
90	   03:37:08.849Z [shim] queued POST /v1/messages (4 in-flight, 4 waiting)
91	   ```
92	
93	   Queue time and think time stack, and both are silent.
94	3. **Every hop has an idle timer.** `Bun.serve({ idleTimeout: 255 })` in the
95	   shim (255s is Bun's ceiling), plus Clash/mihomo on the `--proxy-env` leg to
96	   GitHub. When one of them reaps a silent-but-healthy connection, Claude Code
97	   gets no error — it just waits, which is the Esc-then-`continue` symptom.
98	
99	## Workaround
100	
101	The shim now does two things (`dot_config/shell/copilot-throttle-shim.js`):
102	
103	- **Keepalive.** For a client-requested stream that produces nothing for
104	  `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_AFTER_MS` (default 10000), the shim commits the
105	  `text/event-stream` response itself and emits SSE **comment** frames
106	  (`: copilot-shim keepalive\n\n`) every `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_MS` (default 15000)
107	  until the upstream produces bytes — covering queue time *and* think time, and
108	  continuing through mid-stream gaps. A comment line is discarded by every
109	  spec-compliant SSE parser, so it is invisible to the Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs
110	  and protocol-agnostic (works for `/v1/messages` and Codex's `/responses`).
111	- **Stall watchdog.** Each upstream attempt is bounded by
112	  `COPILOT_SHIM_STALL_MS` (default 240000) — of pre-header silence *and* of
113	  mid-stream silence. A pre-header timeout aborts and goes through the existing
114	  retry path (nothing but comment frames has reached the client, so re-issuing
115	  is transparent); a mid-stream timeout fails the response with a real error
116	  instead of hanging forever.
117	
118	Verify after `chezmoi apply`:
119	
120	```sh
121	copilot-proxy shim off && copilot-proxy shim on
122	copilot-proxy logs shim | tail -1
123	#   [shim] listening on :4142 -> http://localhost:4141 (max=4, retries=3,
124	#          backoff=500ms, ping=15000ms after 10000ms, stall=240000ms)
125	```
126	
127	For a multi-agent workflow, also raise the concurrency cap — the keepalive stops
128	queued agents from *dying*, it does not make them *run*:
129	
130	```sh
131	export COPILOT_SHIM_MAX=8        # persist in ~/.shellrc.adhoc to keep it
132	copilot-proxy shim off && copilot-proxy shim on
133	```
134	
135	(the env var has to be exported, not prefixed — a `VAR=… copilot-proxy shim off`
136	prefix would apply to the `off` and be gone by the time `on` spawns the process).
137	
138	## Prevention
139	
140	- **Before debugging a "hang", check the transcript, not the UI.** A `0 tok`
141	  counter proves nothing; `agent-<id>.jsonl` growing with `assistant` entries
142	  proves the agent is alive.
143	- **A request/response count mismatch in the backend log is the real signal**:
144	
145	  ```sh
146	  L="$TMPDIR/copilot-api-4141.log"; echo "$(grep -ac '^<-- POST' $L) $(grep -ac '^--> POST' $L)"
147	  ```
148	
149	- Do **not** read the `-->` duration as "how long the stream took" — it is
150	  time-to-headers. Measure a stream client-side if you need the real number.
151	- Keep the keepalive as a **comment** frame. An Anthropic-shaped
152	  `event: ping` would be wrong on Codex's `/responses` path; a comment is legal
153	  in both.
154	- Keep the grace window (`COPILOT_SHIM_PING_AFTER_MS`) non-zero. Committing the
155	  SSE response early spends the HTTP status line, so a later non-2xx can only be
156	  reported as an SSE `error` event. Fast failures (`400 model_not_supported`,
157	  `401 IDE token expired`, the 403 burst throttle) all answer well inside the
158	  window and keep their true status code.
159	- `COPILOT_SHIM_STALL_MS` must stay comfortably above the observed p99
160	  time-to-headers (46s, max 89s) or healthy reasoning requests get killed.
161	
162	## Related
163	
164	- [`docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md`](../docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md) —
165	  manager, doctor, throttle-shim guide
166	- [`dot_config/shell/copilot-throttle-shim.js`](../dot_config/shell/copilot-throttle-shim.js) —
167	  keepalive, stall watchdog, semaphore
168	- [`copilot-proxy-ide-token-expired-after-refresh-backoff.md`](copilot-proxy-ide-token-expired-after-refresh-backoff.md) —
169	  the *other* long-running-proxy failure: there the upstream answers (401), here
170	  it answers nothing at all
171	- [`copilot-api-caches-degraded-model-list-at-startup.md`](copilot-api-caches-degraded-model-list-at-startup.md) —
172	  why the model list can contain no `claude-*` ids, which is what pushes this
173	  host onto OpenAI models in the first place
174	- [`backlog/copilot-proxy-supervisor.md`](../backlog/copilot-proxy-supervisor.md) —
175	  process supervision; again insufficient, the process never dies here
176
```
</details></tool-use>

 `./pitfalls/copilot-proxy-ide-token-expired-after-refresh-backoff.md`

```text
1	# `copilot-proxy` stays up but every request returns `401 IDE token expired`
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
4	- `copilot-proxy doctor --live` reports
5	  `✗ round-trip claude-haiku-4-5 → HTTP 401`
6	- `copilot-proxy logs` repeatedly shows
7	  `ERROR HTTP error: IDE token expired: unauthorized: token expired` and
8	  `--> POST /v1/messages?beta=true 401`
9	- The process is still listening, `/v1/models` still returns the cached model
10	  list, and unauthenticated reachability probes still get HTTP 400/401
11	- Earlier log lines show `ERROR Failed to refresh Copilot token`, followed by
12	  `Retrying Copilot token refresh in ...s`; the delay can grow to 600 seconds
13	- A plain `copilot-proxy restart` immediately restores HTTP 200 without another
14	  device login
15	
16	**First seen**: 2026-07
17	**Affects**: `@jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14` on a long-running proxy when
18	GitHub's `copilot_internal/v2/token` exchange is intermittently unreachable;
19	observed on macOS behind Clash/mihomo, but the failure mode is not OS-specific
20	**Status**: upstream refresh loop exists but can leave an expired token active
21	during long retry backoff; immediate workaround documented, reactive local
22	self-heal not yet implemented
23	
24	## Symptom
25	
26	The proxy looks structurally healthy: both the backend and throttle shim are
27	listening, the cached model list contains Claude models, and all GitHub hosts are
28	network-reachable. Only a real inference request fails:
29	
30	```text
31	Live probe
32	  ✗ round-trip       claude-haiku-4-5 → HTTP 401 in 1.077504s
33	```
34	
35	The backend log contains the distinctive upstream response:
36	
37	```text
38	ERROR  Failed to create messages Response { status: 401,
39	  statusText: 'Unauthorized',
40	  ... }
41	
42	ERROR  HTTP error: IDE token expired: unauthorized: token expired
43	
44	--> POST /v1/messages?beta=true 401 1s
45	```
46	
47	This is easy to misdiagnose as a missing token file, an expired long-lived
48	GitHub device-login token, or a dead local process. None was true in the observed
49	case. `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token` existed, the process answered,
50	and restarting it successfully exchanged the same stored credential.
51	
52	## Root cause
53	
54	There are two token layers:
55	
56	1. `copilot-proxy auth` stores a relatively long-lived GitHub `ghu_` credential
57	   in `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`.
58	2. `copilot-api` exchanges that credential at
59	   `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` for a short-lived Copilot
60	   IDE token used against `api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com` or
61	   `api.githubcopilot.com`.
62	
63	The fork already has a refresh loop; this is **not** simply a missing refresh
64	feature. In `@jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14`, `setupCopilotToken()` starts
65	`runCopilotRefreshLoop(refresh_in, ...)`, which refreshes one minute early. When
66	the exchange fails it retries with exponential backoff plus jitter, capped at
67	600 seconds, while retaining the old token in memory.
68	
69	The failed session's rotated log showed all three exchange failure shapes:
70	
71	```text
72	ERROR  Failed to refresh Copilot token: fetch failed
73	[cause]: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND api.github.com
74	WARN  Retrying Copilot token refresh in 23s
75	
76	ERROR  Failed to refresh Copilot token: fetch failed
77	[cause]: Connect Timeout Error (attempted address: api.github.com:443, timeout: 10000ms)
78	
79	ERROR  Failed to get Copilot token response body <!DOCTYPE html>
80	...
81	ERROR  Failed to refresh Copilot token: Failed to get Copilot token
82	WARN  Retrying Copilot token refresh in 600s
83	```
84	
85	Once the in-memory IDE token expires, inference requests return 401 until one of
86	those scheduled exchanges succeeds. The server stays alive and `/v1/models`
87	continues serving its cache, so a process-only health check considers it healthy.
88	
89	This also explains why two `doctor` sections can look contradictory:
90	
91	- `Upstream` accepts an unauthenticated HTTP 400/401 as proof of network
92	  reachability only; it does **not** prove token exchange works.
93	- `Models · upstream could not query GitHub directly` means the authenticated
94	  exchange/model query failed, even though `bun`, `jq`, and the token file are
95	  present.
96	
97	## Workaround
98	
99	Restart the backend and shim through the existing manager. Startup performs an
100	immediate token exchange and resets the refresh-loop backoff:
101	
102	```sh
103	copilot-proxy restart
104	copilot-proxy doctor --live
105	```
106	
107	A healthy result ends with:
108	
109	```text
110	Live probe
111	  ✓ round-trip       claude-haiku-4-5 → HTTP 200
112	
113	all checks passed
114	```
115	
116	Only re-authenticate if restart still returns 401 or startup cannot exchange the
117	stored GitHub credential:
118	
119	```sh
120	copilot-proxy auth
121	copilot-proxy restart
122	copilot-proxy doctor --live
123	```
124	
125	Do not start with `auth`: in the observed case the stored `ghu_` credential was
126	valid, and a restart alone recovered it.
127	
128	## Prevention
129	
130	- When this exact 401 appears, inspect earlier logs for
131	  `Failed to refresh Copilot token` before blaming the token file or Copilot
132	  entitlement.
133	- `launchd KeepAlive` / systemd `Restart=always` alone cannot catch this case:
134	  the process never exits. The existing supervisor backlog is useful for crashes
135	  and login-start, not logical auth health.
136	- The safest future local self-heal is reactive, not periodic: have the throttle
137	  shim detect a `401` whose small response body contains `IDE token expired`,
138	  single-flight a **backend-only** restart, wait for port 4141 to become healthy,
139	  and replay the buffered request once. Add a lock/cooldown to prevent concurrent
140	  401s from causing a restart storm. Do not restart the shim that is holding the
141	  client request.
142	- Avoid periodic live inference probes: they consume quota. Periodic blind
143	  restarts can also interrupt a valid long-running stream.
144	- As of the observed version the shim's retry set is only
145	  `403/429/502/503/504`; adding bare 401 to that set would just resend the same
146	  expired token and is not a fix.
147	
148	This is not being graduated to an `AGENTS.md` hard invariant yet: it does not
149	silently corrupt state, and the workaround is a single manager command.
150	
151	## Related

 `./pitfalls/codex-copilot-empty-mcp-tool-description-400.md`

```text
1	# codex-copilot fails with empty MCP tool description HTTP 400
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): `Invalid 'input[0].tools[0].description': empty string. Expected a string with minimum length 1`; `invalid_request_body`; `POST /responses 400`
4	**First seen**: 2026-08
5	**Affects**: Codex CLI through `@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0` and GitHub Copilot Responses
6	**Status**: fixed in the managed compatibility shim
7	
8	## Symptom
9	
10	```text
11	HTTP error: { error:
12	   { message:
13	      "Invalid 'input[0].tools[0].description': empty string. Expected a string with minimum length 1, but got an empty string instead.",
14	     code: 'invalid_request_body' } }
15	
16	--> POST /responses 400
17	```
18	
19	The model appears in `/v1/models`, `/status` shows the localhost provider, and
20	the request reaches `api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`, but inference never
21	starts.
22	
23	## Root cause
24	
25	Codex persists MCP discovery as Responses `mcp_list_tools` input items. An MCP
26	or plugin tool may legally omit its description, which becomes an empty string
27	in `input[].tools[].description`. GitHub Copilot's Responses validator requires
28	that field to contain at least one character and rejects the entire request.
29	This is a payload-schema mismatch, not a model entitlement or network failure.
30	Codex 0.147 also sends the request with `Content-Encoding: zstd`; inspecting the
31	raw body as JSON silently misses the tool list until it is decompressed.
32	
33	## Workaround
34	
35	Use the managed launcher after applying the dotfiles:
36	
37	```sh
38	chezmoi apply ~/.config/shell/copilot-throttle-shim.js ~/.config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh
39	source ~/.config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh
40	copilot-proxy restart
41	codex-copilot
42	```
43	
44	`codex-copilot` now always starts and targets the shim on port 4142. The shim
45	fills only blank tool descriptions in top-level function definitions and
46	`mcp_list_tools` input items before forwarding `/responses`; it does not mutate
47	user input or JSON Schema descriptions. For a repaired zstd request it forwards
48	ordinary JSON and removes `content-encoding`.
49	
50	## Prevention
51	
52	- Keep the Unix and Windows `copilot-throttle-shim.js` copies byte-identical.
53	- Do not make `codex-copilot` fall back directly to port 4141; the shim is a
54	  Responses compatibility boundary even when burst throttling is disabled.
55	- The shim logs each repaired JSON path without logging request contents.
56	
57	## Related
58	
59	- `docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md`
60	- `dot_config/shell/copilot-throttle-shim.js`
61	- `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh`
62
```
</details></tool-use>

 `./pitfalls/copilot-proxy-start-hangs-at-resolving-dependencies.md`

```text
1	# `copilot-proxy start` hangs at "Resolving dependencies" and never binds the port
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): `copilot-proxy: did not come up in time — check 'copilot-proxy logs'.`; `copilot-proxy logs` shows only `nohup: ignoring input` + `Resolving dependencies` and nothing else; `copilot-proxy status` says `not running on port 4141`; `ps` shows one or more wedged `bun add @jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14 --no-summary`; every retry adds ANOTHER stuck pair and none ever binds the port; `curl` to the npm registry works fine so it does not look like a network fault
4	**First seen**: 2026-07
5	**Affects**: bun 1.3.x (`bunx`) + `@jeffreycao/copilot-api` (any pinned version) on a host with a socks proxy exported as `ALL_PROXY` (Clash/mihomo, `socks://127.0.0.1:7890`)
6	**Status**: **fixed** 2026-07 — the runner no longer resolves at launch (pinned package installed once into `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg`, binary exec'd directly); install is timeout-bounded + killed, and `start` now reaps the server it spawned. `copilot-proxy doctor` still detects the condition as a safety net. The manual workaround below remains valid for any *other* `bunx`-based tool on a proxied host.
7	
8	## Symptom
9	
10	`copilot-proxy start` prints its banner, backgrounds the job, then times out after ~20s:
11	
12	```
13	❯ copilot-proxy start
14	copilot-proxy: starting (@jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14) on port 4141 ...
15	[4] 39859
16	copilot-proxy: did not come up in time — check 'copilot-proxy logs'.
17	```
18	
19	The log is two lines and stops there — no error, no stack, no bind:
20	
21	```
22	❯ copilot-proxy logs
23	nohup: ignoring input
24	Resolving dependencies
25	```
26	
27	`ps` shows the launcher and a package installer that never exits. Retrying stacks
28	them up — this is five processes from three `start` attempts, all still alive:
29	
30	```
31	 8926  bunx @jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14 start --port 4141
32	 8931  …/bun/1.3.8/bin/bun add @jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14 --no-summary
33	10427  bunx @jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14 start --port 4141
34	10434  …/bun/1.3.8/bin/bun add @jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14 --no-summary
35	…
36	```
37	
38	The misleading part: **the network is fine**. `curl` reaches the registry
39	instantly, both through the proxy and directly, so every obvious check passes:
40	
41	```
42	registry.npmmirror.com HTTP 200 in 0.371359s     # via $HTTPS_PROXY
43	registry.npmmirror.com HTTP 200 in 0.182431s     # --noproxy '*'
44	```
45	
46	Auth is fine too (`github_token` present, `doctor` shows the token file and
47	reaches `api.githubcopilot.com`). Nothing points at the installer.
48	
49	## Root cause
50	
51	`copilot-proxy start` runs the proxy via `bunx`, which must **install** the pinned
52	package into a temp dir (`/tmp/bunx-<uid>-@jeffreycao/…`) before `copilot-api start`
53	can bind the port. That install is a `bun add`, and **bun stalls resolving
54	dependencies through a socks `ALL_PROXY`** — indefinitely, with no error and no
55	timeout. `curl` through the same proxy works, which is exactly why this reads as a
56	non-network problem.
57	
58	Two things turn one stall into a permanent wedge:
59	
60	1. The wedged `bun add` **keeps bun's global install-cache lock**
61	   (`~/.bun/install/cache/.tmp`), so the *next* `copilot-proxy start` blocks on the
62	   lock and hangs the same way — even if the proxy stall would have cleared.
63	2. `start`'s 20s timeout returns, but **never kills the process it spawned**. Each
64	   retry leaves another zombie pair behind, so the situation gets monotonically
65	   worse the more you retry.
66	
67	Proof it is the proxy env and not the registry: with the proxy vars stripped, the
68	identical `bunx` command resolves 99 packages and binds the port in 3 seconds.
69	
70	```
71	Resolving dependencies
72	Resolved, downloaded and extracted [99]
73	Saved lockfile
74	➜ Listening on: http://localhost:4141/
75	```
76	
77	Note the registry here is **npmmirror** (`~/.bunfig.toml` → `registry =
78	"https://registry.npmmirror.com"`, set for GFW speed). It is a domestic mirror, so
79	routing it through the proxy buys nothing and is what breaks bun.
80	
81	## Workaround
82	
83	Copy-pasteable. Step 1 clears the wedge, step 2 avoids re-creating it:
84	
85	```bash
86	# 1. kill the wedged installers and release bun's global cache lock
87	pkill -f 'bun add.*copilot-api'
88	rm -rf /tmp/bunx-*-@jeffreycao "$HOME/.bun/install/cache/.tmp"/*
89	
90	# 2. start with the proxy env stripped — bun resolves against npmmirror (domestic),
91	#    which needs no proxy; the copilot-api server itself still reaches GitHub direct
92	env -u ALL_PROXY -u all_proxy -u HTTP_PROXY -u http_proxy \
93	    -u HTTPS_PROXY -u https_proxy \
94	    copilot-proxy start
95	```
96	
97	Step 2 is safe **on a host where GitHub Copilot is reachable without the proxy** —
98	verify with `copilot-proxy doctor`, whose Upstream section probes
99	`api.githubcopilot.com` with `--noproxy '*'`; a `direct HTTP 400` line means reached
100	(an unauthenticated probe is *expected* to be rejected). On a host where GitHub is
101	only reachable *through* the proxy, do NOT strip the env for the server — strip it
102	only for a warm-up `bun add`, then start normally against the now-warm cache.
103	
104	## Prevention
105	
106	`copilot-proxy doctor` detects this directly. Its Proxy section flags any live
107	`bun add … copilot-api` — red when nothing is listening (that IS the fault), yellow
108	when the proxy is up (a leftover that still holds the cache lock and will hang the
109	next restart), and prints the clear-and-restart one-liner:
110	
111	```
112	Proxy
113	  ✗ listening        nothing answering on port 4141
114	                     → copilot-proxy start
115	  ✗ stale installer  3 wedged 'bun add … copilot-api' proc(s) — start is blocked at "Resolving dependencies", never binds port 4141
116	                     → pkill -f 'bun add.*copilot-api'; rm -rf "$HOME/.bun/install/cache/.tmp"/*; copilot-proxy start
117	                     → re-hangs? bun is stalling on the socks proxy — env -u ALL_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u HTTP_PROXY copilot-proxy start
118	```
119	
120	**Clearing the lock alone was not durable** — the stall recurs on the next cold
121	resolve (it did, twice). That's why the fix removes the per-launch resolve entirely
122	rather than making it more likely to succeed:
123	
124	- `_copilot_ensure_pkg` installs the pinned spec **once** into
125	  `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg`, stamped with the spec so a version bump
126	  re-installs. `start` then execs `node_modules/.bin/copilot-api` directly — a warm
127	  start does **zero network** before it binds the port.
128	- `_copilot_pkg_install_try` bounds each attempt and **kills it on timeout**, so a
129	  stalled `bun add` can never again keep bun's global cache lock. Attempt 1 honours
130	  the ambient env (a host may only reach the registry *through* the proxy); attempt
131	  2 strips it. `COPILOT_INSTALL_NOPROXY=1` skips straight to attempt 2.
132	- `start` now **reaps the server it spawned** on timeout. The old code returned and
133	  left it running, which is the whole reason retries stacked orphans.
134	
135	Do not "fix" this by raising `start`'s 20s timeout — the installer is wedged, not
136	slow; a longer wait just wedges for longer.
137	
138	The same trap applies to **any** `bunx`-based tool on this host: bunx re-resolves
139	per launch, so a socks `ALL_PROXY` can hang it the same way. If you add one, either
140	pin+install it or expect this failure mode.
141	
142	## Related
143	
144	- [`docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md`](../docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md) — `copilot-proxy doctor` section documents the stale-installer check
145	- [`dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh`](../dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh) — `_copilot_stale_installers` + the doctor Proxy section
146	- [`copilot-api-caches-degraded-model-list-at-startup.md`](copilot-api-caches-degraded-model-list-at-startup.md) — sibling copilot-api trap; also a startup-time fetch that fails in a way that looks like something else
147
```
</details></tool-use>

 `./backlog/copilot-proxy-global-apply-mode.md`

```text
1	# copilot-proxy global apply mode for Claude Code and Codex
2	
3	**Status**: deferred (2026-08-12)
4	**Effort**: L
5	**Related**: `TODO.md` · `backlog/copilot-proxy-supervisor.md` · `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh`
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	The shipped launchers are scoped and reversible: `claude-copilot` and
10	`codex-copilot` affect one process, while `copilot-here` owns a gitignored
11	Claude project overlay. A user-wide mode would be convenient, but it would make
12	ordinary `claude` and `codex` depend on a localhost daemon and would mutate
13	runtime-owned user config.
14	
15	## Proposed contract
16	
17	Use an explicit target such as `copilot-global on|off|status
18	claude|codex|all`. `on` must prove the supervised proxy/shim healthy, snapshot
19	the exact files/keys it owns with hashes, write validated temporary files then
20	atomically replace, and record an ownership/schema marker. Claude gets the
21	complete role profile; Codex gets the provider/model keys while all unrelated
22	TOML survives.
23	
24	`off` restores the snapshot exactly. If current values differ from both the
25	owned value and snapshot, stop with a drift report rather than overwriting user
26	changes. Interrupted operations must be restartable and idempotent. Tests need
27	fresh/existing config, repeated cycles, mid-stage crash, malformed input, manual
28	drift, state migration, and proxy failure. Implement native PowerShell parity on
29	Windows.
30	
31	## Options considered
32	
33	| Option | Pros | Cons |
34	|---|---|---|
35	| Keep one-shot/project launchers | Safe; no restore state or daemon coupling | Repeated opt-in |
36	| Chezmoi-managed permanent provider | Declarative | Fights runtime writes; may point at a dead daemon |
37	| Stateful global switch | Best UX with exact restore | Requires supervisor, transactions, drift ownership, platform parity |
38	
39	## Decision / blocker
40	
41	Deferred until `copilot-proxy` has a real login-start supervisor and stable log
42	location. Without that prerequisite a global setting can strand both CLIs after
43	reboot. Preserve one-shot launchers as the supported path meanwhile.
44
```
</details></tool-use>
