 `./backlog/copilot-proxy-supervisor.md`

```text
1	# copilot-proxy: replace `nohup` start with a real supervisor (launchd / systemd / pueue)
2	
3	**Status**: P? — evaluation captured, deferred (user wants a plan, not a build)
4	**Effort**: M
5	**Related**: [`dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh`](../dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh) (`copilot-proxy start`, lines ~146-157) · [`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_agent-warmup`](../dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_agent-warmup) (launchd/systemd `install` precedent) · [backlog/agent-quota-warmup-at-time.md](agent-quota-warmup-at-time.md) · [docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md](../docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md) · [pitfalls/agent-warmup-scheduled-run-hangs-or-blank-under-daemon.md](../pitfalls/agent-warmup-scheduled-run-hangs-or-blank-under-daemon.md)
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	2026-07-03, while debugging Claude Code `API error · Retrying …` / `500 fetch failed`
10	loops on the Copilot proxy. Two separate questions surfaced; **this doc is only the
11	second one (how the proxy is started/supervised).** The first — the actual API
12	errors — is a **60 s upstream timeout**, NOT a proxy-process problem (see the
13	"⚠ scope" note below so future-me doesn't conflate them).
14	
15	Today `copilot-proxy start` (`43_copilot_proxy.sh`) launches the fork
16	(`@jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14`) via **`nohup bunx … &`**, tracks the PID in
17	`$TMPDIR/copilot-api-$PORT.pid`, and tees stdout+stderr to a single
18	`$TMPDIR/copilot-api-$PORT.log` (viewable with `copilot-proxy logs [N]`). It works,
19	but the user asked whether there's a "better start with queryable logs — systemd/
20	launchd? surely not nohup?". It is, in fact, nohup.
21	
22	**⚠ scope**: the observed failures (11× HTTP 500, all clustered at 60-62 s) are the
23	*upstream* path cutting long Opus/1M generations. The `copilot-api` **process never
24	crashed**. So a supervisor's auto-restart (`KeepAlive`/`Restart=always`) would
25	**not** have prevented those API errors. This migration buys: survives-crash,
26	start-at-login, stable log path, log rotation — not timeout resilience. Don't sell
27	it as a fix for the 500s.
28	
29	**Root cause of the 500s — FOUND + FIXED (2026-07-03), separate from this backlog.**
30	The 60 s cap was **nginx's default `proxy_read_timeout` (60 s)** on the WebSocket
31	`location` block of the personal V2Ray node the Copilot traffic tunnels through
32	(Clash rule `DOMAIN-KEYWORD,github → PROXY` → Azure-JP V2Ray VM). Long Opus/1M
33	generations that idle >60 s upstream got the WS reaped → `other side closed` →
34	copilot-api returns 500 → Claude Code retry loop. Fixed by adding
35	`proxy_read_timeout 3600s` / `proxy_send_timeout 3600s` to that block. Repo +
36	write-up live in the *separate* `~/Documents/Program/DockerCompose-V2Ray` project:
37	`server/templates/nginx/v2ray.conf.tmpl` + `ansible/roles/vpn/templates/nginx/v2ray.conf.j2`,
38	pitfall `pitfalls/long-connections-drop-at-60s-other-side-closed.md`. (That box was
39	also on the legacy static-conf layout, so the fix was hand-applied on the VPS +
40	committed to templates for the eventual IaC migration.) **This supervisor backlog
41	remains purely about start/supervise ergonomics — the API-error thread is closed.**
42	
43	## Investigation
44	
45	Current start path (`43_copilot_proxy.sh`):
46	
47	```sh
48	# lines ~71-72 — ephemeral $TMPDIR paths (wiped on reboot, differ per launchd session)
49	_copilot_logfile() { printf '%s' "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/copilot-api-$(_copilot_port).log"; }
50	_copilot_pidfile() { printf '%s' "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/copilot-api-$(_copilot_port).pid"; }
51	
52	# lines ~146-157 — the nohup start (fork branch)
53	nohup bunx "$pkg" start --port "$port" >"$logf" 2>&1 &
54	printf '%s\n' "$!" >"$pidf"
55	```
56	
57	Gaps vs a supervisor:
58	
59	1. **No auto-restart** — if the process dies, it stays dead until a manual
60	   `copilot-proxy start`. (Low real-world value here — see ⚠ scope; upstream 500s
61	   don't kill the process. Value is for genuine crashes / OOM / node upgrades.)
62	2. **No start-at-login** — every reboot / fresh shell must re-run `start`.
63	3. **Log lives in `$TMPDIR`** — wiped on reboot, and launchd hands processes a
64	   *different* per-session `$TMPDIR`, so the path isn't stable/predictable.
65	4. **No log rotation** — single unbounded file (116 KB in this session; fine for
66	   now, but grows forever).
67	
68	Precedent already in the repo — **`agent-warmup` (`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_agent-warmup`)
69	solved exactly this daemon-bootstrap shape**:
70	
71	- macOS: writes `~/Library/LaunchAgents/<label>.plist` (`StandardOutPath`,
72	  `RunAtLoad`), loads via `launchctl bootout` + `bootstrap gui/$uid` (fallback
73	  `launchctl load -w`). See `_launchd_path()` / `_install_launchd()` (~lines 447-486).
74	- Linux: writes `~/.config/systemd/user/<unit>.{service,timer}`, verifies with
75	  `systemd-analyze verify` (~lines 494-526).
76	- Carries a `_PATH_PRELUDE` (mirrors `scripts/fleet/exec.py`) so the minimal env
77	  launchd/systemd hand the process still finds `bunx`/`tmux`/`launchctl` — **this is
78	  the key gotcha for us too**: `bunx` comes from mise (`07_bunx_cli.sh`), which is
79	  NOT on launchd's default PATH.
80	
81	Difference from agent-warmup: it schedules a **one-shot timer** (`RunAtLoad: False`
82	+ `StartCalendarInterval` / systemd `.timer`). copilot-api is a **persistent
83	daemon**, so we want `KeepAlive: true` + `RunAtLoad: true` (macOS) and a plain
84	`.service` with `Restart=always` + `WantedBy=default.target` (systemd, **no timer**).
85	
86	Also live on this host: `~/Library/LaunchAgents/homebrew.mxcl.pueue.plist` —
87	**`pueued` is already launchd-supervised via `brew services`**, so the pueue option
88	below has near-zero daemon-bootstrap cost.
89	
90	## Options considered
91	
92	| Option | Pros | Cons |
93	|---|---|---|
94	| **A. launchd LaunchAgent (macOS) + systemd --user (Linux)**, generated at runtime by a `copilot-proxy install` subcommand — reuse agent-warmup's `_install_launchd`/`_install_systemd` + `_PATH_PRELUDE` | Native, `RunAtLoad`+`KeepAlive`/`Restart=always`, stable `StandardOutPath` log, cross-platform, proven pattern in this repo | Must solve mise/`bunx` PATH in the minimal daemon env; log rotation still manual (`newsyslog`/`logrotate` or size-cap in wrapper); plist/unit is runtime-generated (not chezmoi-managed → not in git) |
95	| **B. systemd --user only** | Cleanest logs (`journalctl --user -u copilot-api -f`), built-in rotation, `Restart=always` | Linux-only; this proxy is macOS-primary (personal Copilot sub) → would still need launchd for the main host. Really just the Linux half of A. |
96	| **C. pueue task** (`pueue add -- bunx … start`) | `pueued` already launchd-supervised (zero new daemon); fits existing `fleet pueue`/`pqsum` tooling; `pueue log -f` for logs; survives shell exit | Not a service supervisor: no crash auto-restart by default, no start-at-login semantics for the *task* (only the daemon persists); a `pueue reset`/`clean` could nuke it; semantically a job-queue, not a daemon |
97	| **D. keep nohup, just harden** (stable log path under `$XDG_STATE_HOME`, size-cap rotation, optional cron liveness re-`start`) | Smallest change; no new moving parts | Reinvents a worse supervisor; still no login-start; cron-poll restart is hacky |
98	
99	## Current blocker / open questions
100	
101	- **Is it worth it at all?** Given ⚠ scope (the real pain is upstream 500s, not
102	  crashes), the concrete wins are login-start + stable/rotated logs. Decide whether
103	  that clears the M-effort bar, or whether option D (just move the log to
104	  `$XDG_STATE_HOME` + size-cap) is enough.
105	- **PATH in the daemon env**: confirm the mise-shim resolution for `bunx` under
106	  launchd. Cleanest is to resolve the absolute `bunx` (or `bun x`) path at install
107	  time and bake it into the plist `ProgramArguments`, rather than relying on a login
108	  shell. Cross-check `_PATH_PRELUDE` (chezmoi→cargo→uv→~/bin→brew→linuxbrew order).
109	- **Auth precondition**: `start` today refuses without
110	  `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`. A `KeepAlive` daemon that boots at
111	  login before auth would crash-loop → need `KeepAlive` with a `SuccessfulExit`/
112	  throttle guard, or gate `RunAtLoad` on the token file existing.
113	- **Interaction with `copilot-proxy start/stop/restart`**: the shell verbs must
114	  detect the launchd/systemd unit and delegate (`launchctl kickstart -k` /
115	  `systemctl --user restart`) instead of spawning a second nohup instance. Keep
116	  `logs` working against the new `StandardOutPath`.

656	
657	> 用 **GitHub Copilot** served 的模型驅動 Claude Code 與 Codex，透過只安裝一次、版本釘選的 [copilot-api 維護 fork](https://github.com/caozhiyuan/copilot-api)。Claude Code 有 entitlement 時優先 Claude，否則建立 Sol/Terra/Luna 角色 profile；Codex 優先 native Responses OpenAI model。完整指南、**ToS / rate-limit 風險**與設定分層：[docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md](../tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md)。首次需執行 `copilot-proxy auth`；launcher 不碰 committed project settings 或 chezmoi-managed user settings。
658	
659	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
660	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
661	| `copilot-proxy [start\|stop\|restart\|status\|doctor [--live]\|logs [N]\|whoami\|auth]` | function | `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` | 管理釘選 proxy。`doctor` 區分 stale catalog、geo/policy filter 與網路故障，驗證 main + Claude roles，並獨立檢查遠端 ChatGPT `codex_apps` 路由。`--live` 的 inference probe 花一個 quota unit；Apps GET 不會。 |
662	| `claude-copilot [--no-specstory] [args...]` | function | `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` | 一次性走 proxy 的 Claude Code session，**零檔案寫入**：自動啟動 proxy，per-process 注入完整 role-aware `ANTHROPIC_*` env。既有 `copilot-here` local pin 會蓋過這層。specstory passthrough 會保留設定的 `claude_cmd`；下次直接跑 `claude` 即還原。 |
663	| `codex-copilot [--no-specstory] [args...]` / `codex-copilot-once` | function | `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` | 零持久化的 Codex launcher，走本機 Responses gateway。自動啟動 proxy/shim；明確 `-m` 優先，否則即時排序 OpenAI/Codex → Claude → Gemini。預設整合 SpecStory 並保留 project/user `codex_cmd`；兩個名稱都不改 Codex config。 |
664	| `copilot-run <cmd...>` | function | `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` | 泛用積木：自動啟動代理，然後帶著代理 env 執行 *任意* 指令（例如 `copilot-run specstory run claude`、`copilot-run claude --resume`） |
665	| `copilot-here [on\|off\|status]` | function | `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` | 專案級持續開關，透過 **gitignored** 的 `./.claude/settings.local.json`（覆蓋會 commit 的專案設定，所以 `plansDirectory` 完全不受影響）。`on` 用 jq 合併代理 env 區塊並確保 git 忽略該檔（`.git/info/exclude`）；`off` 只移除那些 key（保留其他內容，檔案清空才刪除）；`status` 顯示釘選狀態 + 模型，代理沒跑時警告。需要 `jq` |

```text
1	# Codex status line
2	
3	The Windows profile uses Codex's built-in TUI footer. Chezmoi enforces only
4	this list and preserves all unrelated live TOML, including providers, project
5	trust, plugins, feature flags, and nested keymaps:
6	
7	```toml
8	[tui]
9	status_line = [
10	  "model-with-reasoning",
11	  "fast-mode",
12	  "git-branch",
13	  "context-remaining",
14	  "task-progress",
15	  "current-dir",
16	]
17	```
18	
19	The modifier uses Bun's built-in TOML parser, which is installed in the baseline
20	toolset. It performs no Python or package-registry access during `chezmoi apply`,
21	so managed machines that block PyPI still get the footer. It accepts one leading
22	UTF-8 BOM as an encoding signature.
23	Malformed TOML, invalid UTF-8, a parser failure, or an invalid managed overlay is
24	fail-closed: the original stdin bytes are emitted exactly, including CRLF. A
25	successful merge is normalized to UTF-8 without BOM, LF line endings, and one
26	final newline. The file is deployed only when **Install coding agents** is
27	enabled.
28	
29	Use `/status` as the routing proof. A `codex-copilot` session should show the
30	localhost provider even though the Account line can still show the logged-in
31	ChatGPT account. The managed footer omits `five-hour-limit` and `weekly-limit`
32	because those may remain ChatGPT-account counters while inference uses Copilot.
33	
34	No Claude-HUD-style extension is installed. Stock Codex accepts only fixed
35	built-in item IDs, while `@jiawang1209/codex-hud` patches and compiles an older
36	Codex tree and adds a PATH shim. The maintenance and supply-chain cost is too
37	high for a footer.
38	
39	`codex_apps` is a separate remote ChatGPT MCP at
40	`https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/apps`, not an Apple Silicon Desktop bridge.
41	Use `copilot-proxy doctor --live` to compare its direct and HTTP-proxy routes.
42	
43	See [copilot-proxy](copilot-proxy.md) and the
44	[Codex config reference](https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference).
45
```
</details></tool-use>

+            [Parameter(Mandatory)]
+            [AllowEmptyCollection()]
+            [byte[]] $LiveBytes,
+
+            [string] $ScriptPath = $RenderedPath,
+
+            [hashtable] $Environment = @{}
+        )
+
+        $startInfo = [System.Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo]::new()
+        $startInfo.FileName = $PwshPath
+        $startInfo.UseShellExecute = $false
+        $startInfo.CreateNoWindow = $true
+        $startInfo.RedirectStandardInput = $true
+        $startInfo.RedirectStandardOutput = $true
+        $startInfo.RedirectStandardError = $true
+        $startInfo.ArgumentList.Add('-NoProfile')
+        $startInfo.ArgumentList.Add('-NonInteractive')
+        $startInfo.ArgumentList.Add('-File')
+        $startInfo.ArgumentList.Add($ScriptPath)
+        foreach ($name in $Environment.Keys) {
+            $startInfo.Environment[$name] = [string] $Environment[$name]
+        }
+
+        $process = [System.Diagnostics.Process]::new()
+        $process.StartInfo = $startInfo
+        $stdout = [System.IO.MemoryStream]::new()
+        $stderr = [System.IO.MemoryStream]::new()
+        try {
+            if (-not $process.Start()) { throw 'failed to start rendered Codex modifier' }
+            $stdoutCopy = $process.StandardOutput.BaseStream.CopyToAsync($stdout)
+            $stderrCopy = $process.StandardError.BaseStream.CopyToAsync($stderr)
+
+            if ($LiveBytes.Length -gt 0) {
+                $process.StandardInput.BaseStream.Write($LiveBytes, 0, $LiveBytes.Length)
+            }
+            $process.StandardInput.BaseStream.Close()
+
+            $process.WaitForExit()
+            $stdoutCopy.GetAwaiter().GetResult()
+            $stderrCopy.GetAwaiter().GetResult()
+
+            return [pscustomobject]@{
+                StdoutBytes = $stdout.ToArray()
+                Stderr      = $Utf8.GetString($stderr.ToArray())
+                ExitCode    = $process.ExitCode
+            }
+        } finally {
+            $stdout.Dispose()
+            $stderr.Dispose()
+            $process.Dispose()
+        }
     }
 }

+
+## Codex through the gateway
+
+`codex-copilot` and its identical `codex-copilot-once` alias start the local
+gateway/shim and pass a `copilot_api` Responses provider through one-invocation
+Codex `-c` overrides. They do not edit user or project Codex config, so plain
+`codex` is unaffected. An explicit `-m` / `--model` wins; otherwise the live raw
+catalog is ranked OpenAI/Codex first (`Sol > Terra > GPT-5.5 > GPT-5.4 > GPT-5.3
+Codex > Luna > mini`), then Claude, Gemini and other chat models. Disabled and
+embedding models are excluded.
+
+This is a separate picker from Claude Code's `copilot-model --auto`: that path
+remains Claude-first, while only the Codex launcher is OpenAI-first.
+
+SpecStory is automatic when installed. The wrapper preserves the effective
+`codex_cmd` (project config > user config > bare `codex`) before appending
+provider/model/user arguments; `--no-specstory` runs Codex directly. Claude and
+Gemini fallback through Responses Lite, which does not support Responses
+`tool_search`, so native Responses OpenAI models stay ahead of Anthropic.
+The launcher also enables gateway-backed remote compaction and excludes the
+`mcp__codex_apps__sites` namespace that depends on unavailable `tool_search`;
+later explicit `-c` arguments can override either setting per invocation.
+
+`codex_apps` itself is not a localhost service and not an Apple-Silicon-only
+Codex Desktop bridge. It is a remote MCP at
+`https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/apps`, so startup can fail even while
+Copilot inference on `localhost:4142` works. Keep Apps enabled and use
+`copilot-proxy doctor --live` to diagnose that route independently.
+
+There is deliberately no Codex equivalent of `copilot-here`: project
+`.codex/config.toml` cannot override provider definitions, provider selection or
+auth metadata. The explicit launcher provides project/session scope without
+changing the user-wide default.
+
+### Experimental direct configuration
+
+The direct `model_providers.copilot-enterprise` example is documented in the
+macOS/Linux guide rather than installed. It is not the localhost proxy path, and
+the pasted `gh auth token` flow is not portable: on the tested EMU account it
+returned `421`/`403`, while the credential stored by `copilot-proxy auth` plus
+the normal short-lived Copilot token exchange worked. The supported launcher
+therefore uses the authenticated local gateway.

+# Optional ChatGPT Apps reachability. This is deliberately separate from the
+# Copilot inference probes: codex_apps is a remote MCP served by chatgpt.com,
+# not a localhost bridge to Codex.app and not part of GitHub Copilot.
+function script:Get-CopilotProbeFailureKind {
+    param($ErrorRecord)
+
+    $message = if ($ErrorRecord -is [System.Management.Automation.ErrorRecord]) {
+        $ErrorRecord.Exception.ToString()
+    } else { [string]$ErrorRecord }
+
+    if ($message -match '(?i)timed?\s*out|timeout|operation.*canceled|deadline') { return 'timeout' }
+    if ($message -match '(?i)certificate|authenticationexception|ssl|tls|secure channel') { return 'tls' }
+    'network'
+}
+
+function script:Invoke-CopilotOptionalHttpProbe {
+    param(
+        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Uri,
+        [string] $Via = 'direct'
+    )
+
+    $transport = @{}
+    if ($Via -eq 'direct') { $transport['NoProxy'] = $true }
+    elseif ($Via) { $transport['Proxy'] = $Via }
+
+    $sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
+    try {
+        $response = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $Uri -Method Get -TimeoutSec 12 `
+            -SkipHttpErrorCheck -Headers @{ 'user-agent' = 'codex-copilot-doctor/1.0' } `
+            @transport -ErrorAction Stop
+        $sw.Stop()
+        [pscustomobject]@{
+            Reached = $true
+            Code    = [int]$response.StatusCode
+            Seconds = [math]::Round($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 2)
+            Kind    = $null
+            Error   = $null
+        }
+    } catch {
+        $sw.Stop()
+        [pscustomobject]@{
+            Reached = $false
+            Code    = 0
+            Seconds = [math]::Round($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 2)
+            Kind    = Get-CopilotProbeFailureKind $_
+            Error   = ($_.Exception.Message -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
+        }
+    }
+}
+

+# Codex prefers a native Responses-capable OpenAI model. Claude/Gemini are
+# Responses Lite fallbacks only, unlike Select-CopilotBestModel (Claude Code),
+# where native Claude remains the first choice.
+function script:Select-CopilotBestCodexModel {
+    param([string[]] $Model)
+    if (-not $Model -or $Model.Count -eq 0) { return $null }
+    $Model = @($Model | ForEach-Object { Remove-CopilotContextHint $_ } | Sort-Object -Unique)
+
+    foreach ($preferred in 'gpt-5.6-sol', 'gpt-5.6-terra', 'gpt-5.5', 'gpt-5.4', 'gpt-5.3-codex',
+                           'gpt-5.6-luna', 'gpt-5.4-mini', 'gpt-5-mini') {
+        if ($Model -contains $preferred) { return $preferred }
+    }
+    $pick = { param($re, $exclude)
+        $c = @($Model | Where-Object { $_ -match $re -and (-not $exclude -or $_ -notmatch $exclude) } | Sort-Object)
+        if ($c.Count -gt 0) { $c[-1] } else { $null }
+    }
+    $r = & $pick '^gpt-' 'mini|nano|luna'
+    if ($r) { return $r }
+    $r = & $pick 'codex' $null
+    if ($r) { return $r }
+    $r = & $pick '^gpt-' $null
+    if ($r) { return $r }
+
+    foreach ($preferred in 'claude-fable-5',
+                           'claude-opus-5', 'claude-opus-4-8', 'claude-opus-4-7', 'claude-opus-4-6',
+                           'claude-sonnet-5', 'claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-sonnet-4-5',
+                           'claude-opus-4-5', 'claude-haiku-4-5') {
+        if ($Model -contains $preferred) { return $preferred }
+    }
+    $r = & $pick '^claude-' $null
+    if ($r) { return $r }
+    $r = & $pick '^gemini-' 'flash'
+    if ($r) { return $r }
+    $r = & $pick '^gemini-' $null
+    if ($r) { return $r }
+    @($Model | Sort-Object)[-1]
+}
+
+function script:Get-SpecstoryCodexCmd {
+    foreach ($f in '.specstory/cli/config.toml', (Join-Path $HOME '.specstory/cli/config.toml')) {
+        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $f)) { continue }
+        foreach ($line in (Get-Content -LiteralPath $f -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
+            if ($line -match '^\s*codex_cmd\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|''([^'']*)'')') {
+                $v = if ($Matches[1]) { $Matches[1] } else { $Matches[2] }
+                if ($v) { return $v }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    'codex'
+}
+

+        Write-Host '  One-off Codex session on the local Copilot Responses gateway.'

+        '-c', 'features.remote_compaction_v2=true',
+        '-c', 'features.code_mode.excluded_tool_namespaces=["mcp__codex_apps__sites"]'
+    )
+    if ($model) {
+        $entry = $catalog.data | Where-Object { $_.id -eq $model } | Select-Object -First 1
+        if ($entry.capabilities.limits.max_context_window_tokens) {
+            $Argv = @('-c', "model_context_window=$($entry.capabilities.limits.max_context_window_tokens)") + @($Argv)

Keep the exact `@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0` pin: it exists on public npm, while the reported `ETARGET` is consistent with the configured corporate mirror lagging. Do not hide the billing error with automatic model replay.
12:One account-side action cannot be automated by this repository: the account holder must select an organization or enterprise in GitHub’s **Usage billed to** setting at <https://github.com/settings/copilot/features>. The code change will identify this precisely and stop suggesting ineffective model/shim retries.
43:## 3. Probe the effective model and classify GitHub billing errors
45:Refactor the model section of `Invoke-CopilotDoctor` in the same module:
47:- Fetch one `/v1/models` catalog snapshot and derive both raw IDs and Claude Code aliases from it, so counts, pin validation, role validation, and live-probe selection use consistent data.
49:  - remove the Claude Code-only `[1m]` suffix from the effective configured main model;
50:  - probe that raw model when served;
51:  - only if it is absent before the request, use `Select-CopilotBestModel` and label the target explicitly as a **catalog fallback**, including why the configured pin was not used.
52:- Send exactly one inference request. Do not replay a failed request on another model.
53:- Add a response-body parser that handles direct and nested gateway shapes (`code`/`message`, `error.code`/`error.message`, and JSON encoded inside `error.message`). Preserve a compact raw-body fallback for unknown shapes.
54:- Classify HTTP 402 plus `billing_not_configured` as nonretryable, account-wide GitHub Copilot configuration. Print the GitHub settings URL and state that changing the model, running `copilot-model --auto`, or toggling the shim does not repair it.
55:- Reserve model-switch hints for genuine unavailable/unsupported-model errors. Change catalog wording from “Claude available” to “Claude advertised/served aliases”; catalog presence is not proof of successful inference.
56:- Remove the claim that role-aware OpenAI fallback happens automatically at request time. Describe `copilot-model --auto` as an explicit pin-selection command only.
76:- Auth: maintained fork emits `auth, login, --provider, copilot`; original flavor keeps bare `auth`; nonzero child status is surfaced once; no fallback argv or `--show-token` is used.
77:- Doctor helpers: configured main wins over alphabetic Gemini/Haiku; `[1m]` is stripped; an absent pin produces a labeled catalog fallback; direct and nested `billing_not_configured` bodies receive the account-wide diagnosis and URL; ordinary 4xx/model errors do not.
104:- `docs/copilot-proxy.md` / `docs/copilot-proxy.zh-TW.md`: canonical auth argv, verified installed metadata, exact `2.1.0` pin, `ETARGET`/configured-registry diagnosis, effective-model live probe, catalog-vs-inference distinction, nonretryable 402 action, and no automatic request-time fallback.

```text
1	# Windows dotfiles — standalone, pure-Windows chezmoi repo
2	
3	## Context & direction change
4	
5	Original idea was to graft native-Windows support into the existing macOS/Linux chezmoi repo (`~/.local/share/chezmoi`). Rejected by the user: it forces too many `{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "windows" }}` branches and, worst of all, a mechanical line-by-line port of the POSIX `dot_config/shell/*.sh` layer into PowerShell that would be unmaintainable. Those edits have been **restored** (repo back on clean `main`).
6	
7	New direction: build a **self-contained, Windows-only chezmoi dotfiles repo in the cwd** (`/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles`). PowerShell config is written **natively and idiomatically**, not as a translation of the Unix files. No OS branching (the repo assumes Windows). Genuinely-portable static configs (starship.toml, alacritty.toml, editor settings/keybindings) are **copied in** as the single small files they are — the maintenance cost the user worried about is the *shell* layer, which we now author fresh.
8	
9	## Confirmed decisions (carried over)
10	
11	- **Shell**: PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`). WSL is out of scope (that's the existing Linux repo's job).
12	- **Package manager**: **scoop** (user-scoped, no-admin) for CLI tools + **winget** for GUI apps. Chocolatey documented as fallback only.
13	- **Prompt**: **starship** (`starship init powershell`), config copied verbatim.
14	- **Testing**: GitHub Actions `windows-latest` CI is the real gate; local `pwsh` (brew-installed) for PSScriptAnalyzer/Pester + `chezmoi execute-template` render checks. A `dockur/windows` compose is included but flagged x86-Linux-host-only (won't run on this Apple-Silicon Mac).
15	- **Raycast vs PowerToys**: both default to Alt+Space — Raycast owns it, disable PowerToys Run. Documented + handled in installer.
16	- **Roles/bundles**: init prompts (name/email + `installX` toggles) like the parent repo, but Windows-scoped; a small set of bundles (workstation / minimal).
17	
18	## Feature scope (from the request)
19	
20	Essentials: PowerShell 7, starship, scoop+winget, core CLIs (git, neovim, lazygit, zoxide, fzf, bat, eza, ripgrep, fd, gh, delta, jq, yazi, btop), runtimes (uv required; mise, node, bun). AI agents: claude-code, opencode, codex, github-copilot-cli, specstory, antigravity. Editors: VSCode, Cursor, Notepad++. Apps: Windows Terminal, Alacritty, Raycast, PowerToys, Steam. Native PowerShell rewrite of the `copilot-proxy` tool series (`*.ps1`). Bilingual mkdocs docs.
21	
22	## Repo layout (cwd is the chezmoi source root)

1	# codex-copilot fails with empty MCP tool description HTTP 400
2	
3	**Symptoms**: `Invalid 'input[0].tools[0].description': empty string. Expected a string with minimum length 1`; `invalid_request_body`; `POST /responses 400`
4	**First seen**: 2026-08
5	**Affects**: Codex CLI through `@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0` and GitHub Copilot Responses
6	**Status**: fixed in the managed compatibility shim
7	
8	## Symptom
9	
10	```text
11	Invalid 'input[0].tools[0].description': empty string. Expected a string with minimum length 1, but got an empty string instead.
12	```
13	
14	The model is served and the request reaches GitHub, but inference never starts.
15	
16	## Root cause
17	
18	Codex records MCP discovery as Responses `mcp_list_tools` input items. An MCP
19	tool may omit its description, but GitHub Copilot's Responses validator requires
20	at least one character. This is a payload-schema mismatch, not entitlement or
21	network failure.
22	Codex 0.147 also zstd-compresses this request, so the shim must decode it before
23	the tool definitions are visible.
24	
25	## Workaround
26	
27	Apply the managed module and use `codex-copilot`. It always starts and targets
28	the shim on port 4142; the shim fills only blank tool-definition descriptions.
29	
30	## Prevention
31	
32	- Keep both repositories' `copilot-throttle-shim.js` byte-identical.
33	- Never let `codex-copilot` fall back directly to port 4141.
34	- The shim logs repaired JSON paths without request content.
35
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# `copilot-proxy` install dies with `error: ConnectionRefused downloading package manifest`
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): `copilot-proxy start` / `copilot-proxy reinstall`
4	prints
5	
6	```
7	Resolving dependencies
8	Resolved, downloaded and extracted [6]
9	error: ConnectionRefused downloading package manifest @jeffreycao/copilot-api
10	WARNING: copilot-proxy: install stalled with the proxy env — retrying without it ...
11	Resolving dependencies
12	Resolved, downloaded and extracted [6]
13	error: ConnectionRefused downloading package manifest @jeffreycao/copilot-api
14	Write-Error: copilot-proxy: could not install @jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14 — run 'copilot-proxy doctor'.
15	```
16	
17	Both attempts fail identically (with and without the proxy env), so it looks
18	like a hard network block. `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg` stays empty and
19	`.installed-spec` is never written. Meanwhile plain `npm` works fine —
20	`npm view @jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14 version` returns the version, and
21	other global npm CLIs install without complaint. That mismatch is the tell.
22	**First seen**: 2026-07-29
23	**Affects**: corp/managed Windows boxes where the npm registry is an internal
24	mirror (here `packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io`) and `registry.npmjs.org` is
25	blocked, **and** the deployed Copilot module predates the npm-install branch.
26	**Status**: fixed — `chezmoi apply`.
27	
28	## Root cause
29	
30	Two things compound:
31	
32	1. **Bun does not use the corp npm registry.** `Resolving dependencies` /
33	   `Resolved, downloaded and extracted [N]` / `error: ConnectionRefused` is
34	   **Bun's** output format, not npm's. Bun reaches for `registry.npmjs.org`,
35	   which the corp network blocks, hence `ConnectionRefused`. npm, by contrast,
36	   honours the `registry=` line in `~/.npmrc` (and the machine-level npmrc), so
37	   the same package resolves instantly.
38	2. **The deployed module was stale.** `Invoke-CopilotPkgInstallTry` prefers npm
39	   when `npm.cmd` is on PATH and only falls back to Bun otherwise — but that
40	   npm branch was added in commit `5351411`. The copy at
41	   `~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1` still had the
42	   **Bun-only** version, because `chezmoi apply` had not been run since. The
43	   source tree was correct; the deployed file was not.
44	
45	So the error says "network", the real answer is "your deployed module is behind
46	your source tree". `chezmoi status` had been flagging it the whole time:
47	
48	```
49	 M .config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1
50	```
51	
52	## Workaround
53	
54	```powershell
55	chezmoi status                 # look for a modified Copilot.psm1
56	chezmoi apply ~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1
57	copilot-proxy reinstall        # now uses npm
58	# copilot-proxy: installed @jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14 -> ...\copilot-api\pkg
59	```
60	
61	Successful run takes ~22s and reports `added 149 packages`.
62	
63	A full `chezmoi apply` also works but runs the `run_onchange` package installers
64	(scoop/winget/npm), which can take many minutes; target the single file when
65	you only need the module refreshed.
66	
67	## Prevention
68	
69	- **Check `chezmoi status` before debugging any behaviour of a chezmoi-managed
70	  script.** A stale deployed copy reproduces bugs that no longer exist in the
71	  source, and nothing warns you.
72	- Do **not** conclude "the registry is broken" from a Bun error. Confirm with
73	  npm first — `npm view <pkg> version` uses the configured registry, Bun does
74	  not. See
75	  [`packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path`](packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path.md)
76	  for how to probe the registry correctly.
77	- This is why `Copilot.psm1` carries the warning
78	  `npm.cmd not found; falling back to Bun (authenticated Azure Artifacts feeds require npm)`
79	  — if you see that line, the Bun path is about to be taken and will fail on a
80	  corp network.
81	
82	## Related
83	
84	- [`packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path`](packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path.md)
85	  — the companion trap: probing the internal registry the wrong way and
86	  concluding it is broken.
87	- `docs/copilot-proxy.md` — module overview; note it lists **bun** as the only
88	  prerequisite, which is true for *running* the proxy but not for *installing*
89	  the package on a corp feed.
90
```

160	request is rejected during **request validation**, before it reaches

165	|---|---|---|
166	| `messages must be non-empty` | **usable** — `/chat/completions` works | **emit** into `providers.yaml` |
167	| `model_not_supported` | catalogue lists it, this account is not entitled | drop |
168	| `unsupported_api_for_model` | model exists, but only on `/responses` | drop |
169	
170	What the three responses actually look like (copilot-api wraps the upstream error
171	verbatim inside `error.message`, hence the double JSON):
172	
173	```
174	$ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4141/v1/chat/completions \
175	    -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"model":"claude-opus-5","messages":[]}'

180

182	{"error":{"message":"{\"error\":{\"message\":\"model \\\"gpt-5.5\\\" is not accessible via the /chat/completions endpoint\",\"code\":\"unsupported_api_for_model\"}}\n","type":"error"}}
183	```
184	
185	!!! danger "The static `/v1/models` metadata lies in BOTH directions"
186	    **It drops models that work**: `gemini-2.5-pro` and `gemini-3-flash-preview`
187	    have `supported_endpoints: null` (empty), so a metadata filter deletes them
188	    outright — and **both are usable**.

190	    **It keeps models that don't**: `claude-sonnet-4-5` (plus
191	    `claude-opus-4-6/4-7/4-8`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-haiku-4-5`) has

195

201	    #   gemini-2.5-pro     true  "enabled"  null                                   → actually usable
202	    ```

204	    **No field in `/v1/models` predicts this.** The probe is the only truth.

399	### `copilot-raycast edit`
400	
401	Open the config in `$EDITOR` and **re-validate on save**. A broken result is
402	reported explicitly with a `generate`-or-restore-from-backup hint, instead of
403	leaving you staring at an empty model picker in Raycast. Exits 1 when the file

405	
406	## Config
407	
408	| Env var | Default | Meaning |
409	|---|---|---|
410	| `COPILOT_RAYCAST_CONFIG` | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/raycast/ai/providers.yaml` | the file Raycast watches |
411	| `COPILOT_RAYCAST_ID` | `copilot` | the `providers[].id` this tool owns; every **other** id in the file is preserved |
412	| `COPILOT_RAYCAST_LABEL` | `GitHub Copilot` | `providers[].name` |
413	| `COPILOT_RAYCAST_SUFFIX` | `" (Copilot)"` | appended to each model's display name, so typing `copilot` in the picker finds them all |
414	| `COPILOT_RAYCAST_TEMP` | `auto` | `auto`\|`on`\|`off` — overrides the temperature heuristic (it cannot be probed) |
415	| `COPILOT_RAYCAST_JOBS` | `6` | concurrent probes in the sweep |
416	| `COPILOT_RAYCAST_PROBE_BASE` | `$(_copilot_base)` (`:4141`) | where the probe POSTs; deliberately **not** the shim |
417	| `COPILOT_RAYCAST_KEEP` | `10` | timestamped backups to retain |
418	
419	Set these in `~/.shellrc.adhoc` (or `~/.config/{zsh/secrets.zsh,bash/secrets.sh}`).
420	
421	## Gotchas (these cost real debugging time)
422	
423	### Raycast validates `providers.yaml` all-or-nothing and reports NOTHING
424	
425	One model missing `context`, or written as `context: "128000"` (a type mismatch
426	on the Swift side), makes **every** custom provider disappear from the picker —
427	including providers that have nothing to do with this file. No error message, no
428	red badge, no log line.
429	
430	That is why `generate` always renders to a temp file and validates it with `yq`
431	(at least one provider, provider ids unique, every model carrying `!!str id`,
432	`!!str name`, `!!int context`) before the `mv`. Hand edits should always go
433	through `copilot-raycast edit` (which re-validates for you), or be followed
434	immediately by `copilot-raycast status` to check the `raycast` line's count.
435	
436	### `model_picker_enabled: true` does not mean the model works
437	
438	`claude-sonnet-4-5` reports `model_picker_enabled: true`,
439	`policy.state: "enabled"` and a `supported_endpoints` that explicitly lists
440	`"/chat/completions"` — and returns `model_not_supported` when you send to it.
441	Conversely `gemini-2.5-pro` has `supported_endpoints: null` and works perfectly.
442	Filtering on metadata gets it wrong in both directions at once. See
443	[the zero-quota probe](#the-zero-quota-probe) above.
444	
445	### A model missing from the picker is usually a rejected file, not a missing model
446	
447	Ask what Raycast actually loaded before guessing.
448	`raycastAI_modelRouterModelInfo` is a base64 JSON blob keyed by provider id,
449	containing the models Raycast **accepted**:
450	
451	```sh
452	plutil -extract raycastAI_modelRouterModelInfo raw -o - \
453	  ~/Library/Preferences/com.raycast.macos.plist | base64 -d | jq -r '.copilot[].model'
454	```
```

```text
1	# Copilot embeddings → semantic search
2	
3	The [Copilot → Claude Code proxy](copilot-claude-proxy.md) (`copilot-api` on
4	`localhost:4141`) is OpenAI-compatible and also serves **`POST /v1/embeddings`**,
5	backed by the same GitHub Copilot subscription. Copilot exposes three **1536-dim**
6	embedding models — `text-embedding-3-small` (default), `text-embedding-ada-002`,
7	`text-embedding-3-small-inference`. This turns the proxy into a zero-extra-cost
8	**local semantic-search** backend.
9	
10	- **Shell helpers**: `~/.config/shell/44_copilot_embed.sh` (`copilot-embed`, `semsearch`)
11	- **Search engine**: `scripts/semsearch.py` (run via `uv run --script`, resolved by
12	  `chezmoi source-path` — stays in the chezmoi source tree, not applied to `$HOME`)
13	- **Model pin (SSOT)**: `AICAP_EMBED_MODEL` in `~/.config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh`
14	- Requires the proxy to be running (`copilot-proxy start`); both helpers auto-start it.
15	
16	!!! warning "Same Copilot ToS caveat as the proxy"
17	    Embeddings go through the same reverse-engineered proxy and Copilot
18	    subscription — see the [proxy doc's ToS warning](copilot-claude-proxy.md).
19	    Indexing a large corpus fires many requests and the fork has **no rate
20	    limiter**; index big trees deliberately.
21	
22	## Quick start
23	
24	```sh
25	copilot-embed "hello world" | jq 'length'     # → 1536 (a raw embedding vector)
26	
27	semsearch index                                # index the default corpus (chezmoi docs/tools)
28	semsearch "how do I switch the copilot model"  # natural-language search → ranked hits
29	semsearch "trim a video clip" -k 5             # top-5
30	semsearch index ~/notes                        # index another directory
31	semsearch "quarterly goals" --corpus ~/notes   # query that corpus
32	```
33	
34	## How it works
35	
36	```
37	text ──▶ copilot-embed / semsearch.py ──POST /v1/embeddings──▶ copilot-api (localhost:4141)
38	                                                                 │ Authorization: Bearer <copilot token>
39	                                                                 ▼
40	                                                          api.githubcopilot.com  (your Copilot sub)
41	```
42	
43	`semsearch` chunks files by blank-line paragraphs (tracking each chunk's start
44	line), embeds them in batches, caches the vectors, and ranks by cosine similarity
45	against your query embedding. Ranking is by **meaning**, not keywords — e.g.
46	`"trim a video clip"` surfaces `ffmpeg.md`'s *"Trim / cut"* section even though the
47	words differ.
48	
49	!!! danger "The embeddings `input` MUST be an array (issue #100)"
50	    The proxy rejects a **scalar** `input` string with a generic `400 Bad Request`
51	    — this is the fork's
52	    [issue #100](https://github.com/caozhiyuan/copilot-api/issues/100)
53	    ("Can not call /v1/embeddings successful"). The fix is simply to send
54	    `"input": ["your text"]` (an array) — `{"input":"your text"}` 400s,
55	    `{"input":["your text"]}` returns a vector. Both helpers always send an array
56	    (`copilot-embed` wraps one text; `semsearch.py` batches up to 64 per request).
57	
58	## Shell helpers
59	
60	### `copilot-embed [--model M] [--json] [TEXT | -]`
61	
62	Embeds `TEXT` (a positional arg) or **stdin** (`-` or piped) and prints the vector
63	as a JSON array on **stdout** (status/metadata go to **stderr**, so pipes stay clean).
64	
65	```sh
66	copilot-embed "some text"           # vector as a JSON array
67	printf 'doc body' | copilot-embed   # embed from stdin
68	copilot-embed --json "hi" | jq '.usage'   # full API response (usage, index, …)
69	copilot-embed --model text-embedding-ada-002 "text"   # override the model
70	copilot-embed -l                    # list the embedding-model ids the proxy serves
71	```
72	
73	| Flag / env | Default | Meaning |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| `--model M` / `AICAP_EMBED_MODEL` | `text-embedding-3-small` | embedding model (empty → endpoint default) |
76	| `--json` | off | print the full response instead of just the vector |
77	| `-l` / `--list` | — | list embedding models from `/v1/models` |
78	
79	Auto-starts the proxy when it isn't answering (mirrors `copilot-run`). Requires
80	`curl` + `jq`.
81	
82	### `semsearch index [PATH...]` / `semsearch <QUERY> [-k N] [--corpus PATH]`
83	
84	Thin wrapper over `scripts/semsearch.py` (resolved via `chezmoi source-path`,
85	cached per-shell — same pattern as `aiblock`). Auto-starts the proxy, then runs the
86	engine with `uv`.
87	
88	- **`index [PATH...]`** — walk each `PATH` for `*.md,*.txt,*.sh,*.py` (override with
89	  `--glob '*.md,*.py'`), chunk, batch-embed, cache. Default `PATH` (none given) =
90	  `<chezmoi source>/docs/tools`. **Incremental**: only chunks whose content hash is
91	  new get embedded; unchanged chunks are reused and deleted/changed ones pruned.
92	  `--rebuild` forces a full re-embed.
93	- **`<QUERY>`** — embed the query, print the top-`k` (default 8) chunks as
94	  `score  path:start_line` + a one-line snippet, best first. `--corpus PATH` selects
95	  which indexed corpus to search (default: the docs corpus).
96	
97	Each corpus is keyed by a hash of its root path(s), so different trees don't
98	collide. Cache lives at:
99	
100	```
```
</details></tool-use>

1	#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
2	# /// script
3	# requires-python = ">=3.11"
4	# dependencies = [
5	#     "numpy>=2",
6	# ]
7	# ///
8	"""semsearch — semantic search over local text via the Copilot proxy.
9	
10	Engine behind the `semsearch` shell wrapper (dot_config/shell/44_copilot_embed.sh).
11	The wrapper resolves this file via `chezmoi source-path`, ensures the proxy is up,
12	and runs it with `uv run --script`. Two modes:
13	
14	  semsearch index [PATH...]          build/refresh an embedding index
15	  semsearch <QUERY> [-k N] [--corpus PATH]
16	                                     rank the indexed chunks against QUERY
17	
18	Default corpus (no PATH / no --corpus) = `<chezmoi source>/docs/tools`, so
19	"where did I document X?" becomes a natural-language query.
20	
21	Design:
22	  - Chunk each file by blank-line paragraphs, remembering each chunk's start line.
23	  - Embed via POST /v1/embeddings on the local proxy. The proxy REQUIRES `input`
24	    to be an ARRAY (a scalar 400s — the fork's issue #100), so we always send a
25	    list and batch many chunks per request.
26	  - Cache one JSONL per corpus under $XDG_STATE_HOME/copilot-proxy/embeddings/;
27	    re-indexing only embeds chunks whose content hash is new (incremental).
28	  - Query = embed the text, cosine top-k over the cached matrix (numpy).
29	
30	Config (env, set by the wrapper / the SSOT 04_ai_agents.sh):
31	  COPILOT_EMBED_BASE   proxy base URL     (fallback: http://localhost:$COPILOT_PROXY_PORT)
32	  COPILOT_PROXY_PORT   proxy port         (fallback: 4141)
33	  AICAP_EMBED_MODEL    embedding model    (fallback: text-embedding-3-small; empty → endpoint default)
34	"""
35	from __future__ import annotations
36	
37	import fnmatch
38	import hashlib
39	import json
40	import os
41	import subprocess
42	import sys
43	import urllib.error
44	import urllib.request
45	
46	import numpy as np
47	
48	DEFAULT_GLOBS = ["*.md", "*.txt", "*.sh", "*.py"]
49	MAX_CHARS = 8000          # per-chunk cap (embeddings handle ~8k tokens)
50	BATCH = 64                # texts per /v1/embeddings request
51	TIMEOUT = 120
52	
53	
54	# --- config ---------------------------------------------------------------------
55	
56	def proxy_base() -> str:
57	    base = os.environ.get("COPILOT_EMBED_BASE")
58	    if base:
59	        return base.rstrip("/")
60	    port = os.environ.get("COPILOT_PROXY_PORT", "4141")
61	    return f"http://localhost:{port}"
62	
63	
64	def embed_model() -> str:
65	    # Empty string is meaningful: omit the model so the endpoint default applies.
66	    return os.environ.get("AICAP_EMBED_MODEL", "text-embedding-3-small")
67	
68	
69	def cache_dir() -> str:
70	    state = os.environ.get("XDG_STATE_HOME") or os.path.expanduser("~/.local/state")
71	    d = os.path.join(state, "copilot-proxy", "embeddings")
72	    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
73	    return d
74	
75	
76	def default_root() -> str | None:
77	    try:
78	        out = subprocess.run(

105	def embed_batch(texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
106	    """POST a list of texts to /v1/embeddings; return vectors in input order."""

120	            body = json.load(resp)

122	        detail = e.read().decode(errors="replace")
123	        try:

125	        except (ValueError, AttributeError):
126	            pass

128	    except urllib.error.URLError as e:

130	    data = sorted(body.get("data", []), key=lambda d: d.get("index", 0))
131	    if len(data) != len(texts):
132	        die(f"embeddings returned {len(data)} vectors for {len(texts)} inputs")
133	    return [d["embedding"] for d in data]

137	    out: list[list[float]] = []
138	    for i in range(0, len(texts), BATCH):
139	        batch = texts[i : i + BATCH]
140	        out.extend(embed_batch(batch))
141	        eprint(f"  embedded {min(i + BATCH, len(texts))}/{len(texts)} chunks")
142	    return out

1	# Codex status line
2	
3	Codex now uses its built-in TUI footer; no fork or PATH shim is installed.
4	Chezmoi merges this provider-neutral list into `~/.codex/config.toml` while
5	preserving project trust, providers, plugins, and other live settings:
6	
7	```toml
8	[tui]
9	status_line = [
10	  "model-with-reasoning",
11	  "fast-mode",
12	  "git-branch",
13	  "context-remaining",
14	  "task-progress",
15	  "current-dir",
16	]
17	```
18	
19	Run `/status` when you need authoritative routing details. In a
20	`codex-copilot` session it should show the localhost model provider even if the
21	Account line still shows the logged-in ChatGPT account; that account is UI/auth
22	state, not evidence that inference bypassed the proxy.
23	
24	## Why the quota fields are absent
25	
26	Codex also offers `five-hour-limit` and `weekly-limit`, but those counters can
27	still describe the ChatGPT account when a one-shot launcher changes only the
28	model provider. Showing them beside Copilot inference would be ambiguous, so the
29	managed footer sticks to provider-neutral facts. [CodexBar](codexbar.md) remains
30	the complementary menu-bar view for account usage.
31	
32	## Why not a Claude-HUD-style extension?
33	
34	Stock Codex accepts a fixed list of status item IDs; it does not run an
35	arbitrary status command or support custom ANSI/conditional rendering. The
36	third-party `@jiawang1209/codex-hud` can emulate Claude HUD only by patching and
37	compiling an older Codex Rust tree and placing a shim ahead of the official
38	binary. That upgrade and supply-chain surface is not worthwhile for a footer,
39	so it is documented but intentionally not installed.
40	
41	`codex_apps` is unrelated to the footer and unrelated to Codex.app. It is a
42	remote ChatGPT MCP route at `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/apps`; the CLI
43	can use it on Intel or Apple Silicon. `copilot-proxy doctor --live` probes that
44	route directly and through the detected HTTP proxy, separately from localhost
45	Copilot inference.
46	
47	References: [Codex configuration](https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference),
48	[fixed status-item limitation](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/20244),
49	[custom status-line request](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/17827).
50

# 3. `[1m]`, model normalization, and capability context

## `[1m]` semantics

Canonical suffix is lowercase `[1m]`; there is no separate uppercase `[1M]` model label.

Removal:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1:753-756`

Live conversion:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1:883-899`

Behavior:

1. Strip an existing trailing `[1m]`.
2. Find the raw `.id` catalog entry.
3. If `capabilities.limits.max_context_window_tokens >= 1,000,000`, return `raw[1m]`.
4. Otherwise return raw ID without suffix.
5. If catalog is unavailable, preserve an existing suffix but do not add one to an unsuffixed model.

The suffix is Claude Code-only. Doctor and selectors remove it before inference/ranking.

Tests:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/tests/Copilot.Tests.ps1:402-417`
  - Sol at 1,000,000 gets `[1m]`.
  - Terra at 400,000 loses a stale `[1m]`.

## Manual model-ID normalization

Manual `copilot-model <id>` normalization is at:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1:2062-2075`

Candidate forms, in order:

1. Input base unchanged
2. `claude-<base>`
3. All dots changed to hyphens
4. `claude-<dot-to-hyphen form>`
5. Unique substring match against the raw list

This handles inputs such as dotted Claude family names, but only on this command path. Environment variables, manually edited state files, and existing project pins are not normalized.

## Claude role profile

Profile construction:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1:907-953`

For `gpt-5.6-sol`:

- Main/Fable/Opus: selected main
- Sonnet: `gpt-5.6-terra` if served, otherwise main
- Haiku/small-fast: `gpt-5.6-luna`, then `gpt-5.4-mini`, then `gpt-5-mini`, otherwise main

Each role independently receives or loses `[1m]` based on its own catalog metadata.

Shared environment writer:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1:984-1021`

It writes:

- `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`
- Fable/Opus/Sonnet/Haiku defaults
- `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL`
- Base/auth and traffic-control variables

It intentionally does not set `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`.

## Codex context capability injection

For an automatically selected Codex model:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1:1689-1697`

Mappings:

# 5. “Auto fallback” versus retries

There is **no runtime model failover** after inference begins.

Intentional behavior:

- A stale/missing configured model can be replaced only during explicit preselection:
  - `copilot-model --auto`
  - Codex launcher’s automatic pre-launch choice
  - Doctor’s clearly labeled fallback when the configured raw ID is absent from the catalog
- Doctor sends exactly one raw-model request and bypasses the shim:
  - `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1:1509-1545`
- Unsupported models get advice to run `copilot-model --auto`:
  - lines 858–868
- Account-wide `billing_not_configured` explicitly forbids model/shim retry advice:
  - lines 845–855

Documentation makes this explicit:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/docs/copilot-proxy.md:162-177`
- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/docs/copilot-proxy.zh-TW.md:151-162`

The shim’s retries are transport retries of the **same model/request**, not fallback:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/copilot-throttle-shim.js:197-227`

Codex also configures same-provider retries:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1:1683-1685`

# 7. Likely bugs and gaps

## High confidence

### 1. Claude `--auto` does not filter disabled or non-chat entries

Codex filters catalog eligibility at lines 1662–1665, but Claude `copilot-model --auto` feeds every raw `.id` into its picker:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1:2037-2048`

Doctor fallback similarly filters only IDs whose names contain `embedding`:

- lines 760–779

Consequences:

- A disabled high-priority Sol/Claude model can be selected.
- A `model_picker_enabled=false` entry can be selected.
- If only unknown/embedding IDs remain, the final catch-all can select one.
- Doctor’s “served” validation also includes disabled entries.

There are no policy-disabled, picker-disabled, or embedding-only Claude-picker tests.

### 2. Explicit `[1m]` bypasses live metadata

Manual selection detects and reattaches `[1m]` directly:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1:2062-2074`

That bypasses `ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel` when a suffix was supplied.

Example with live Terra metadata at 400k:

- Global target writes `gpt-5.6-terra[1m]` into state.
- Local target recomputes the role profile and strips it, but status messages still describe `$resolved` as suffixed.
- Thus local saved data and command output can disagree.

This contradicts the tested rule at `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/tests/Copilot.Tests.ps1:402-417`.

### 3. Explicit Codex models receive no context metadata

`Test-CopilotExplicitCodexModel` returns only a Boolean:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1:1628-1634`

When `-m`/`--model` is present, `$model` remains null. Context-window and compaction overrides are guarded by `if ($model)`:

- lines 1689–1697

Therefore:

- Auto `gpt-5.6-sol` gets live `model_context_window` and compact limit.
- Explicit `-m gpt-5.6-sol` does not.
- An explicit `[1m]` is not normalized away for raw Codex use.

No launcher-argument/context-injection test covers this.

### 4. Project-pin ownership is inferred from any `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`

The following all treat any project-local Anthropic gateway as owned by `copilot-here`:

- Effective precedence: lines 968–975
- `copilot-model` local-target choice: lines 1987–2000
- `copilot-here` status/drift: lines 1856–1870, 1917–1932

There is no ownership marker or check that the base is port 4141/4142. Consequently `copilot-model` can rewrite role aliases belonging to another gateway, and `copilot-here off` can remove another tool’s Anthropic keys.

The deferred global-mode design explicitly requires ownership markers and drift-safe restoration:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/backlog/copilot-proxy-global-apply-mode-for-claude-code-and-codex.md:15-22`

### 5. `copilot-here on` destroys malformed JSON

At:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1:1878-1889`

A parse failure is converted to an empty object:

```powershell
catch { [pscustomobject]@{} }
```

The command then rewrites the file, dropping all malformed/unparseable original content. `off` correctly refuses malformed JSON, but `on` does not. Writes are also non-atomic.

No malformed-settings test exists.

### 6. `copilot-here on` reports the wrong base when the shim is enabled

The written environment uses `Get-CopilotPinnedBase`, which returns port 4142 when shim mode is enabled:

- lines 707–709, 1004

But the success message always prints `Get-CopilotBase`, port 4141:

- line 1899

The ignored active pin demonstrates this mismatch: actual base is 4142.

## Medium confidence / future drift

### 7. Model normalization is incomplete and may preserve noncanonical casing

Normalization only occurs for explicit `copilot-model` arguments. It is absent for:

- `$COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL`
- Existing state file
- Existing project pin

This conflicts with the warning that dotted Claude IDs cause legacy labeling/context assumptions:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1:711-718`

Additionally, PowerShell `-contains` is case-insensitive, but the code stores the user-supplied candidate rather than the catalog’s canonical string:

- lines 2064–2067

Thus uppercase/mixed-case input can match a lowercase catalog ID and then persist the caller’s spelling.

The substring fallback also treats user `*`, `?`, and bracket characters as PowerShell wildcard syntax:

- lines 2068–2071

No dotted-ID, casing, wildcard, environment, or state normalization tests exist.

### 8. “Capability-ranked” fallback is mostly hard-coded name ranking

Capabilities are used for context size, not quality/ranking. Unknown future models are selected by lexicographic `Sort-Object`, for example:

- Claude generic fallback: lines 1952–1957
- GPT/Gemini generic fallbacks: lines 1963–1976
- Codex equivalents: lines 1589–1612

This can misorder versions such as `5.10` versus `5.9` and places future Codex models according to spelling rather than advertised capability.

The Codex exact list is also evaluated before generic future GPTs, so a future flagship not in the hard-coded list can rank below today’s Luna/mini entries.

### 9. Documented Claude-family order is not the literal main-selector order

Documentation says `Fable > Opus > Sonnet > Haiku`:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/docs/copilot-proxy.md:93-103`

But `claude-opus-4-5` is below Sonnet 5/4.6/4.5 in both selectors:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1:1946-1950`
- lines 1600–1604

This may be intentional cross-generation quality ranking, but the docs and tests do not explain it.

### 10. Offline built-in `[1m]` can become a stale persistent hint

When no catalog is available, an explicitly present suffix is preserved:

- lines 896–898

The built-in default itself is already suffixed:

- line 723

Therefore `copilot-here on` while the proxy/catalog is unavailable can persist `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]` without live confirmation. This is weaker than the documentation’s statement that the hint is derived from live metadata.

### 11. Context metadata lacks type/range validation

Both Claude and Codex directly trust nested capability fields:

- Claude cast: lines 892–895
- Codex overrides: lines 1690–1696

A nonnumeric Claude context can throw during `[long]` conversion. Codex can pass malformed/negative/string limits directly into CLI configuration. There are no malformed-capability tests.

### 12. Current-profile display can mask missing role keys

For a local pin, `copilot-model -c` substitutes the main model whenever a role key is missing:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1:2010-2018`

That makes an incomplete old pin look complete. Doctor and drift detection can expose it, but the command advertised as inspecting the profile does not. It also does not display `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL`.

### 13. Retry layers can multiply attempts

Codex configures provider request retries of 3 and stream retries of 1:

- lines 1683–1685

The shim independently retries up to 3 times:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/copilot-throttle-shim.js:29-34,197-227`

These are same-model retries, but nesting them can create substantially more upstream attempts during a persistent 403/429/5xx incident—the type of burst the shim is intended to control. No integration test constrains total attempt count.

# Read-only audit report

No files were modified. I inspected the working tree, tracked history, tests, documentation, pitfalls, backlog notes, generated copies, and historical transcripts. I did not run the Bats suite because it creates temporary files; I only invoked a few pure selector functions in read-only shells to confirm edge behavior.

## Executive findings

The reference implementation is centered on:

- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh`
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/copilot-throttle-shim.js`
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/tests/unit/copilot_proxy.bats`

The model design is intentional and mostly coherent:

- Claude Code model selection is Claude-first.
- Codex model selection is OpenAI-first.
- `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]` is the final built-in Claude-facing default.
- Raw API clients and Codex use plain model IDs.
- Claude-facing IDs receive `[1m]` when live catalog metadata reports at least 1,000,000 context tokens.
- Claude Code gets a complete Fable/Opus/Sonnet/Haiku role profile.
- Global state stores only the main model; per-project pins store all role aliases.

The most important issues found are:

1. **Exact stale-catalog comparison is a confirmed regression.** `_copilot_norm_models` and its tests remain, but production doctor no longer calls it.
2. **Claude `copilot-model --auto` does not filter disabled, non-picker, or embedding models**, unlike Codex, and can select an embedding model from an embedding-only catalog.
3. **Explicit Codex `-m/--model` choices do not receive live context and compaction limits.**
4. **Any nonempty project `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is treated as owned by `copilot-here`**, even when it belongs to another gateway.
5. **The documentation’s Luna `[1m]` example contradicts both implementation and tests.**
6. **The repository contains contradictory statements about whether Claude Code sends or strips `[1m]`.**
7. **“Auto” is persistent per launch for Codex but only a one-time saved selection for Claude Code; there is no inference-time model failover.**

# 2. Proxy control flow

## Startup

`copilot-proxy start` runs through:

1. Check whether port 4141 already answers:
   - `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh:612-616`
2. Require the saved GitHub token:
   - lines 617–621
3. Rotate three generations of logs:
   - lines 622–630
4. Install the pinned package once if necessary:
   - lines 631–634
   - package prefix/stamp logic is at lines 126–245
5. Resolve direct versus local HTTP proxy egress:
   - lines 635–648
6. Launch either:
   - original package with `--rate-limit --wait`, lines 650–670
   - maintained fork with optional `--proxy-env`, lines 671–686
7. Poll `/v1/models` for up to `COPILOT_PROXY_START_TIMEOUT`, default 45 seconds:
   - lines 689–717
8. Start the shim if persistently enabled:
   - lines 694–699

## Claude Code session flow

`claude-copilot` delegates to `copilot-run`:

1. Auto-start the gateway, lines 1237–1239.
2. Start the shim if enabled but down, line 1242.
3. Resolve the selected main model through `_copilot_default_model`.
4. Build a live role profile through `_copilot_model_profile_json`, lines 1243–1249.
5. Inject:
   - `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`
   - `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL`
   - `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL`
   - `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL`
   - `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL`
   - `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL`
   - lines 1262–1272.

An active project `settings.local.json` pin can still outrank this inherited environment, as documented at lines 37–47 and 1220–1224.

## Codex session flow

`codex-copilot`:

1. Auto-starts the proxy, line 1399.
2. Always starts the compatibility shim, even if persistent throttling is off:
   - lines 1400–1403
3. Loads the live model catalog:
   - lines 1405–1408
4. Honors explicit `-m/--model`; otherwise filters and auto-selects:
   - lines 1409–1429
5. For an auto-selected model, extracts:
   - `max_context_window_tokens`
   - `max_prompt_tokens`
   - lines 1434–1446
6. Pins the installed Codex binary’s bundled catalog:
   - lines 1448–1454
7. Supplies the per-process Responses provider and remote-compaction settings:
   - lines 1457–1490

## Persistent model flow

The default precedence is:

1. Project pin, but only in `_copilot_effective_model`
2. `COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL`
3. `$XDG_STATE_HOME/copilot-proxy/model`
4. `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]`

Exact code:

- Default/global precedence: lines 346–354
- Doctor/effective precedence: lines 382–396

`copilot-model` writes:

- full role set to `.claude/settings.local.json` when it decides `copilot-here` is active, lines 2228–2251
- one main-model line to global state otherwise, lines 2252–2257

# 3. Exact candidate ordering

## Claude Code `copilot-model --auto`

Implemented at `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh:1932-1976`.

All candidates first have a trailing `[1m]` stripped.

### Fixed Claude order

1. `claude-fable-5`
2. `claude-opus-5`
3. `claude-opus-4-8`
4. `claude-opus-4-7`
5. `claude-opus-4-6`
6. `claude-sonnet-5`
7. `claude-sonnet-4-6`
8. `claude-sonnet-4-5`
9. `claude-opus-4-5`
10. `claude-haiku-4-5`

Then the lexicographically greatest remaining `claude-*` ID.

The documentation’s shorthand “Fable > Opus > Sonnet > Haiku” is not exact: `claude-opus-4-5` intentionally follows the named Sonnet models.

### Fixed OpenAI order

1. `gpt-5.6-sol`
2. `gpt-5.6-terra`
3. `gpt-5.5`
4. `gpt-5.4`
5. `gpt-5.3-codex`
6. `gpt-5.6-luna`
7. `gpt-5.4-mini`
8. `gpt-5-mini`

Then:

1. lexicographically greatest `gpt-*` excluding `mini|nano|luna`
2. lexicographically greatest ID containing `codex`
3. lexicographically greatest remaining `gpt-*`

### Gemini and final fallback

1. Lexicographically greatest non-Flash `gemini-*`
2. Lexicographically greatest `gemini-*`
3. Lexicographically greatest model of any kind

This is ID/name ranking, not capability-field scoring.

## Codex auto ordering

Implemented at lines 1280–1323.

Codex uses the same fixed OpenAI list first, then generic GPT/Codex fallbacks, then the same fixed Claude list, then Gemini, then arbitrary fallback.

The key difference is therefore:

- Claude Code: Claude → OpenAI → Gemini → other
- Codex: OpenAI → Claude → Gemini → other

Codex’s catalog input is filtered at lines 1413–1418 for:

- `policy.state != disabled`
- `model_picker_enabled != false`
- non-embedding capability type

The Claude picker does not apply these filters.

## Role-profile ordering

Implemented at lines 1982–2032.

### Native Claude main

For each role:

- Fable: `claude-fable-5`, then greatest `claude-fable-*`, then main
- Opus: Opus 5 → 4.8 → 4.7 → 4.6 → 4.5, then greatest Opus, then main
- Sonnet: Sonnet 5 → 4.6 → 4.5, then greatest Sonnet, then main
- Haiku: Haiku 4.5, then greatest Haiku, then main

### GPT/Codex main

- Main: selected model
- Fable: selected model
- Opus: selected model
- Sonnet: `gpt-5.6-terra`, otherwise selected model
- Haiku/background:
  1. `gpt-5.6-luna`
  2. `gpt-5.4-mini`
  3. `gpt-5-mini`
  4. selected model

### Other provider

All roles use the selected main.

# 4. Model ID and `[1m]` handling

## Three model-ID views

The implementation correctly distinguishes:

1. **Raw gateway ID**  
   Example: `gpt-5.6-sol` or `claude-opus-4-8`.

2. **Claude-facing ID**  
   Example: `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]`.

3. **Cross-source comparison key**  
   Lowercase, dots changed to dashes, `[1m]` stripped.

## Cross-source normalization

`_copilot_norm_models` at lines 558–563 performs:

```text
uppercase → lowercase
"." → "-"
trailing "[1m]" → removed
sort -u
```

It is designed to fold:

- upstream `claude-opus-4.8`
- proxy raw `claude-opus-4-8`
- proxy alias `claude-opus-4-8[1m]`

into one key.

However, it is currently dead production code; see finding 1 below.

## Manual fuzzy normalization

`copilot-model` uses a different, much narrower normalization at lines 2180–2207:

- strips explicit `[1m]`
- changes dots to dashes
- tries exact input
- tries `claude-` prefix
- tries normalized input
- tries normalized `claude-` prefix
- finally requires a unique substring match

It does not lowercase input. `_copilot_norm_models`’ lowercasing therefore does not make manual `copilot-model` matching case-insensitive.

## Context hint generation

`_copilot_model_for_claude`, lines 1892–1914:

- strips existing `[1m]`
- finds the raw ID in `.data[].id`
- reads `.capabilities.limits.max_context_window_tokens`
- appends `[1m]` when the value is numeric and `>= 1000000`
- removes the hint when live metadata says less than 1M
- preserves an explicit stored hint only when there is no live catalog

Every role is passed through this function at lines 2025–2031.

## Display handling

The proxy script itself does not produce friendly Claude HUD names. The display chain is documented at:

- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/pitfalls/claude-hud-shows-raw-model-id.md:31-53`
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/claude-hud.md:208-209`
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/claude-hud.md:233-235`

Claude Code supplies `model.display_name`; claude-hud uses it when present and otherwise falls back to raw `model.id`. An old Claude Code binary that does not recognize an ID can therefore show literal `claude-opus-5[1m]` and use the wrong context size.

Raycast has separate display logic:

- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/45_copilot_raycast.sh:186-208` chooses `.name`, then `.display_name`, then `.id`.
- Lines 382–398 append `" (Copilot)"` and emit integer context.

Codex display/metadata is preserved with the bundled catalog override rather than by changing the model string.
