1554	function copilot-run {
1555	    [CmdletBinding()]
1556	    param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argv)
1557	    if (-not $Argv -or $Argv.Count -eq 0) { Write-Error 'Usage: copilot-run <cmd> [args...]'; return }
1558	    if (-not (Test-CopilotAlive)) { copilot-proxy start; if (-not (Test-CopilotAlive)) { return } }
1559	    if ((Get-CopilotShimEnabled) -and -not (Test-CopilotShimAlive)) { Start-CopilotShim | Out-Null }
1560	
1561	    # Single source of truth — see Get-CopilotEnvBlock.
1562	    $inject = Get-CopilotEnvBlock
1563	    # Scope env to the child process: set, run, restore (equivalent to `env VAR=..`).
1564	    $saved = @{}
1565	    foreach ($k in $inject.Keys) { $saved[$k] = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable($k); Set-Item "env:$k" $inject[$k] }
1566	    try {
1567	        $exe = $Argv[0]; $rest = if ($Argv.Count -gt 1) { $Argv[1..($Argv.Count - 1)] } else { @() }
1568	        & $exe @rest
1569	    } finally {
1570	        foreach ($k in $inject.Keys) {
1571	            if ($null -eq $saved[$k]) { Remove-Item "env:$k" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
1572	            else { Set-Item "env:$k" $saved[$k] }
1573	        }
1574	    }
1575	}

1723	# to -c \"custom command\"" — same slot, last write wins. So a hardcoded
1724	# `-c "claude $args"` silently drops every flag in `claude_cmd` the moment
1725	# claude-copilot has args to pass through, which made these two disagree:

1731	# truth for BOTH branches. `--no-specstory` deliberately does NOT inherit it.

42	## copilot-proxy
43	- Module at `~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot`. Commands: `copilot-proxy`
44	  (`start`/`stop`/`restart`/`status`/`doctor`/`logs`/`shim`/`whoami`/`auth`/`reinstall`),
45	  `copilot-run`, `claude-copilot`, `claude-copilot-once`, `copilot-here`,

47	- Needs `bun`. Token: `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`. Ports 4141 (proxy) /
48	  4142 (throttle shim). Default main model `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]`; the OpenAI role
49	  profile maps Fable/Opus to Sol, Sonnet to Terra, and Haiku/background to Luna.
50	  `copilot-here` writes
51	  only the gitignored `./.claude/settings.local.json`. The pinned copilot-api is
52	  installed ONCE into `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg` (never `bunx` at launch);
53	  `COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY` (auto|always|never|URL) controls whether Node fetches the
54	  GitHub model catalog through the local proxy. Full guide: `docs/copilot-proxy.md`.
55	
56	## Editors / terminal / tv
57	- VSCode & Cursor settings + keybindings are deep-merged into `%APPDATA%\{Code,Cursor}\User`
58	  by `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_20_editor_overlays.ps1.tmpl` (sources under `editors/`).
59	- Windows Terminal `profiles.defaults`, Alacritty (`%APPDATA%\alacritty\alacritty.toml`),
60	  and WezTerm (`~/.config/wezterm/wezterm.lua`, pwsh as default shell) are managed too.
61	  Television channels live under `%APPDATA%\television\cable\` (`tv <name>`).

135	# behind its 4-permit semaphore for no benefit, because a rejected-at-validation
136	# request never reaches the point the shim's retry logic protects. Override with
137	# COPILOT_RAYCAST_PROBE_BASE if you ever want the sweep throttled too.
138	_copilot_raycast_probe_base() { printf '%s' "${COPILOT_RAYCAST_PROBE_BASE:-$(_copilot_base)}"; }

140	# Sort key: bigger = earlier in providers.yaml. Mirrors _copilot_pick_best_model's
141	# vendor ranking (Claude > Codex > GPT > Gemini) but keeps ALL of them, and adds
142	# a within-family tier so opus lands above sonnet above haiku. Ties are broken by
143	# `sort -Vr` on the id, i.e. newest version first.
144	_copilot_raycast_rank() {
145	  case "$1" in
146	    claude-opus-*)   printf '59' ;;
147	    claude-sonnet-*) printf '58' ;;
148	    claude-haiku-*)  printf '57' ;;
149	    claude-*)        printf '56' ;;
150	    *codex*)         printf '45' ;;
151	    # gemini MUST be matched before any *mini* rule — "ge-mini" contains "mini",
152	    # and a naive `*mini*` arm silently demotes the entire Google family.
153	    gemini-*pro*)    printf '25' ;;
154	    gemini-*flash*)  printf '24' ;;
155	    gemini-*)        printf '23' ;;
156	    gpt-*mini*|o1*mini*|o3*mini*|o4*mini*) printf '34' ;;
157	    gpt-*|o1*|o3*|o4*)                     printf '35' ;;
158	    *)               printf '10' ;;
159	  esac
160	}

163	_copilot_raycast_temp() {

166	    0|off|false|no) printf 'false'; return 0 ;;
167	  esac
168	  case "$1" in

174	# Escape a scalar for a YAML double-quoted string (backslash first, then quote).
175	_copilot_raycast_yesc() {

179	# --- catalogue + zero-quota probe -----------------------------------------------
180	
181	# Live chat models from the proxy, one TSV row each:
182	#   id \t name \t vendor \t context \t vision \t tools \t reasoning_effort
183	# Pre-filters on capabilities.type == "chat" (drops the three embedding models)
184	# and on the "[1m]" alias, which is Claude Code-only sugar the proxy rejects from
185	# a raw API client. Everything else is decided by the probe, never by metadata.
186	_copilot_raycast_catalog() {
187	  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
188	  command curl -fsS --max-time 10 "$(_copilot_base)/v1/models" 2>/dev/null \
189	    | jq -r '
190	        .data[]
191	        | select(.capabilities.type == "chat")
192	        | [ .id,
193	            # `//` only falls through on null/false, so an EMPTY name would ship
194	            # an empty TSV field — and IFS=<tab> is IFS-whitespace, which
195	            # collapses runs of separators, silently shifting every column right
196	            # of it (name<-vendor, context<-vision, …). Coerce empties too.
197	            (if (.name // "") == "" then
198	               (if (.display_name // "") == "" then .id else .display_name end)
199	             else .name end),
200	            (if (.vendor // "") == "" then "Other" else .vendor end),
201	            (.capabilities.limits.max_context_window_tokens // 0),
202	            (if .capabilities.supports.vision      == true then "1" else "0" end),
203	            (if .capabilities.supports.tool_calls  == true then "1" else "0" end),
204	            (if (.capabilities.supports.reasoning_effort | type) == "array"
205	                and (.capabilities.supports.reasoning_effort | length) > 0
206	             then "1" else "0" end)
207	          ] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
208	    | command grep -v '\[1m\]'
209	}
210	
211	# Classify ONE model id. Echoes one of:
212	#   ok | not_supported | responses_only | no_response | unknown
213	# Body is deliberately {"messages":[]} — see the header GOTCHA. One free retry
214	# covers a transient 429/502 from the burst, which would otherwise read as a
215	# permanent "unknown" and silently drop a good model from the file.
216	_copilot_raycast_probe_one() {
217	  local model="$1" body resp i=0
218	  body="$(printf '{"model":"%s","messages":[]}' "$model")"
219	  while [ "$i" -lt 2 ]; do
220	    resp="$(command curl -s --max-time 25 \
221	              -X POST "$(_copilot_raycast_probe_base)/v1/chat/completions" \
222	              -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$body" 2>/dev/null)"
223	    case "$resp" in
224	      *'messages must be non-empty'*) printf 'ok';             return 0 ;;
225	      *model_not_supported*)          printf 'not_supported';  return 0 ;;
226	      *unsupported_api_for_model*)    printf 'responses_only'; return 0 ;;
227	    esac
228	    i=$((i + 1))
229	    [ "$i" -lt 2 ] && sleep 1

1	# Copilot.psm1 — GitHub Copilot agent gateway for Claude Code and Codex, native
2	# PowerShell port of the POSIX 43_copilot_proxy.sh / 44_copilot_embed.sh.
3	#
4	# Runs the maintained copilot-api fork (npm @jeffreycao/copilot-api) from a pinned
5	# local install so a GitHub Copilot subscription can back Claude Code and Codex.
6	# The optional Bun throttle shim (copilot-throttle-shim.js) is reused verbatim from
7	# the unix side.
8	#
9	# Public commands (exported with their original hyphenated names for muscle
10	# memory — PSUseApprovedVerbs is intentionally waived):
11	#   copilot-proxy [start|stop|restart|status|doctor [--live]|logs [shim|N]|shim [on|off|status]|whoami|auth|reinstall]
12	#   copilot-run <cmd...>            run a command with the proxy env injected
13	#   claude-copilot [args...]        one-off Claude Code session on the proxy
14	#   claude-copilot-once [args...]   pinned one-shot session, auto-reverted
15	#   codex-copilot [args...]         one-off Codex session on Responses proxy
16	#   codex-copilot-once [args...]    identical zero-persistence alias
17	# (claude-copilot / -once run claude with --dangerously-skip-permissions — the
18	#  proxy flow is the trusted, hands-off path; plain `claude` is unaffected.)
19	#   copilot-here [on|off|status]    per-project pin via ./.claude/settings.local.json
20	#   copilot-model [<id>|-l|-c|--auto]  switch the pinned model
21	#   copilot-embed [--model M] [--json] [TEXT|-] | -l
22	#   semsearch index [PATH...] | semsearch <QUERY> [-k N] [--corpus PATH]
23	#
24	# Contract preserved from the unix version: token at
25	# ~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token, ports 4141 (proxy) / 4142 (shim),
26	# state under $XDG_STATE_HOME/copilot-proxy, per-project ./.claude/settings.local.json
27	# pin, default model gpt-5.6-sol[1m], and the ANTHROPIC_* env block.
28	#
29	# The pinned package is INSTALLED ONCE into $XDG_DATA_HOME/copilot-api/pkg and the
30	# proxy runs that binary directly. It deliberately does NOT use `bunx` at launch:
31	# bunx re-resolves the package on every start, and bun stalls forever resolving
32	# through a socks proxy — which wedged `start` at "Resolving dependencies" AND kept
33	# bun's global cache lock, so every retry hung too. Force a re-install with
34	# `copilot-proxy reinstall`.
35	#
36	# Env knobs:
37	#   COPILOT_PROXY_PORT   default 4141    - port the proxy listens on
38	#   COPILOT_PROXY_START_TIMEOUT default 45 - seconds allowed for model refresh
39	#   COPILOT_SHIM_PORT    default 4142    - throttle shim port
40	#   COPILOT_API_PKG      default @jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0 - registry spec
41	#                          (name or @scope/name + optional version/tag/range;
42	#                           aliases/local/git/URL specs are rejected before cleanup)
43	#   COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL                 - override the pinned model
44	#   COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET  1               - add the telemetry-suppressing env keys
45	#   COPILOT_INSTALL_NOPROXY 1            - skip straight to the no-proxy install try
46	#   COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY   default auto    - Node->GitHub /models egress:
47	#                          auto   = use the Windows System Proxy (WinINET registry)
48	#                                   or HTTPS_PROXY when either is set; Node ignores
49	#                                   the system setting unless it is passed the env.
50	#                          always = same, but warn when no proxy is found
51	#                          never  = never pass --proxy-env
52	#                          http://127.0.0.1:PORT = force that URL
53	
54	Set-StrictMode -Off

58	function script:Get-CopilotPort { if ($env:COPILOT_PROXY_PORT) { $env:COPILOT_PROXY_PORT } else { '4141' } }
59	function script:Get-CopilotPkg  { if ($env:COPILOT_API_PKG)   { $env:COPILOT_API_PKG }   else { $script:CopilotDefaultPkg } }

555	# --- egress: which proxy should Node use for the GitHub /models fetch? --------
556	#
557	# copilot-api fetches /models at startup and refreshes its cache periodically;
558	# restart forces an immediate refresh. GitHub geo-filters the Claude catalog on
559	# some egress paths. Node does NOT honour the Windows System Proxy on its own — it
560	# only sees HTTP(S)_PROXY — so a host whose browser reaches the unfiltered catalog
561	# could still have the proxy cache a Claude-less list, which then looks exactly
562	# like an entitlement problem. Resolve the URL here and hand it to the child.
563	#
564	# COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY: auto|always|never|<url>. Returns a URL or $null.
565	function script:Resolve-CopilotHttpProxy {
566	    $mode = if ($env:COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY) { $env:COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY } else { 'auto' }
567	    switch -Regex ($mode) {
568	        '^(never|off|0|false|no)$' { return $null }
569	        '^(http|https|socks5h?)://' { return $mode }
570	        '^(always|auto|on|1|true|yes)$' { break }
571	        default {
572	            Write-Warning "copilot-proxy: unknown COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY='$mode' (use auto|always|never|http://...)"
573	            return $null
574	        }

11	#   weasel.custom.yaml      {{ include "AppData/Roaming/Rime/weasel.custom.yaml" | sha256sum }}
12	#
13	# Numbered 50 so it runs after 10_packages has had a chance to install Weasel.
14	# Like every run-script here it must never abort the apply (invariant #2): a box
15	# where Weasel isn't installed yet just warns and exits 0.
16	
17	$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
18	$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $false
19	
20	function Info($m) { Write-Host "==> $m" -ForegroundColor Cyan }
21	
22	$dir = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Rime\Weasel' -Name InstallDir -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).InstallDir
23	if (-not $dir) {
24	    Write-Warning 'Rime deploy skipped: Weasel is not installed (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Rime\Weasel missing).'
25	    Write-Warning "Re-run 'just apply' after the Weasel install completes."
26	    exit 0
27	}
28	
29	# WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy is exactly what the tray menu's 重新部署 runs
30	# (WeaselDeployer/WeaselDeployer.cpp). It takes a single argument and compares it
31	# with wcscmp, so nothing else may be appended. It also holds an exclusive mutex
32	# and returns 1 immediately if another deployer is already running.
33	$deployer = Join-Path $dir 'WeaselDeployer.exe'
34	if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $deployer)) {
35	    Write-Warning "Rime deploy skipped: $deployer not found."
36	    exit 0
37	}
38	
39	Info 'redeploying Rime (WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy)'
40	try {
41	    $p = Start-Process -FilePath $deployer -ArgumentList '/deploy' -Wait -PassThru
42	    if ($p.ExitCode -ne 0) {
43	        Write-Warning "WeaselDeployer /deploy exited $($p.ExitCode). If a deploy was already running this is harmless; otherwise redeploy from the tray icon (右鍵 → 重新部署)."
44	    } else {
45	        Info 'Rime deploy complete'
46	    }
47	} catch {
48	    Write-Warning "Rime deploy error: $_"
49	}
50	
51	exit 0
52	{{ else -}}
53	# installInputMethod is off — nothing to deploy.
54	exit 0
55	{{ end -}}
56
```

2	// copilot-throttle-shim.js — a tiny streaming reverse proxy that sits IN FRONT
3	// of the local copilot-api fork (default :4141). It provides the request
4	// compatibility fixes shared by Codex/Claude Code and stops GitHub's enterprise
5	// Copilot backend from 403-ing ("Forbidden") on bursts of premium requests,
6	// WITHOUT adding latency to normal single-agent flow.
7	//
8	//   agent client ─▶ shim (:4142) ─▶ copilot-api fork (:4141) ─▶ Copilot backend
9	//                    │
10	//                    ├─ semaphore: at most MAX concurrent in-flight upstream
11	//                    │   POSTs; a burst queues instead of hitting the backend
12	//                    │   all at once (that simultaneity is what trips abuse
13	//                    │   detection). Under the cap there is ZERO added latency.
14	//                    │
15	//                    └─ transparent retry on 403/429/502/503/504 + network
16	//                        errors, jittered backoff, BEFORE any response body is
17	//                        streamed — so the agent never sees the transient 403
18	//                        ("Please run /login"). GET/HEAD (health, /v1/models)
19	//                        bypass both, so liveness checks stay instant.
20	//
21	// Managed by copilot-proxy (see 43_copilot_proxy.sh: `copilot-proxy shim on`).
22	// Config via env (all optional):
23	//   COPILOT_SHIM_PORT       listen port                    (default 4142)
24	//   COPILOT_SHIM_UPSTREAM   upstream base URL              (default http://localhost:4141)
25	//   COPILOT_SHIM_MAX        max concurrent in-flight POSTs (default 4)
26	//   COPILOT_SHIM_RETRIES    retry attempts on transient    (default 3)
27	//   COPILOT_SHIM_BACKOFF_MS base backoff ms, doubles/try   (default 500)
28	
29	const PORT = Number(process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_PORT ?? 4142);
30	const UPSTREAM = (process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_UPSTREAM ?? "http://localhost:4141").replace(/\/+$/, "");
31	const MAX = Math.max(1, Number(process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_MAX ?? 4));
32	const RETRIES = Math.max(0, Number(process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_RETRIES ?? 3));
33	const BACKOFF_MS = Math.max(0, Number(process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_BACKOFF_MS ?? 500));
34	const RETRY_STATUS = new Set([403, 429, 502, 503, 504]);
35	
36	const log = (...a) => console.log(new Date().toISOString(), "[shim]", ...a);
37	const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
38	
39	// ---- semaphore (at most MAX permits; hands a permit straight to a waiter) ----
40	let active = 0;
41	const waiters = [];
42	function acquire() {
43	  if (active < MAX) { active++; return Promise.resolve(); }
44	  return new Promise((res) => waiters.push(res));
45	}
46	function release() {
47	  active--;
48	  const next = waiters.shift();
49	  if (next) { active++; next(); }
50	}
51	
52	function backoffMs(attempt, retryAfter) {
53	  const ra = Number(retryAfter);
54	  if (Number.isFinite(ra) && ra > 0) return Math.min(ra * 1000, 30000);
55	  return BACKOFF_MS * 2 ** attempt + Math.floor(Math.random() * BACKOFF_MS); // + jitter
56	}
57	
58	function buildUpstream(req, bodyBuf, bodyWasDecoded = false) {
59	  const url = new URL(req.url);
60	  const target = UPSTREAM + url.pathname + url.search;
61	  const headers = new Headers(req.headers);
62	  headers.delete("host");
63	  headers.delete("content-length"); // fetch recomputes from body
64	  if (bodyWasDecoded) headers.delete("content-encoding");
65	  const init = { method: req.method, headers, signal: req.signal };
66	  if (bodyBuf !== undefined) init.body = bodyBuf;
67	  return { target, init };
68	}
69	
70	function blankDescription(value) {
71	  return typeof value !== "string" || value.trim().length === 0;
72	}
73	
74	function toolLabel(tool) {
75	  const name = tool?.name ?? tool?.tool_name ?? tool?.title;
76	  return typeof name === "string" && name.trim() ? name.trim() : "unnamed tool";
77	}

79	// Codex records MCP discovery in Responses input items. Some MCP/plugin
80	// servers legally omit a tool description, which Codex serializes as "". The
81	// GitHub Copilot Responses endpoint is stricter than OpenAI's endpoint and
82	// rejects that request before inference:
83	//
84	//   Invalid 'input[0].tools[0].description': empty string.
85	//
86	// Only touch tool-definition arrays in the two Responses locations Codex uses;
87	// do not recursively rewrite user input, JSON Schema descriptions, or outputs.
88	export function normalizeResponsesToolDescriptions(payload) {
89	  let changed = 0;
90	  const patched = [];
91	
92	  const normalizeTools = (tools, prefix, requireDescriptionField = false) => {
93	    if (!Array.isArray(tools)) return;
94	    tools.forEach((tool, index) => {
95	      if (!tool || typeof tool !== "object") return;
96	      if (requireDescriptionField && !("description" in tool)) return;
97	      if (!blankDescription(tool.description)) return;
98	      const label = toolLabel(tool);
99	      tool.description = `Tool ${label}.`;
100	      changed++;
101	      patched.push(`${prefix}[${index}].description`);
102	    });
103	  };
104	
105	  if (!payload || typeof payload !== "object") return { changed, patched };
106	  // Built-in top-level tools such as web_search do not have a description by
107	  // design, so only repair an explicitly present-but-blank field there.
108	  normalizeTools(payload.tools, "tools", true);
109	  if (Array.isArray(payload.input)) {
110	    payload.input.forEach((item, index) => {
111	      // Codex versions have used more than one discriminator for persisted MCP
112	      // discovery. The stable shape is the nested tool-definition array itself.
113	      if (!item || typeof item !== "object") return;
114	      normalizeTools(item.tools, `input[${index}].tools`);
115	    });
116	  }
117	  return { changed, patched };
118	}
119	
120	export function normalizeRequestBody(pathname, bodyBuf, contentEncoding = "") {
121	  if (pathname !== "/responses" && pathname !== "/v1/responses") {
122	    return { body: bodyBuf, changed: 0, patched: [], parseError: null, decoded: false };
123	  }
124	  try {
125	    const encoding = contentEncoding.trim().toLowerCase();
126	    const decodedBody = encoding === "zstd" ? Bun.zstdDecompressSync(new Uint8Array(bodyBuf)) : bodyBuf;
127	    const payload = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(decodedBody));
128	    const result = normalizeResponsesToolDescriptions(payload);
129	    if (result.changed === 0) return { body: bodyBuf, ...result, parseError: null, decoded: false };
130	    return { body: JSON.stringify(payload), ...result, parseError: null, decoded: encoding === "zstd" };
131	  } catch (error) {
132	    // Preserve malformed/non-JSON requests verbatim; the upstream remains the
133	    // authority for their validation and error response.
134	    return { body: bodyBuf, changed: 0, patched: [], parseError: String(error), decoded: false };
135	  }
136	}
137	
138	// Stream an upstream response to the client, holding the semaphore permit until
139	// the stream ends / errors / is cancelled (true in-flight accounting).
140	function streamThrough(resp, releaseOnce) {
141	  const headers = new Headers(resp.headers);
142	  headers.delete("content-encoding");  // Bun already decoded the upstream body
143	  headers.delete("content-length");
144	  headers.delete("transfer-encoding");
145	  if (!resp.body) { releaseOnce(); return new Response(null, { status: resp.status, headers }); }
146	
147	  const reader = resp.body.getReader();
148	  const stream = new ReadableStream({
149	    async pull(controller) {
150	      try {
151	        const { done, value } = await reader.read();
152	        if (done) { controller.close(); releaseOnce(); return; }
153	        controller.enqueue(value);
154	      } catch (err) { releaseOnce(); controller.error(err); }
155	    },
156	    cancel(reason) { releaseOnce(); try { reader.cancel(reason); } catch {} },
157	  });
158	  return new Response(stream, { status: resp.status, headers });
159	}

161	export function startServer() {
162	  const server = Bun.serve({
163	    port: PORT,
164	    idleTimeout: 255, // seconds — long opus streams (saw up to ~77s)
165	    async fetch(req) {
166	    const url = new URL(req.url);
167	    const method = req.method;
168	
169	    // Health / metadata reads: straight passthrough, no permit, no retry.

188	    }

191	    const willQueue = active >= MAX;

193	    if (willQueue) log(`queued ${method} ${url.pathname} (${active} in-flight, ${waiters.length} waiting)`);

7	//
8	//   agent client ─▶ shim (:4142) ─▶ copilot-api fork (:4141) ─▶ Copilot backend
9	//                    │
10	//                    ├─ semaphore: at most MAX concurrent in-flight upstream
11	//                    │   POSTs; a burst queues instead of hitting the backend
12	//                    │   all at once (that simultaneity is what trips abuse
13	//                    │   detection). Under the cap there is ZERO added latency.
14	//                    │
15	//                    ├─ transparent retry on 403/429/502/503/504 + network
16	//                    │   errors, jittered backoff, BEFORE any response body is
17	//                    │   streamed — so the agent never sees the transient 403
18	//                    │   ("Please run /login"). GET/HEAD (health, /v1/models)
19	//                    │   bypass both, so liveness checks stay instant.
20	//                    │
21	//                    └─ SSE keepalive + stall watchdog: an OpenAI reasoning
22	//                        model produces NOTHING on the wire until its first
23	//                        token, and copilot-api withholds the response headers
24	//                        for that whole time, so the client socket can sit
25	//                        silent for minutes. See "silent socket" below.
26	//
27	// The silent socket (why the keepalive exists)
28	// --------------------------------------------
29	// copilot-api does not open the SSE stream early: measured against :4141 with
30	// gpt-5.6-sol, the response HEADERS arrive at 8.11s and the first body chunk at
31	// 8.12s — the think time is spent entirely inside one `fetch()` with zero bytes
32	// on either socket. The backend log's own p50/p90/max for that window is
33	// 7s/20s/89s, and queueing on the semaphore above stacks on top of it. Real
34	// Anthropic streams cover this with periodic `ping` events; copilot-api emits
35	// none (verified: message_start / content_block_* / message_delta / message_stop
36	// only). A silent socket is free to be reaped by anything in the path — Bun's
37	// own idleTimeout, a Clash/mihomo idle sweep — and the agent then hangs with no
38	// error at all, which is the interrupt-and-type-"continue" symptom.
39	//
40	// So for client-requested streams the shim commits a `text/event-stream`
41	// response after PING_AFTER_MS and emits SSE comment frames (`: …\n\n`, ignored
42	// by every spec-compliant parser, including the Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs)
43	// until the upstream produces something. Requests answered inside the grace
44	// window keep the old behaviour byte for byte, real status code included.
45	//
46	// Managed by copilot-proxy (see 43_copilot_proxy.sh: `copilot-proxy shim on`).
47	// Config via env (all optional):
48	//   COPILOT_SHIM_PORT       listen port                    (default 4142)
49	//   COPILOT_SHIM_UPSTREAM   upstream base URL              (default http://localhost:4141)
50	//   COPILOT_SHIM_MAX        max concurrent in-flight POSTs (default 4)
51	//   COPILOT_SHIM_RETRIES    retry attempts on transient    (default 3)
52	//   COPILOT_SHIM_BACKOFF_MS base backoff ms, doubles/try   (default 500)

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bats
# Unit tests for the pure helpers behind `copilot-proxy doctor`
#   dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh
#
# Only the OFFLINE, deterministic helpers are covered here. The doctor's
# network checks (_copilot_probe, _copilot_upstream_models) need GitHub and a
# running proxy, so they're exercised by hand, not in CI.
#
# The contract we care about (silent-regression risk):
#   1. _copilot_norm_models must fold the THREE id spellings that the same
#      model has across sources into one key, or the stale-cache diff reports
#      false positives on every run:
#        upstream GitHub : claude-opus-4.8       (dotted)
#        proxy .id       : claude-opus-4-8       (hyphenated)
#        proxy alias     : claude-opus-4-8[1m]   (Claude Code-only suffix)
#   2. _copilot_effective_model must honour the same precedence copilot-model
#      writes with (project pin > $COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL > state file > default),
#      or doctor validates a model the client never sends.

load "../test_helper.bash"

SOURCE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT"

setup() {
  SHELL_LIB="$SOURCE_DIR/dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh"
  [ -f "$SHELL_LIB" ] || skip "43_copilot_proxy.sh not found"
  TMP="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/copilot-proxy.XXXXXX")"
}

# `skip` in setup() aborts before TMP exists, so guard — an unguarded
# `[ -n .. ] && rm` would exit non-zero and fail the test it just skipped.
teardown() {
  if [ -n "${TMP:-}" ] && [ -d "$TMP" ]; then rm -rf "$TMP"; fi
  return 0
}

write_fake_codex() {
  mkdir -p "$TMP/bin" "$TMP/proj"
  printf '%s\n' \
    '#!/bin/sh' \
    'printf "key=<%s>\n" "$GITHUB_COPILOT_API_KEY"' \
    'i=0' \
    'for arg do printf "arg[%s]=<%s>\n" "$i" "$arg"; i=$((i + 1)); done' \
    > "$TMP/bin/codex"
  chmod +x "$TMP/bin/codex"
}

# --- _copilot_norm_models -------------------------------------------------------

@test "probe failure kind: curl timeout is distinct from TLS and network" {
  run bash -c "source '$SHELL_LIB'; printf '%s|%s|%s' \
    \"\$(_copilot_probe_failure_kind 28 'operation timed out')\" \
    \"\$(_copilot_probe_failure_kind 60 'SSL certificate problem')\" \
    \"\$(_copilot_probe_failure_kind 7 'failed to connect')\""
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [ "$output" = "timeout|tls|network" ]
}

@test "optional HTTP probe: any non-000 HTTP response counts as reachable" {
  mkdir -p "$TMP/bin"
  cat > "$TMP/bin/curl" <<'SH'
#!/bin/sh
printf '\n403|0.125'
SH
  chmod +x "$TMP/bin/curl"
  run bash -c "PATH='$TMP/bin:/usr/bin:/bin'; source '$SHELL_LIB'; _copilot_optional_http_probe https://example.invalid"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [ "$output" = "reached|403|0.125|" ]
}

@test "optional HTTP probe: certificate failures stay distinguishable" {
  mkdir -p "$TMP/bin"
  cat > "$TMP/bin/curl" <<'SH'
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' 'curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate' '000|0.250'
exit 60
SH
  chmod +x "$TMP/bin/curl"
  run bash -c "PATH='$TMP/bin:/usr/bin:/bin'; source '$SHELL_LIB'; _copilot_optional_http_probe https://example.invalid"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [[ "$output" == "failed|tls|0.250|"* ]]
}

@test "norm_models: dotted, hyphenated and [1m] spellings fold to one key" {
  run bash -c "printf '%s\n' 'claude-opus-4.8' 'claude-opus-4-8' 'claude-opus-4-8[1m]' \
    | { source '$SHELL_LIB'; _copilot_norm_models; }"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [ "$output" = "claude-opus-4-8" ]
}

@test "norm_models: lowercases and de-duplicates" {
  run bash -c "printf '%s\n' 'CLAUDE-Sonnet-5' 'claude-sonnet-5' \
    | { source '$SHELL_LIB'; _copilot_norm_models; }"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [ "$output" = "claude-sonnet-5" ]
}

@test "norm_models: strips [1m] only as a suffix, not mid-string" {
  run bash -c "printf '%s\n' 'gpt-5.5[1m]' 'weird[1m]name' \
    | { source '$SHELL_LIB'; _copilot_norm_models; }"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  printf '%s\n' "$output" | grep -qx 'gpt-5-5'
  printf '%s\n' "$output" | grep -qx 'weird\[1m\]name'
}

@test "norm_models: a missing upstream id survives the set-difference" {
  # The diff doctor performs: upstream MINUS served, restricted to claude ids.
  local served upstream missing
  served="$(printf '%s\n' 'gpt-5.5' 'gemini-2.5-pro' | { source "$SHELL_LIB"; _copilot_norm_models; })"
  upstream="$(printf '%s\n' 'claude-opus-4.8' 'gpt-5.5' | { source "$SHELL_LIB"; _copilot_norm_models; })"
  missing="$(printf '%s\n' "$upstream" | grep -i '^claude' | while IFS= read -r m; do
    printf '%s\n' "$served" | grep -qxF "$m" || printf '%s\n' "$m"
  done)"
  [ "$missing" = "claude-opus-4-8" ]
}

@test "norm_models: identical lists yield an empty difference" {
  local served upstream missing
  served="$(printf '%s\n' 'claude-opus-4-8' 'claude-opus-4-8[1m]' | { source "$SHELL_LIB"; _copilot_norm_models; })"
  upstream="$(printf '%s\n' 'claude-opus-4.8' | { source "$SHELL_LIB"; _copilot_norm_models; })"
  missing="$(printf '%s\n' "$upstream" | grep -i '^claude' | while IFS= read -r m; do
    printf '%s\n' "$served" | grep -qxF "$m" || printf '%s\n' "$m"
  done)"
  [ -z "$missing" ]
}

# --- _copilot_pkg_name / _copilot_pkg_ready -------------------------------------
#
# pkg_name feeds the pkill pattern that reaps a stalled `bun add`. The naive
# "${spec%@*}" returns EMPTY for a scoped spec with no version, which would turn
# the reap into `pkill -f 'bun add.*'` — a pattern that matches every bun install
# on the box. Hence the scope-stripped test inside the helper, and these cases.

@test "pkg_name: strips the version but keeps the @scope" {
  run bash -c "COPILOT_API_PKG='@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0' \
    bash -c \"source '$SHELL_LIB'; _copilot_pkg_name\""
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [ "$output" = "@jeffreycao/copilot-api" ]
}

@test "pkg_name: a scoped spec with NO version survives intact (not emptied)" {
  run bash -c "COPILOT_API_PKG='@jeffreycao/copilot-api' \
    bash -c \"source '$SHELL_LIB'; _copilot_pkg_name\""
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [ -n "$output" ]
  [ "$output" = "@jeffreycao/copilot-api" ]
}

@test "pkg_name: unscoped spec, with and without a version" {
  run bash -c "COPILOT_API_PKG='copilot-api@0.7.0' \
    bash -c \"source '$SHELL_LIB'; _copilot_pkg_name\""
  [ "$output" = "copilot-api" ]
  run bash -c "COPILOT_API_PKG='copilot-api' \
    bash -c \"source '$SHELL_LIB'; _copilot_pkg_name\""
  [ "$output" = "copilot-api" ]
}

@test "pkg_ready: false when the stamp names a DIFFERENT spec than the pin" {

    source '$SHELL_LIB'; _copilot_pkg_ready"

@test "wantsStream only classifies an explicit stream:true body" {

  local shim="$SOURCE_DIR/dot_config/shell/copilot-throttle-shim.js"
  run bun -e "import { wantsStream as w } from '$shim';
    const enc=(o)=>new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(o)).buffer;
    console.log(JSON.stringify({
      yes:      w(enc({model:'m',stream:true})),
      str:      w(JSON.stringify({model:'m',stream:true})),
      no:       w(enc({model:'m',stream:false})),
      missing:  w(enc({model:'m'})),
      truthy:   w(enc({model:'m',stream:'true'})),
      garbage:  w(new TextEncoder().encode('not json').buffer),
    }));"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [ "$(printf '%s' "$output" | jq -r '.yes')" = "true" ]
  [ "$(printf '%s' "$output" | jq -r '.str')" = "true" ]
  # Anything that is not literally `true` must fall back to the pre-keepalive
  # path — a non-streaming caller would choke on injected comment frames.
  [ "$(printf '%s' "$output" | jq -r '.no')" = "false" ]
  [ "$(printf '%s' "$output" | jq -r '.missing')" = "false" ]
  [ "$(printf '%s' "$output" | jq -r '.truthy')" = "false" ]
  [ "$(printf '%s' "$output" | jq -r '.garbage')" = "false" ]
}

# End-to-end against a mock upstream that withholds its response headers the way
# copilot-api does while a reasoning model thinks. Guards the four-way split the
# keepalive introduced; see pitfalls/copilot-proxy-openai-model-silent-stall.md.
@test "shim keepalive fires only on slow streams, leaving fast + non-stream untouched" {
  command -v bun >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "bun not installed"
  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not installed"
  local shim="$SOURCE_DIR/dot_config/shell/copilot-throttle-shim.js"
  cat >"$TMP/keepalive.js" <<'JS'
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
const up = Bun.serve({ port: 0, idleTimeout: 60, async fetch(req) {
  const u = new URL(req.url);
  await sleep(Number(u.searchParams.get("delay") ?? 0));
  if (u.searchParams.get("mode") === "status")
    return new Response('{"error":"nope"}', { status: 400, headers: { "content-type": "application/json" } });
  return new Response("event: message_start\ndata: {}\n\nevent: message_stop\ndata: {}\n\n",
    { headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" } });
} });
process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_PORT = "0";
process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_UPSTREAM = `http://localhost:${up.port}`;
process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_PING_MS = "150";
process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_PING_AFTER_MS = "100";
process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_STALL_MS = "5000";
const { startServer } = await import(process.argv[2]);
const shim = startServer();
const call = async (q, stream = true) => {
  const r = await fetch(`http://localhost:${shim.port}/v1/messages${q}`, { method: "POST",
    headers: { "content-type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ model: "m", stream }) });
  const body = await r.text();
  return { status: r.status, ct: r.headers.get("content-type"),
    pings: (body.match(/^: /gm) ?? []).length,
    events: (body.match(/^event: (\S+)/gm) ?? []).map((s) => s.slice(7)) };
};
const out = {
  slow:    await call("?delay=800"),
  fast:    await call("?delay=0"),
  plain:   await call("?delay=800&mode=status", false),
  lateErr: await call("?delay=800&mode=status"),
};
console.log(JSON.stringify(out));
shim.stop(true); up.stop(true);
JS
  run bash -c "bun '$TMP/keepalive.js' '$shim' 2>&1 | tail -n 1"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  local j="$output"
  # Slow stream: comment frames while the upstream is silent, real events after.
  [ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r '.slow.pings > 0')" = "true" ]
  [ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r '.slow.events | join(",")')" = "message_start,message_stop" ]
  # Fast stream: inside the grace window, so nothing is injected at all.
  [ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r '.fast.pings')" = "0" ]
  # Non-streaming request: never eligible — real 400 and the JSON body verbatim.
  [ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r '.plain.status')" = "400" ]
  [ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r '.plain.ct')" = "application/json" ]
  [ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r '.plain.pings')" = "0" ]
  # A non-2xx that arrives AFTER the early commit can only be an SSE error event.
  [ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r '.lateErr.status')" = "200" ]
  [ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r '.lateErr.events | join(",")')" = "error" ]
}

```text
1	# codex-copilot fails with empty MCP tool description HTTP 400
2	
3	**Symptoms**: `Invalid 'input[0].tools[0].description': empty string. Expected a string with minimum length 1`; `invalid_request_body`; `POST /responses 400`
4	**First seen**: 2026-08
5	**Affects**: Codex CLI through `@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0` and GitHub Copilot Responses
6	**Status**: fixed in the managed compatibility shim
7	
8	## Symptom
9	
10	```text
11	Invalid 'input[0].tools[0].description': empty string. Expected a string with minimum length 1, but got an empty string instead.
12	```
13	
14	The model is served and the request reaches GitHub, but inference never starts.
15	
16	## Root cause
17	
18	Codex records MCP discovery as Responses `mcp_list_tools` input items. An MCP
19	tool may omit its description, but GitHub Copilot's Responses validator requires
20	at least one character. This is a payload-schema mismatch, not entitlement or
21	network failure.
22	Codex 0.147 also zstd-compresses this request, so the shim must decode it before
23	the tool definitions are visible.
24	
25	## Workaround
26	
27	Apply the managed module and use `codex-copilot`. It always starts and targets
28	the shim on port 4142; the shim fills only blank tool-definition descriptions.
29	
30	## Prevention
31	
32	- Keep both repositories' `copilot-throttle-shim.js` byte-identical.
33	- Never let `codex-copilot` fall back directly to port 4141.
34	- The shim logs repaired JSON paths without request content.
35
```
</details></tool-use>

commit ee5612c57278df5540ac80ad28ede91b57c3f09c
Author:     Da-Wei Lee <daviddwlee84@gmail.com>
AuthorDate: Wed Aug 19 12:09:53 2026 +0800
Commit:     Da-Wei Lee <daviddwlee84@gmail.com>
CommitDate: Wed Aug 19 12:20:08 2026 +0800

    copilot shim: SSE keepalive + stall watchdog for silent reasoning streams
    
    copilot-api does not open the SSE stream early: measured against :4141 with
    gpt-5.6-sol, the response headers arrive at 8.11s and the first body chunk at
    8.12s, so a reasoning model's whole think time is spent inside one fetch() with
    zero bytes on either socket (backend log p50/p90/max time-to-headers:
    7s/20s/89s). It also emits no `ping` events, which is how the real Anthropic API
    covers that window. Queueing on the shim's semaphore (COPILOT_SHIM_MAX=4) stacks
    more silence on top: request 5 waits with literally no traffic.
    
    Three timers race on that silence, and the tightest one is ours:
    Bun.serve idleTimeout 255s < Claude Code's 300s stream-idle watchdog for a
    third-party base URL < its 600s API_TIMEOUT_MS. So a queued agent in a 6-agent
    workflow gets its socket reaped by the shim itself, and the session hangs with
    no error — the interrupt-and-type-"continue" symptom.
    
    The shim now commits the text/event-stream response itself after
    COPILOT_SHIM_PING_AFTER_MS of silence and emits SSE comment frames every
    COPILOT_SHIM_PING_MS until real bytes arrive. A comment line is discarded by
    every spec-compliant parser, so it is invisible to the Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs
    alike and works for /v1/messages and Codex's /responses. The permit is now taken
    inside the pipeline so queue time is covered too, and COPILOT_SHIM_STALL_MS
    bounds each attempt: a pre-header stall retries transparently (nothing but
    comment frames has reached the client), a mid-stream stall fails the response
    instead of hanging.
    
    Requests answered inside the grace window are untouched — real status, real
    headers — which keeps a fast 400 model_not_supported or 401 IDE token expired
    reporting itself properly.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

diff --git a/docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md b/docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md
index 14e4677..06062d5 100644
--- a/docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md
+++ b/docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md
@@ -505,80 +505,118 @@ Full post-mortem, with the verbatim symptoms to grep:
 
 `copilot-api` fetches `/models` from GitHub when the process starts, caches the
 result for its whole lifetime, and never re-fetches. Two common ways that one
 request returns a **Claude-less** catalog:
 
 1. **Egress geo-filter (GFW hosts, post-TUN)** — GitHub serves Claude ids when the
    request egresses overseas (e.g. Singapore VLESS), and omits them on direct/CN
    egress. **Node does not honor the macOS System Proxy**, so with only
    System Proxy / no TUN, `copilot-api` and OpenCode fetch the direct catalog
    (0 Claude) while `curl` through Clash still sees Claude. Fix: `copilot-proxy
    start` with `COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY=auto` (default) attaches `--proxy-env` +
    `HTTPS_PROXY` when `proxy-status` finds a local proxy. OpenCode needs the
    same env in its launch environment.
 2. **Flaky node** — a degraded Clash node returns a truncated list; restart after
    the node is healthy.
 
 The tell is in the startup banner:
 
 ```
 ℹ Models refresh: 17 new     ← often the direct/CN catalog (no claude ids)
 ℹ Models refresh: 25 new     ← healthy via overseas proxy (includes claude-*)
 ```
 
 `copilot-proxy doctor` A/Bs **upstream direct** vs **upstream via proxy** vs the
 **served** cache so it no longer mis-labels geo-filter as "org entitlement".
 Full write-up:
 [`pitfalls/copilot-api-caches-degraded-model-list-at-startup.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/copilot-api-caches-degraded-model-list-at-startup.md).
 
 ### `settings.local.json` env beats shell env (docs say otherwise)
 
 Verified empirically (2026-07): current Claude Code lets the `env` block of
 `./.claude/settings.local.json` **override inherited shell env vars** — the
 opposite of what the official settings docs imply. Consequences:
 
 - `claude-copilot` / `copilot-run` **cannot** redirect a project where
   `copilot-here on` is active (harmless when both point at the same proxy,
   silently wrong when they don't).
 - Trialing another proxy/port via the wrapper requires `copilot-here off`
   first.
 
+### OpenAI models go silent while they think — the shim keeps the socket warm
+
+`copilot-api` does **not** open the SSE stream early: measured against `:4141`
+with `gpt-5.6-sol`, the response *headers* arrive at 8.11s and the first body
+chunk at 8.12s, so a reasoning model's whole think time is spent inside one
+`fetch()` with zero bytes on the wire. Real Anthropic streams cover that with
+periodic `ping` events; this gateway emits none. Add the shim's concurrency
+queue on top (`COPILOT_SHIM_MAX`, default 4 — request 5 waits in total silence)
+and any idle timer in the path is free to reap a perfectly healthy connection.
+The agent then hangs with no error, and the only way out is Esc + `continue`.
+
+So for client-requested streams the shim commits the `text/event-stream`
+response itself after `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_AFTER_MS` of silence and emits SSE
+*comment* frames (`: copilot-shim keepalive`, discarded by every spec-compliant
+parser, so invisible to both the Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs) every
+`COPILOT_SHIM_PING_MS` until real bytes arrive — covering queue time, think
+time, and mid-stream reasoning gaps alike. `COPILOT_SHIM_STALL_MS` bounds each
+attempt: a pre-header stall is aborted and retried transparently (nothing but
+comment frames has reached the client), a mid-stream stall fails the response
+with a real error instead of hanging.
+
+| Env | Default | Meaning |
+|---|---|---|
+| `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_MS` | `15000` | keepalive interval; `0` disables |
+| `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_AFTER_MS` | `10000` | silence tolerated before the SSE response is committed early |
+| `COPILOT_SHIM_STALL_MS` | `240000` | silence that counts as a wedged upstream; `0` disables |
+
+Requests answered inside the grace window are untouched — real status code, real
+headers — which is what keeps a fast `400 model_not_supported` or `401 IDE token
+expired` reporting itself properly. Beware the flip side: once the SSE response
+is committed, a late non-2xx can only be delivered as an SSE `error` event, so
+don't shrink `COPILOT_SHIM_PING_AFTER_MS` to zero.
+
+`0 tok` in FleetView is **not** evidence of this bug — that counter is only
+filled in when an agent finishes. Check `agent-<id>.jsonl` for growing
+`assistant` entries first. Full diagnosis:
+[`pitfalls/copilot-proxy-openai-model-silent-stall.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/copilot-proxy-openai-model-silent-stall.md).
+
 ### The fork has no rate limiter
 
 The fork's `start` dropped `--rate-limit`/`--wait`. Its README's mitigation is
 reducing Claude Code's chatter instead — that's exactly what
 `COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET=1` injects (off by default here; we prioritize UX over
 Copilot quota). If you really want request throttling, fall back to the
 original: `COPILOT_API_PKG=copilot-api@0.7.0`.
 
 ### Context management is translated, not Anthropic-native
 
 Older fork releases could forward Claude Code's `context_management` field to
 an endpoint that rejected it with 400
 ([caozhiyuan#305](https://github.com/caozhiyuan/copilot-api/issues/305)). The
 `2.1.0` GPT-5.6 path suppresses that incompatible field and relies on Responses
 reasoning/context handling instead. This avoids the 400, but Anthropic's exact
 context-editing and prompt-cache semantics are not reproduced; long-session
 behavior remains a compatibility surface to watch.
 
 ### Do not use Claude Code's `/model` picker
 
 It sends Anthropic's *official* dated ids (e.g. `claude-opus-4-8-YYYYMMDD`),
 which the Copilot backend rejects:
 
 ```
 API Error: 400 {"error":{"message":"The requested model is not supported.",
 "code":"model_not_supported", ...}}
 ```
 
 Pin the model with `copilot-model` instead — undated hyphenated ids
 (`claude-opus-4-8`) work; only the picker's dated ids fail.
 
 ### Dotted ids cause the "[Opus 4] retired" warning and a >100% context HUD
 
 Historic gotcha, fixed by the hyphenated defaults. With a **dotted** id
 (`claude-opus-4.8`, the only shape the original proxy accepted), Claude Code
 fails to match its built-in model table, so it:
 
 - displays `[Opus 4]` and warns *"Claude Opus 4 was retired"* (falls back to
   the nearest known, retired name), and
 - assumes a **200k** context window, while Copilot actually serves opus-5 /

--- a/dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh

@@ -208,84 +208,90 @@ _copilot_ensure_pkg() {
     '{"name":"copilot-api-runner","private":true,"version":"0.0.0"}' >"$prefix/package.json"
 
   printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: installing $spec (one-time — later starts skip this) ..."
   # Attempt 1 honours the ambient env: on a host where the npm registry is only
   # reachable THROUGH the proxy, stripping it would break the install. Attempt 2
   # strips it, which is what rescues the socks stall. COPILOT_INSTALL_NOPROXY=1
   # skips straight to attempt 2 (saves the 45s stall on a known-bad host).
   if [ "${COPILOT_INSTALL_NOPROXY:-0}" = "1" ] \
      || ! _copilot_pkg_install_try "$prefix" env 45; then
     if [ "${COPILOT_INSTALL_NOPROXY:-0}" != "1" ]; then
       printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: install stalled with the proxy env — retrying without it ..." >&2
       # Drop bun's cache lock dir before retrying; the killed attempt may have
       # left it behind, and a stale lock hangs the retry for the same reason.
       command rm -rf -- "${BUN_INSTALL:-$HOME/.bun}/install/cache/.tmp" 2>/dev/null
     fi
     if ! _copilot_pkg_install_try "$prefix" noproxy 90; then
       # Bun and Node do not always use the same CA store. A Clash/TUN node that
       # produces UNKNOWN_CERTIFICATE_VERIFICATION_ERROR in Bun can still be
       # installed safely by npm with normal TLS verification enabled.
       if command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
         printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: Bun install failed — retrying with npm's CA stack ..." >&2
         if ! _copilot_pkg_install_try "$prefix" npm 90; then
           printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: could not install $spec — run 'copilot-proxy doctor'." >&2
           return 1
         fi
       else
         printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: could not install $spec — run 'copilot-proxy doctor'." >&2
         return 1
       fi
     fi
   fi
 
   if [ ! -x "$bin" ]; then
     printf '%s\n' "copilot-proxy: install finished but $bin is missing." >&2
     return 1
   fi
   printf '%s\n' "$spec" >"$(_copilot_pkg_stamp)"
 }

+# End-to-end against a mock upstream that withholds its response headers the way
+# copilot-api does while a reasoning model thinks. Guards the four-way split the
+# keepalive introduced; see pitfalls/copilot-proxy-openai-model-silent-stall.md.
+@test "shim keepalive fires only on slow streams, leaving fast + non-stream untouched" {
+  command -v bun >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "bun not installed"
+  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not installed"
+  local shim="$SOURCE_DIR/dot_config/shell/copilot-throttle-shim.js"
+  cat >"$TMP/keepalive.js" <<'JS'
+const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
+const up = Bun.serve({ port: 0, idleTimeout: 60, async fetch(req) {
+  const u = new URL(req.url);
+  await sleep(Number(u.searchParams.get("delay") ?? 0));
+  if (u.searchParams.get("mode") === "status")
+    return new Response('{"error":"nope"}', { status: 400, headers: { "content-type": "application/json" } });
+  return new Response("event: message_start\ndata: {}\n\nevent: message_stop\ndata: {}\n\n",
+    { headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" } });
+} });
+process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_PORT = "0";
+process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_UPSTREAM = `http://localhost:${up.port}`;
+process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_PING_MS = "150";
+process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_PING_AFTER_MS = "100";
+process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_STALL_MS = "5000";
+const { startServer } = await import(process.argv[2]);
+const shim = startServer();
+const call = async (q, stream = true) => {
+  const r = await fetch(`http://localhost:${shim.port}/v1/messages${q}`, { method: "POST",
+    headers: { "content-type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ model: "m", stream }) });
+  const body = await r.text();
+  return { status: r.status, ct: r.headers.get("content-type"),
+    pings: (body.match(/^: /gm) ?? []).length,
+    events: (body.match(/^event: (\S+)/gm) ?? []).map((s) => s.slice(7)) };
+};
+const out = {
+  slow:    await call("?delay=800"),
+  fast:    await call("?delay=0"),
+  plain:   await call("?delay=800&mode=status", false),
+  lateErr: await call("?delay=800&mode=status"),
+};
+console.log(JSON.stringify(out));
+shim.stop(true); up.stop(true);
+JS
+  run bash -c "bun '$TMP/keepalive.js' '$shim' 2>&1 | tail -n 1"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  local j="$output"
+  # Slow stream: comment frames while the upstream is silent, real events after.
+  [ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r '.slow.pings > 0')" = "true" ]
+  [ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r '.slow.events | join(",")')" = "message_start,message_stop" ]
+  # Fast stream: inside the grace window, so nothing is injected at all.
+  [ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r '.fast.pings')" = "0" ]
+  # Non-streaming request: never eligible — real 400 and the JSON body verbatim.
+  [ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r '.plain.status')" = "400" ]
+  [ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r '.plain.ct')" = "application/json" ]
+  [ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r '.plain.pings')" = "0" ]
+  # A non-2xx that arrives AFTER the early commit can only be an SSE error event.
+  [ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r '.lateErr.status')" = "200" ]
+  [ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r '.lateErr.events | join(",")')" = "error" ]
+}

```text
1	# copilot-proxy
2	
3	A native PowerShell port of the `copilot-proxy` tool series. It runs the
4	[`@jeffreycao/copilot-api`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@jeffreycao/copilot-api)
5	fork so a **GitHub Copilot subscription** can back **Claude Code** and other
6	Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible clients.
7	
8	The module is deployed to `~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot` and imported by
9	the PowerShell profile. It requires Bun, Node/npm and a Copilot subscription.
10	
11	## Commands
12	
13	| Command | What it does |
14	|---|---|
15	| `copilot-proxy auth` | one-time GitHub device login (`copilot-api auth login --provider copilot`; stores but does not display the token) |
16	| `copilot-proxy start` / `stop` / `restart` | manage the local proxy (port 4141) |
17	| `copilot-proxy status` | show raw served count and Claude availability |
18	| `copilot-proxy doctor [--live]` | diagnose package, auth, proxy, catalog, roles, upstream and Codex Apps |
19	| `copilot-proxy logs [N]` | tail the proxy log |
20	| `copilot-proxy shim [on\|off]` | toggle the throttle shim (port 4142) |
21	| `copilot-proxy whoami` | account / plan / quota |
22	| `copilot-proxy reinstall` | wipe and reinstall the pinned package |
23	| `copilot-run <cmd...>` | run a command with the proxy env injected |
24	| `claude-copilot` | one-off Claude Code session on the proxy |
25	| `claude-copilot-once` | pin this project, run once, then restore it |
26	| `codex-copilot` / `codex-copilot-once` | zero-persistence Codex session on the Responses proxy |
27	| `copilot-here [on\|off\|status]` | sticky project pin in `.claude/settings.local.json` |
28	| `copilot-model [<id>\|-l\|-c\|--auto]` | switch or inspect the complete role profile |
29	| `copilot-embed [TEXT\|-]` | embed text through `/v1/embeddings` |
30	| `semsearch index \| <QUERY>` | semantic search over local text |
31	
32	## Quick start
33	
34	```powershell
35	copilot-proxy auth                 # once
36	copilot-proxy start
37	copilot-model --auto              # select from the live catalog
38	copilot-model -c                   # inspect Main/Fable/Opus/Sonnet/Haiku
39	copilot-here on                    # sticky project; or use claude-copilot-once
40	codex-copilot                     # Codex; live OpenAI-first model selection
41	```
42	
43	Existing global and project pins are deliberately not migrated by `chezmoi
44	apply`. Run `copilot-model --auto` once after this upgrade. When `copilot-here`
45	is active, that command refreshes the local role set; otherwise it updates the
46	global one-line main-model state.
47	
48	## How routing works
49	
50	```text
51	Claude Code --Anthropic /v1/messages--> copilot-api (localhost:4141)
52	                                          | Claude: native Messages path
53	                                          | GPT: Anthropic -> Responses translation
54	                                          v
55	                                  GitHub Copilot API
56	```
57	
58	The default package is `@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0`. For GPT ids it translates
59	Claude Code requests to Responses, including `output_config.effort` to
60	`reasoning.effort`. This is required for GPT-5.6 and Claude Code's `ultracode`
61	effort setting; the old `1.13.14` path could replace the requested effort with a
62	hard-coded fallback.
63	
64	The package is installed once under `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg`. Windows
65	uses `npm.cmd` first because it understands the Azure Artifacts credential
66	provider in `~/.npmrc`; Bun remains the fallback/runtime. Readiness is based on
67	the installed `package.json` name/version, a verified stamp, and a runnable launch
68	path—not merely an old directory or binlink. A failed install cannot restamp or
69	launch stale package contents. `COPILOT_API_PKG` accepts registry package specs
70	(name or `@scope/name` with an optional version/tag/range); npm aliases and
71	local/git/URL specs are rejected before filesystem cleanup. Warm starts do no
72	package network work.
73	
74	On a corporate mirror, `ETARGET` can mean the exact public version has not synced
75	yet. Check the registry that npm is actually using before deleting the working
76	prefix:
77	
78	```powershell
79	npm config get registry
80	npm view '@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0' version
81	# Optional comparison where direct public npm is permitted:
82	npm view '@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0' version --registry https://registry.npmjs.org/
83	```
84	
85	If only the configured mirror is missing the version, wait/request mirror sync or
86	use an approved registry for `copilot-proxy reinstall`. The Windows module also
87	falls back automatically to the exact 2.1.0 runtime files on jsDelivr, verifies a
88	baked SHA-256 for every file, then resolves only its ordinary dependencies through
89	the configured npm registry. This handles a lagging mirror without weakening the
90	pin or bypassing the approved feed for the dependency tree. Do not replace the
91	tested exact pin with `latest`.
92	
93	## Model selection and role profile
94	
95	`copilot-model --auto` requires the live `/v1/models` catalog. It prefers served
96	Claude families (`Fable > Opus > Sonnet > Haiku`), then ranks OpenAI by capability:
97	
98	```text
99	Sol > Terra > GPT-5.5 > GPT-5.4 > GPT-5.3 Codex > Luna > mini > Gemini
100	```
101	
102	Luna follows the older flagships because it is the lightweight tier. This role
103	intent follows OpenAI's [current model guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model).
104	For the normal Claude-less Copilot catalog, the generated profile is:
105	
106	| Claude Code role | Copilot model |
107	|---|---|
108	| Main / Fable / Opus | `gpt-5.6-sol` |
109	| Sonnet | `gpt-5.6-terra` |
110	| Haiku / background / legacy small-fast | `gpt-5.6-luna` |
111	
112	A manually selected OpenAI main remains Main/Fable/Opus; Terra and Luna are used
113	for the lower roles when served. Missing tiers fall back to the selected main,
114	never to an unserved hard-coded id. Native Claude profiles select the strongest
115	served model in each Claude family.
116	
117	The `[1m]` suffix is a Claude Code-only context hint. It is derived from each
118	model's live `max_context_window_tokens` metadata when the value is at least one
119	million. Raw API clients must use the plain id. Offline manual discovery remains
120	available, but offline `--auto` refuses to write a potentially stale pin.
121	
122	Both `copilot-run` and `copilot-here on` inject the same variables:
123	
124	```text
125	ANTHROPIC_MODEL
```
</details></tool-use>

### Terminology that should remain explicit

There are currently several unrelated “fallback” mechanisms:

- **Catalog auto-selection, before inference**
  - `copilot-model --auto` reads live `/v1/models`, ranks models, and persists a main/role profile.
  - `codex-copilot` independently reads the catalog, ranks OpenAI-first, and injects `-m` for that invocation.
- **Doctor catalog fallback**
  - `Resolve-CopilotDoctorTarget` selects an advertised diagnostic target when the configured pin is absent.
  - Doctor still sends exactly one inference request.
- **Same-model retry**
  - The throttle shim retries transient 403/429 bursts.
  - Codex configures request/stream retries.
  - Neither substitutes a different model.
- **Package-install fallback**
  - npm/Bun installation can fall back to hash-pinned jsDelivr runtime files.

A new feature should therefore be labeled distinctly:

- **Catalog auto-selection:** chooses a model before sending a request.
- **Request-time model failover:** after an eligible inference failure, attempts the request using a different model.

The current guides explicitly state that failed Claude requests are not replayed against OpenAI and that doctor never retries another model. Those statements are in the diagnostics sections of both proxy guides and must change only if actual runtime model substitution is implemented. Doctor’s one-attempt contract can remain unchanged even if normal client traffic gains failover.

Request-time failover documentation should specify:

- eligible status/error classes;
- ordered candidates and maximum attempts;
- whether explicit model selections participate;
- whether fallback is transient or updates persisted state;
- streaming boundary—never replay after output has been committed;
- exclusion of account-wide HTTP 402 `billing_not_configured`;
- distinction from shim same-model retries and package fallback.

### Test layout and recommended split

All Copilot tests currently live in:

`/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/tests/Copilot.Tests.ps1`

Keep two separate test groups:

1. **Catalog selection tests**
   - ranking from a catalog;
   - role-profile generation;
   - offline `--auto` refusal;
   - Codex’s separate OpenAI-first ranking.

2. **Request-time failover tests**
   - precise eligible/noneligible errors;
   - deterministic candidate order;
   - bounded attempts;
   - no fallback for HTTP 402/billing;
   - no replay after stream/output commitment;
   - explicit-model behavior;
   - no unintended persisted-model mutation;
   - interaction with existing same-model retries.

The existing doctor test asserting one catalog fetch and one inference attempt should remain separate and green.

### Portable parity and validation precedents

There is no tracked Copilot model-policy fixture directory today. Existing mechanisms are:

- Optional SHA-256 equality check between Windows and Unix throttle shims in `tests/Copilot.Tests.ps1`; it skips when the sibling checkout is unavailable.
- Baked SHA-256/base64 manifest for the exact `@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0` CDN copy.
- Installed `package.json` name/version, verified stamp, dependency, and runnable-launch postconditions.
- Chezmoi content hashes in the Rime deployment script, used to retrigger `run_onchange`, not as behavioral fixtures.
- `Copilot.psd1` remains at module version `1.0.0`; this is not currently an enforced release/version check.

If Bash and PowerShell must share an identical failover policy, the clearest new mechanism is a versioned, platform-neutral JSON fixture containing catalogs, failures, expected candidate order, and expected decisions. Copy it byte-identically into both repositories and have native Pester/Bats tests consume it. An optional sibling SHA check can detect local drift, while each repository’s CI independently validates semantics.

If failover is implemented in the shared shim, both copies must remain byte-identical:

- `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-windows-dotfiles/dot_config/powershell/copilot-throttle-shim.js`
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/copilot-throttle-shim.js`

# Building LLM-Powered Applications with Claude

This skill helps you build LLM-powered applications with Claude. Choose the right surface based on your needs, detect the project language, then read the relevant language-specific documentation.

## Before You Start

Scan the target file (or, if no target file, the prompt and project) for non-Anthropic provider markers — `import openai`, `from openai`, `langchain_openai`, `OpenAI(`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-5`, file names like `agent-openai.py` or `*-generic.py`, or any explicit instruction to keep the code provider-neutral. If you find any, stop and tell the user that this skill produces Claude/Anthropic SDK code; ask whether they want to switch the file to Claude or want a non-Claude implementation. Do not edit a non-Anthropic file with Anthropic SDK calls. (Exception: the `prompt-audit` subcommand is non-interactive and does not stop here — it records non-Anthropic provider markers in its report's stated assumptions and never proposes switching a non-Anthropic file to the Anthropic SDK.)

## Output Requirement

When the user asks you to add, modify, or implement a Claude feature, your code must call Claude through one of:

1. **The official Anthropic SDK** for the project's language (`anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `com.anthropic.*`, etc.). This is the default whenever a supported SDK exists for the project.
2. **Raw HTTP** (`curl`, `requests`, `fetch`, `httpx`, etc.) — only when the user explicitly asks for cURL/REST/raw HTTP, the project is a shell/cURL project, or the language has no official SDK.

Never mix the two — don't reach for `requests`/`fetch` in a Python or TypeScript project just because it feels lighter. Never fall back to OpenAI-compatible shims.

**Never guess SDK usage.** Function names, class names, namespaces, method signatures, and import paths must come from explicit documentation — either the `{lang}/` files in this skill or the official SDK repositories or documentation links listed in `shared/live-sources.md`. If the binding you need is not explicitly documented in the skill files, WebFetch the relevant SDK repo from `shared/live-sources.md` before writing code. Do not infer Ruby/Java/Go/PHP/C# APIs from cURL shapes or from another language's SDK.

**If WebFetch or repository access fails** (network restricted, timeouts, clone blocked): do not keep retrying — write code from the patterns and namespace/package tables in the `{lang}/` file, run the compiler or interpreter on it, and iterate on the error output. For statically-typed SDKs (C#, Java, Go) a compile-fix loop against local errors reaches working code faster than blocked network research.

## Defaults

Unless the user requests otherwise:

For the Claude model version, please use Claude Opus 5, which you can access via the exact model string `claude-opus-5`. Please default to using adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) for anything remotely complicated. And finally, please default to streaming for any request that may involve long input, long output, or high `max_tokens` — it prevents hitting request timeouts. Use the SDK's `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()` helper to get the complete response if you don't need to handle individual stream events

## ⚠️ API Drift — Your Training Prior May Be Stale

Several common Claude API shapes changed in 2025–2026. If you recall a pattern from training, verify it against the `{lang}/` files in this skill before writing — the rows below are the most frequent drift points:

| Area | Stale prior | Current API |
|---|---|---|
| Extended thinking | `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | On Claude 4.6+ models: `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. `budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and **rejected with a 400** on Fable 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 / 4.8 / 4.7. Pre-4.6 models still use `budget_tokens`. |
| Web search / web fetch tool type | `web_search_20250305`, `web_fetch_20250910` | `web_search_20260209`, `web_fetch_20260209` (dynamic filtering) on Opus 5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6. Older models keep the basic variants; on Vertex AI only basic `web_search_20250305` is available (web fetch is not on Vertex) — see the Server Tools QR below. |
| PHP parameter names | snake_case wire names as named args (`max_tokens`) | Top-level named args are camelCase (`maxTokens`). Nested array keys vary by feature (e.g. `'taskBudget'`, `'skillID'`, `'mcp_server_name'`) — copy the exact key from the documented example; do not bulk-convert. |
| Managed Agents credentials | Keep secrets host-side via custom tools (the only option before vaults shipped) | Vault `environment_variable` credentials — stored by Anthropic, substituted at egress, never visible in the sandbox (`shared/managed-agents-tools.md` → Vaults). Host-side custom tools remain the fallback for self-hosted sandboxes. |

The `{lang}/` files in this skill are authoritative over recalled patterns.

### Language-Specific Feature Support

Every SDK language above supports both the beta Tool Runner and Managed Agents (beta) — Python (`@beta_tool` decorator), TypeScript (`betaZodTool` + Zod), Java (annotated classes), Go (`BetaToolRunner` in the `toolrunner` pkg), Ruby (`BaseTool` + `tool_runner`), C# (`BetaToolRunner` + raw JSON schema), PHP (`BetaRunnableTool` + `toolRunner()`); code entry points are in the Tool Use Patterns quick reference below. cURL is raw HTTP (no SDK features) and supports Managed Agents.

> **Managed Agents code examples**: see the reading guide in the `## Managed Agents (Beta)` section below.

## Which Surface Should I Use?

> **Start simple.** Default to the simplest tier that meets your needs. Single API calls and workflows handle most use cases — only reach for agents when the task genuinely requires open-ended, model-driven exploration. "Simplest" means the least code you own: for a hosted, scheduled, or memory-backed agent, Managed Agents is usually the simplest option (no loop code, no state files, no scheduler), even though it's a bigger platform.

| Use Case                                        | Tier            | Recommended Surface       | Why                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Classification, summarization, extraction, Q&A  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | One request, one response                                    |
| Batch processing or embeddings                  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | Specialized endpoints                                        |
| Multi-step pipelines with code-controlled logic | Workflow        | **Claude API + tool use** | You orchestrate the loop                                     |
| Custom agent with your own tools                | Agent           | **Claude API + tool use** | Maximum flexibility                                          |
| Server-managed stateful agent with workspace    | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Anthropic runs the loop and hosts the tool-execution sandbox |
| Persisted, versioned agent configs              | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Agents are stored objects; sessions pin to a version         |
| Long-running multi-turn agent with file mounts  | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Per-session containers, SSE event stream, Skills + MCP       |
| Agent that runs on a schedule (cron, "every night") | Agent       | **Managed Agents** — scheduled deployments | Deployments fire sessions autonomously; no client-side scheduler |

> **Note:** Managed Agents is the right choice when you want Anthropic to run the agent loop *and* host the container where tools execute — file ops, bash, code execution all run in the per-session workspace. If you want to host the compute yourself or run your own custom tool runtime, Claude API + tool use is the right choice — use the tool runner for the agentic loop — its per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, logging, error interception, and conditional execution (see `shared/tool-use-concepts.md`) — or the manual loop when you want to own the entire loop yourself.

> **Cloud-provider access.** **Claude Platform on AWS** is Anthropic-operated with same-day API parity — see `shared/claude-platform-on-aws.md` for client setup. For per-feature availability on **Claude Platform on AWS**, **Amazon Bedrock**, **Google Vertex AI**, and **Microsoft Foundry**, see `shared/platform-availability.md` — that table is the single source of truth in this skill; do not infer availability from anywhere else.

### Building an Agent: Four Approaches

Once you've decided you actually need an agent (open-ended, model-driven tool use), there are four distinct ways to build one. Two independent questions separate them: **who supplies the harness** (the agent loop + context management) and **who supplies the deployment** (the infra the agent runs on). The Tool Runner and the Claude Agent SDK both supply a *harness only* — you still host and deploy them yourself — which is why they're easy to conflate. Managed Agents (CMA) is the only option that supplies **both** the harness *and* managed deployment; the manual loop supplies neither.

| # | Approach | You write | Harness & deployment | Tools available | Use when |
|---|----------|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|----------|
| 1 | **Claude API — manual loop** | The `while stop_reason == "tool_use"` loop yourself | You build the harness; you host | Only tools you define | You want to own the *entire* loop — no beta dependency, or a control flow the Tool Runner's per-turn hooks don't fit |
| 2 | **Claude API — Tool Runner** (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner` + `@beta_tool` / `betaZodTool`) | Just the tool functions | SDK supplies the loop (**harness only**); you host | Only tools you define | A custom-tool agent without hand-writing the loop (most cases). Per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, error interception, result modification (e.g. `cache_control`), retries, streaming, and compaction |
| 3 | **Managed Agents** (REST, beta) | Agent config + your tool results | Anthropic supplies the harness **and** hosts a per-session sandbox (**harness + deployment**) | Anthropic-hosted sandbox (bash, files, code exec) + Skills/MCP + your tools | You want Anthropic to run the loop *and* host the per-session workspace; persisted/versioned configs; long-running sessions |
| 4 | **Claude Agent SDK** — *separate product* (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) | A prompt + options | SDK supplies the Claude Code harness + built-in tools (**harness only**); you host | Built-in Read/Write/Edit/Bash/Glob/Grep/WebSearch/WebFetch + MCP + subagents | You want a batteries-included coding/filesystem agent running on your own infra |

The harness/deployment split is the key mental model: options 1, 2, and 4 all **leave deployment to you**; only option 3 (CMA) adds managed deployment. Options 1–3 are what this skill generates; option 4 is a different library with its own docs — see the disambiguation below.

> **Tool Runner ≠ Claude Agent SDK.** These sound alike but are different packages:
> - **Tool Runner** is part of the regular Anthropic API SDK (`anthropic` / `@anthropic-ai/sdk`), reached via `client.beta.messages.tool_runner`. It automates the request → execute → loop cycle *for tools you define*. No built-in tools, no filesystem access, no sandbox — you supply every tool and host the compute. It is option 2 above, a thin helper over `POST /v1/messages`.
> - **Claude Agent SDK** (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) is Claude Code packaged as a library. It ships built-in tools (file read/write/edit, bash, grep, web search), the full agent loop, context management, hooks, subagents, permissions, and sessions. You call `query(prompt, options)` and it drives everything.
>
> Both are **harness-only — you host and deploy them.** The difference is scope of harness: the Tool Runner loops over tools *you* define (with per-turn hooks for approval, interception, result modification, and retries — but no built-in tools); the Agent SDK is the full Claude Code harness with built-in tools. Neither provides managed deployment — that's what **Managed Agents (CMA)** adds (Anthropic hosts the loop and a per-session sandbox).
>
> **This skill covers the Claude API and Managed Agents (options 1–3); it does not generate Claude Agent SDK code.** If the user actually wants the Claude Agent SDK, point them to its docs (`code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk`) — don't substitute the API Tool Runner for it, or vice-versa.

### Should I Build an Agent?

Before choosing the agent tier, check all four criteria:

- **Complexity** — Is the task multi-step and hard to fully specify in advance? (e.g., "turn this design doc into a PR" vs. "extract the title from this PDF")
- **Value** — Does the outcome justify higher cost and latency?
- **Viability** — Is Claude capable at this task type?
- **Cost of error** — Can errors be caught and recovered from? (tests, review, rollback)

If the answer is "no" to any of these, stay at a simpler tier (single call or workflow).

---

## Architecture

Everything goes through `POST /v1/messages`. Tools and output constraints are features of this single endpoint — not separate APIs.

**User-defined tools** — You define tools (via decorators, Zod schemas, or raw JSON), and the SDK's tool runner handles calling the API, executing your functions, and looping until Claude is done. For full control, you can write the loop manually.

**Server-side tools** — Anthropic-hosted tools that run on Anthropic's infrastructure. Code execution is fully server-side (declare it in `tools`, Claude runs code automatically). Computer use can be server-hosted or self-hosted.

**Structured outputs** — Constrains the Messages API response format (`output_config.format`) and/or tool parameter validation (`strict: true`). The recommended approach is `client.messages.parse()` which validates responses against your schema automatically. Note: the old `output_format` parameter is deprecated; use `output_config: {format: {...}}` on `messages.create()`.

**Supporting endpoints** — Batches (`POST /v1/messages/batches`), Files (`POST /v1/files`), Token Counting (`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` — see `shared/token-counting.md`), and Models (`GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{id}` — live capability/context-window discovery) feed into or support Messages API requests.
