```text
#!/usr/bin/env bun
// copilot-throttle-shim.js — a tiny streaming reverse proxy that sits IN FRONT
// of the local copilot-api fork (default :4141). It provides the request
// compatibility fixes shared by Codex/Claude Code and stops GitHub's enterprise
// Copilot backend from 403-ing ("Forbidden") on bursts of premium requests,
// WITHOUT adding latency to normal single-agent flow.
//
//   agent client ─▶ shim (:4142) ─▶ copilot-api fork (:4141) ─▶ Copilot backend
//                    │
//                    ├─ semaphore: at most MAX concurrent in-flight upstream
//                    │   POSTs; a burst queues instead of hitting the backend
//                    │   all at once (that simultaneity is what trips abuse
//                    │   detection). Under the cap there is ZERO added latency.
//                    │
//                    ├─ transparent retry on 403/429/502/503/504 + network
//                    │   errors, jittered backoff, BEFORE any response body is
//                    │   streamed — so the agent never sees the transient 403
//                    │   ("Please run /login"). GET/HEAD (health, /v1/models)
//                    │   bypass both, so liveness checks stay instant.
//                    │
//                    └─ SSE keepalive + stall watchdog: an OpenAI reasoning
//                        model produces NOTHING on the wire until its first
//                        token, and copilot-api withholds the response headers
//                        for that whole time, so the client socket can sit
//                        silent for minutes. See "silent socket" below.
//
// The silent socket (why the keepalive exists)
// --------------------------------------------
// copilot-api does not open the SSE stream early: measured against :4141 with
// gpt-5.6-sol, the response HEADERS arrive at 8.11s and the first body chunk at
// 8.12s — the think time is spent entirely inside one `fetch()` with zero bytes
// on either socket. The backend log's own p50/p90/max for that window is
// 7s/20s/89s, and queueing on the semaphore above stacks on top of it. Real
// Anthropic streams cover this with periodic `ping` events; copilot-api emits
// none (verified: message_start / content_block_* / message_delta / message_stop
// only). A silent socket is free to be reaped by anything in the path — Bun's
// own idleTimeout, a Clash/mihomo idle sweep — and the agent then hangs with no
// error at all, which is the interrupt-and-type-"continue" symptom.
//
// So for client-requested streams the shim commits a `text/event-stream`
// response after PING_AFTER_MS and emits SSE comment frames (`: …\n\n`, ignored
// by every spec-compliant parser, including the Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs)
// until the upstream produces something. Requests answered inside the grace
// window keep the old behaviour byte for byte, real status code included.
//
// Managed by copilot-proxy (see 43_copilot_proxy.sh: `copilot-proxy shim on`).
// Config via env (all optional):
//   COPILOT_SHIM_PORT       listen port                    (default 4142)
//   COPILOT_SHIM_UPSTREAM   upstream base URL              (default http://localhost:4141)
//   COPILOT_SHIM_MAX        max concurrent in-flight POSTs (default 4)
//   COPILOT_SHIM_RETRIES    retry attempts on transient    (default 3)
//   COPILOT_SHIM_BACKOFF_MS base backoff ms, doubles/try   (default 500)
//   COPILOT_SHIM_PING_MS    keepalive interval, 0=off      (default 15000)
//   COPILOT_SHIM_PING_AFTER_MS  silence tolerated before the SSE response is
//                           committed and pings start      (default 10000)
//   COPILOT_SHIM_STALL_MS   silence that counts as a wedged upstream: the
//                           attempt is aborted (retried when no bytes have
//                           reached the client yet), 0=off (default 240000)

const PORT = Number(process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_PORT ?? 4142);
const UPSTREAM = (process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_UPSTREAM ?? "http://localhost:4141").replace(/\/+$/, "");
const MAX = Math.max(1, Number(process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_MAX ?? 4));
const RETRIES = Math.max(0, Number(process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_RETRIES ?? 3));
const BACKOFF_MS = Math.max(0, Number(process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_BACKOFF_MS ?? 500));
const PING_MS = Math.max(0, Number(process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_PING_MS ?? 15000));
const PING_AFTER_MS = Math.max(0, Number(process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_PING_AFTER_MS ?? 10000));
const STALL_MS = Math.max(0, Number(process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_STALL_MS ?? 240000));
const RETRY_STATUS = new Set([403, 429, 502, 503, 504]);

// Ceiling for the keepalive path's own patience. It must outlast the WHOLE
// pipeline — every attempt's STALL_MS plus the backoffs between them — or it
// tears the client stream down mid-retry and throws away a retry that was about
// to succeed. 0 (watchdog disabled) means wait as long as the upstream does.
const GIVEUP_MS = STALL_MS ? (RETRIES + 1) * (STALL_MS + 30000) : 0;

// SSE comment frame. The spec says a line starting with ":" is a comment and is
// discarded by the parser, so this is invisible to the agent yet counts as
// traffic for every idle timer in the path.
const PING_FRAME = new TextEncoder().encode(": copilot-shim keepalive\n\n");

const log = (...a) => console.log(new Date().toISOString(), "[shim]", ...a);
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));

// A cancellable timer promise. Racing a bare `sleep()` would leave one live
// timer per pull, which on a long stream is thousands of them.
function timeoutToken(ms) {
  let id;
  const promise = new Promise((res) => { id = setTimeout(() => res({ tick: true }), ms); });
  return { promise, cancel: () => clearTimeout(id) };
}

// ---- semaphore (at most MAX permits; hands a permit straight to a waiter) ----
let active = 0;
const waiters = [];
function acquire() {
  if (active < MAX) { active++; return Promise.resolve(); }
  return new Promise((res) => waiters.push(res));
}
function release() {
  active--;
  const next = waiters.shift();
  if (next) { active++; next(); }
}

function backoffMs(attempt, retryAfter) {
  const ra = Number(retryAfter);
  if (Number.isFinite(ra) && ra > 0) return Math.min(ra * 1000, 30000);
  return BACKOFF_MS * 2 ** attempt + Math.floor(Math.random() * BACKOFF_MS); // + jitter
}

function buildUpstream(req, bodyBuf, bodyWasDecoded = false) {
  const url = new URL(req.url);
  const target = UPSTREAM + url.pathname + url.search;
  const headers = new Headers(req.headers);
  headers.delete("host");
  headers.delete("content-length"); // fetch recomputes from body
  if (bodyWasDecoded) headers.delete("content-encoding");
  const init = { method: req.method, headers, signal: req.signal };
  if (bodyBuf !== undefined) init.body = bodyBuf;
  return { target, init };
}

function blankDescription(value) {
  return typeof value !== "string" || value.trim().length === 0;
}

function toolLabel(tool) {
  const name = tool?.name ?? tool?.tool_name ?? tool?.title;
  return typeof name === "string" && name.trim() ? name.trim() : "unnamed tool";
}

// Codex records MCP discovery in Responses input items. Some MCP/plugin
// servers legally omit a tool description, which Codex serializes as "". The
// GitHub Copilot Responses endpoint is stricter than OpenAI's endpoint and
// rejects that request before inference:
//
//   Invalid 'input[0].tools[0].description': empty string.
//
// Only touch tool-definition arrays in the two Responses locations Codex uses;
// do not recursively rewrite user input, JSON Schema descriptions, or outputs.
export function normalizeResponsesToolDescriptions(payload) {
  let changed = 0;
  const patched = [];

  const normalizeTools = (tools, prefix, requireDescriptionField = false) => {
    if (!Array.isArray(tools)) return;
    tools.forEach((tool, index) => {
      if (!tool || typeof tool !== "object") return;
      if (requireDescriptionField && !("description" in tool)) return;
      if (!blankDescription(tool.description)) return;
      const label = toolLabel(tool);
      tool.description = `Tool ${label}.`;
      changed++;
      patched.push(`${prefix}[${index}].description`);
    });
  };

  if (!payload || typeof payload !== "object") return { changed, patched };
  // Built-in top-level tools such as web_search do not have a description by
  // design, so only repair an explicitly present-but-blank field there.
  normalizeTools(payload.tools, "tools", true);
  if (Array.isArray(payload.input)) {
    payload.input.forEach((item, index) => {
      // Codex versions have used more than one discriminator for persisted MCP
      // discovery. The stable shape is the nested tool-definition array itself.
      if (!item || typeof item !== "object") return;
      normalizeTools(item.tools, `input[${index}].tools`);
    });
  }
  return { changed, patched };
}

export function normalizeRequestBody(pathname, bodyBuf, contentEncoding = "") {
  if (pathname !== "/responses" && pathname !== "/v1/responses") {
    return { body: bodyBuf, changed: 0, patched: [], parseError: null, decoded: false };
  }
  try {
    const encoding = contentEncoding.trim().toLowerCase();
    const decodedBody = encoding === "zstd" ? Bun.zstdDecompressSync(new Uint8Array(bodyBuf)) : bodyBuf;
    const payload = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(decodedBody));
    const result = normalizeResponsesToolDescriptions(payload);
    if (result.changed === 0) return { body: bodyBuf, ...result, parseError: null, decoded: false };
    return { body: JSON.stringify(payload), ...result, parseError: null, decoded: encoding === "zstd" };
  } catch (error) {
    // Preserve malformed/non-JSON requests verbatim; the upstream remains the
    // authority for their validation and error response.
    return { body: bodyBuf, changed: 0, patched: [], parseError: String(error), decoded: false };
  }
}

// Did the client ask for a streamed response? Only those may be answered with
// the early `text/event-stream` commit — a non-streaming caller expects one JSON
// body and would choke on comment frames. Unparseable/compressed bodies fall
// back to `false`, i.e. to the pre-keepalive behaviour.
export function wantsStream(body) {
  try {
    const text = typeof body === "string" ? body : new TextDecoder().decode(body);
    return JSON.parse(text)?.stream === true;
  } catch { return false; }
}

// One upstream `fetch` attempt with a ceiling on the silent pre-header window.
// A wedged upstream otherwise never settles this promise and the agent waits
// forever; RETRIES then gets a chance to re-issue the request instead.
function fetchAttempt(target, init, clientSignal) {
  if (!STALL_MS) return fetch(target, { ...init, signal: clientSignal });
  const ctl = new AbortController();
  const onClientAbort = () => ctl.abort();
  if (clientSignal?.aborted) ctl.abort();
  else clientSignal?.addEventListener("abort", onClientAbort, { once: true });
  let stalled = false;
  const timer = setTimeout(() => { stalled = true; ctl.abort(); }, STALL_MS);
  const done = () => {
    clearTimeout(timer);
    clientSignal?.removeEventListener("abort", onClientAbort);
  };
  return fetch(target, { ...init, signal: ctl.signal }).then(
    (resp) => { done(); return resp; },
    (err) => {
      done();
      throw stalled ? new Error(`upstream sent no response headers in ${STALL_MS}ms`) : err;
    },
  );
}

// One `pull` step over an upstream reader: forward the next chunk, or emit a
// keepalive frame once the upstream has been silent for PING_MS, or fail the
// stream when that silence reaches STALL_MS.
//
// `state.pending` is load-bearing: when the ping timer wins the race the read
// promise is NOT abandoned, it is carried into the next pull. Re-reading would
// drop a chunk. Keeping the pull-driven shape (rather than a `start()` pump)
// preserves backpressure toward the upstream.
async function pumpStep(state, controller, releaseOnce, label) {
  if (!state.pending) state.pending = state.reader.read();

  if (!state.keepalive) {
    const { done, value } = await state.pending;
    state.pending = null;
    if (done) { controller.close(); releaseOnce(); return; }
    controller.enqueue(value);
    return;
  }

  const tick = timeoutToken(PING_MS);
  const winner = await Promise.race([state.pending.then((read) => ({ read })), tick.promise]);
  tick.cancel();

  if (winner.read) {
    state.pending = null;
    state.idleMs = 0;
    if (winner.read.done) { controller.close(); releaseOnce(); return; }
    controller.enqueue(winner.read.value);
    return;
  }

  state.idleMs += PING_MS;
  if (STALL_MS && state.idleMs >= STALL_MS) {
    const secs = Math.round(state.idleMs / 1000);
    log(`${label} stalled mid-stream: no upstream bytes for ${secs}s; failing the response`);
    try { state.reader.cancel(new Error("stalled")); } catch {}
    releaseOnce();
    controller.error(new Error(`shim: upstream stalled for ${secs}s`));
    return;
  }
  controller.enqueue(PING_FRAME);
}

// Stream an upstream response to the client, holding the semaphore permit until
// the stream ends / errors / is cancelled (true in-flight accounting).
function streamThrough(resp, releaseOnce, label = "stream") {
  const headers = new Headers(resp.headers);
  headers.delete("content-encoding");  // Bun already decoded the upstream body
  headers.delete("content-length");
  headers.delete("transfer-encoding");
  if (!resp.body) { releaseOnce(); return new Response(null, { status: resp.status, headers }); }

  const state = {
    reader: resp.body.getReader(),
    pending: null,
    idleMs: 0,
    // Only an SSE body may carry comment frames; a JSON body must stay verbatim.
    keepalive: PING_MS > 0 && (headers.get("content-type") ?? "").includes("text/event-stream"),
  };
  const stream = new ReadableStream({
    async pull(controller) {
      try { await pumpStep(state, controller, releaseOnce, label); }
      catch (err) { releaseOnce(); controller.error(err); }
    },
    cancel(reason) { releaseOnce(); try { state.reader.cancel(reason); } catch {} },
  });
  return new Response(stream, { status: resp.status, headers });
}

// The upstream committed a non-2xx AFTER the shim already promised the client a
// 200 SSE stream, so the status line is spent. Both the Anthropic and the
// OpenAI streaming protocols carry failures as an `error` event, which their
// SDKs surface as a normal API error — that is the only channel left here.
async function sseErrorFrame(resp, err) {
  let detail = err ? String(err) : `upstream returned ${resp.status}`;
  if (resp && !err) {
    try { detail = `upstream returned ${resp.status}: ${(await resp.text()).slice(0, 500)}`; } catch {}
  }
  const payload = JSON.stringify({ type: "error", error: { type: "api_error", message: `shim: ${detail}` } });
  return new TextEncoder().encode(`event: error\ndata: ${payload}\n\n`);
}

// Slow path body: ping until `pipeline` (queueing + retries + upstream headers)
// settles, then forward the real stream through the same pump.
function keepaliveThenForward(pipeline, releaseOnce, label) {
  const state = { reader: null, pending: null, idleMs: 0, keepalive: true };
  let settled = false;
  return new ReadableStream({
    async pull(controller) {
      try {
        if (!settled) {
          const tick = timeoutToken(PING_MS);
          const winner = await Promise.race([
            pipeline.then((resp) => ({ resp }), (err) => ({ err })),
            tick.promise,
          ]);
          tick.cancel();

          if (winner.tick) {
            state.idleMs += PING_MS;
            if (GIVEUP_MS && state.idleMs >= GIVEUP_MS) {
              // fetchAttempt bounds each attempt, so reaching this means the
              // pipeline itself is wedged past its whole retry budget.
              const secs = Math.round(state.idleMs / 1000);
              log(`${label} gave up after ${secs}s without upstream headers`);
              settled = true;
              pipeline.then((resp) => resp?.body?.cancel()).catch(() => {});
              controller.enqueue(await sseErrorFrame(null, `no upstream response in ${secs}s`));
              controller.close();
              releaseOnce();
              return;
            }
            controller.enqueue(PING_FRAME);
            return;
          }

          settled = true;
          state.idleMs = 0;
          const { resp, err } = winner;
          if (err || !resp.ok || !resp.body) {
            log(`${label} committed as SSE but upstream answered ${err ? `error (${err})` : resp.status}`);
            controller.enqueue(await sseErrorFrame(err ? null : resp, err));
            controller.close();
            releaseOnce();
            return;
          }
          state.reader = resp.body.getReader();
        }
        await pumpStep(state, controller, releaseOnce, label);
      } catch (err) { releaseOnce(); controller.error(err); }
    },
    cancel(reason) {
      releaseOnce();
      try { state.reader?.cancel(reason); } catch {}
      pipeline.then((resp) => resp?.body?.cancel(reason)).catch(() => {});
    },
  });
}

export function startServer() {
  const server = Bun.serve({
    port: PORT,
    // Seconds; 255 is Bun's ceiling. With PING_MS keepalives the client socket
    // no longer goes quiet for anywhere near this long, but leave the headroom:
    // it is the last line of defence when pings are disabled.
    idleTimeout: 255,
    async fetch(req) {
    const url = new URL(req.url);
    const method = req.method;

    // Health / metadata reads: straight passthrough, no permit, no retry.
    if (method === "GET" || method === "HEAD") {
      try {
        const { target, init } = buildUpstream(req, undefined);
        return streamThrough(await fetch(target, init), () => {});
      } catch (err) {
        return new Response(`shim: upstream unreachable: ${err}`, { status: 502 });
      }
    }

    // Mutating requests (POST /v1/messages …): buffer body so we can resend on
    // retry, then throttle + retry.
    const bodyBuf = await req.arrayBuffer();
    const normalized = normalizeRequestBody(url.pathname, bodyBuf, req.headers.get("content-encoding") ?? "");
    if (normalized.parseError) {
      log(`${method} ${url.pathname} could not inspect JSON (${bodyBuf.byteLength} bytes, content-type=${req.headers.get("content-type") ?? "unset"}, content-encoding=${req.headers.get("content-encoding") ?? "unset"}): ${normalized.parseError}`);
    }
    if (normalized.changed > 0) {
      log(`${method} ${url.pathname} filled ${normalized.changed} empty tool description(s): ${normalized.patched.join(", ")}`);
    }
    const { target, init } = buildUpstream(req, normalized.body, normalized.decoded);

    const label = `${method} ${url.pathname}`;
    // The permit is now taken INSIDE the pipeline: queue time is silent time on
    // the client socket too, so the keepalive below has to be able to cover it.
    let acquired = false;
    let released = false;
    const releaseOnce = () => { if (acquired && !released) { released = true; release(); } };

    // Queue for a permit, then talk to the upstream until a response is
    // committed. Resolves to a Response whose body has NOT been read yet, or to
    // a synthetic error Response (permit already released in that case).
    const runUpstream = async () => {
      const willQueue = active >= MAX;
      await acquire();
      acquired = true;
      if (willQueue) log(`queued ${label} (${active} in-flight, ${waiters.length} waiting)`);

      for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= RETRIES; attempt++) {
        let resp;
        try {
          resp = await fetchAttempt(target, init, req.signal);
        } catch (err) {
          if (req.signal?.aborted) { releaseOnce(); return new Response("client aborted", { status: 499 }); }
          if (attempt < RETRIES) {
            const d = backoffMs(attempt);
            log(`${label} network error (${err}); retry ${attempt + 1}/${RETRIES} in ${d}ms`);
            await sleep(d);
            continue;
          }
          releaseOnce();
          return new Response(`shim: upstream unreachable: ${err}`, { status: 502 });
        }

        // Retryable status and attempts left → back off and try again. The 403
        // arrives fast (<2s, before any body), so retrying here is safe.
        if (RETRY_STATUS.has(resp.status) && attempt < RETRIES) {
          const d = backoffMs(attempt, resp.headers.get("retry-after"));
          log(`${label} -> ${resp.status}; retry ${attempt + 1}/${RETRIES} in ${d}ms`);
          try { await resp.body?.cancel(); } catch {}
          await sleep(d);
          continue;
        }

        if (attempt > 0) log(`${label} -> ${resp.status} after ${attempt} retr${attempt === 1 ? "y" : "ies"}`);
        return resp;
      }
      releaseOnce(); // unreachable (last attempt always commits) — safety net
      return new Response("shim: retries exhausted", { status: 502 });
    };

    const pipeline = runUpstream();

    // Non-streaming callers keep the original shape: one await, real status.
    const eligible = PING_MS > 0 && PING_AFTER_MS > 0 && wantsStream(normalized.body);
    if (!eligible) {
      try { return streamThrough(await pipeline, releaseOnce, label); }
      catch (err) { releaseOnce(); return new Response(`shim: ${err}`, { status: 500 }); }
    }

    // Fast path — upstream answered inside the grace window, so nothing about
    // this request changes: real status, real headers, no injected frames.
    const grace = timeoutToken(PING_AFTER_MS);
    const early = await Promise.race([
      pipeline.then((resp) => ({ resp }), (err) => ({ err })),
      grace.promise,
    ]);
    grace.cancel();
    if (early.err) { releaseOnce(); return new Response(`shim: ${early.err}`, { status: 500 }); }
    if (early.resp) return streamThrough(early.resp, releaseOnce, label);

    // Slow path — still queued, or the model is still thinking. Commit the SSE
    // response now and start the heartbeat; the real stream is spliced in
    // underneath once the pipeline settles.
    log(`${label} silent for ${PING_AFTER_MS}ms; committing SSE early and sending keepalives`);
    return new Response(keepaliveThenForward(pipeline, releaseOnce, label), {
      status: 200,
      headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream", "cache-control": "no-cache", connection: "keep-alive" },
    });
    },
  });

  log(`listening on :${server.port} -> ${UPSTREAM} (max=${MAX}, retries=${RETRIES}, backoff=${BACKOFF_MS}ms, ping=${PING_MS}ms after ${PING_AFTER_MS}ms, stall=${STALL_MS}ms)`);
  return server;
}

The model is **key-level pull-through**: the baseline owns a fixed set of `section.key` pairs and every other live key is carried over untouched — the inverse of the parent repo's allowlist, which would silently drop `[otel]` and future corp sections. Two hard rules: `core.hooksPath` is **never** emitted (git honours it *instead of* `.git/hooks/`, silently disarming `pre-commit`), and the carry dictionary is **case-sensitive** (`[ordered]@{}` collapses `azrepos:org/O365Exchange` into `azrepos:org/o365exchange`, merging two credential contexts).
58	- **Docs** — bilingual mkdocs-material (`docs/X.md` + `docs/X.zh-TW.md`), deployed to GitHub Pages by `.github/workflows/docs.yml`. `docs/rationale.md` records the design choices (scoop > Chocolatey, starship > oh-my-posh, pwsh > cmd, native pwsh tree > ported shell layer).
59	- **CI** — `.github/workflows/windows.yml` on `windows-latest` is the real gate: PSScriptAnalyzer, non-interactive `chezmoi init --apply`, render+parse of every `.ps1.tmpl`, and Pester.
60	
61	## Conventions & hard invariants
62	
63	1. **A new/renamed init prompt must update the CI flags in the same commit.** `chezmoi init --promptBool/--promptChoice "<text>=value"` matches the prompt's exact TEXT (3rd arg to `promptXOnce` in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`), used non-interactively by `.github/workflows/windows.yml`. Forget it → CI's init hangs/EOFs (`error calling promptChoiceOnce: EOF`; this broke three consecutive pushes when `agentSounds` was added). Corollary: **never put `=` in a prompt's text** — the `name=value` parser splits on the first `=` (this broke the `role` prompt once). Enforced by `tests/InitPrompts.Tests.ps1` (missing flag, stale flag, wrong flag kind, `=` in text), which CI runs *before* `chezmoi init` so the failure names the missing flag instead of EOF-ing — run `Invoke-Pester -Path ./tests/InitPrompts.Tests.ps1` locally after touching either file.
64	2. **Run-scripts must never abort the apply.** The installer + editor/terminal/backup/skill scripts use `$ErrorActionPreference='Continue'` (+ `PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference=$false`), collect failures via `Register-Failure`, print a summary, and exit 0. One bad scoop/winget manifest (e.g. btop's stale `.conf`) must not stop the rest.
65	3. **Preserve raw escapes when authoring config with control chars.** Alacritty CSI-u (`[…u`), VSCode `sendSequence`, tv `\t` — hand-typing tends to drop them. Generate via a throwaway Python script and re-parse (`tomllib` / `json`) to confirm the escape landed.
66	4. **tv channel commands are `pwsh -NoProfile -Command "…"` inside TOML literal (`'''…'''`) strings** — runs regardless of tv's shell, sidesteps nested-quote escaping; placeholders `{split: :0}` (space) / `{split:\t:0}` (tab). tv reads config from `%APPDATA%\television\` on Windows.
67	5. **Editors use a run_onchange pwsh merger, not `modify_`** (`modify_` interpreter selection is unreliable on Windows). Overlay sources live in `editors/` (chezmoi-ignored, embedded via `{{ include }}`).
68	6. **The agent skill body lives once** in `.chezmoitemplates/dotfiles-windows-skill.md`; both `dot_agents/skills/dotfiles-windows/SKILL.md.tmpl` and `dot_claude/skills/dotfiles-windows/SKILL.md.tmpl` render it via `{{ "{{" }} template … {{ "}}" }}` → real files at `~/.agents/skills/` and `~/.claude/skills/`. Edit the shared template, not the two one-line renderers (no symlink/junction — those need elevation/Developer Mode on Windows).
69	7. **PSScriptAnalyzer exclusions are intentional** (`PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1`): hyphenated command names, `Write-Host`, `Invoke-Expression` for tool init, no-BOM UTF-8. Don't "fix" these; do fix real Errors.
70	
71	### Cross-file mirrors (same commit)
72	
73	- New installer tool → `docs/tools.md` **and** `docs/tools.zh-TW.md`.
74	- New init prompt → `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` + `windows.yml` flags + `docs/setup.md`/`setup.zh-TW.md` tables + the "What's enabled" block in `.chezmoitemplates/dotfiles-windows-skill.md`.
75	- New `docs/**/*.md` → its `.zh-TW.md` twin + `nav` + `nav_translations` in `mkdocs.yml`; `just docs-build` must stay green.
76	- Any edit under `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` → copy the file verbatim into the parent repo's `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` (`chezmoi source-path` there, usually `~/.local/share/chezmoi`). They must stay byte-identical; verify with `diff -r`. Frontend-only changes (`weasel.custom.yaml`) do **not** cross over.
77	- `core.autocrlf = input` has **two writers** — `bootstrap.ps1` (runs before chezmoi exists, so scoop's first bucket clone is protected) and `.chezmoitemplates/git/gitconfig` (the managed baseline). Change one → change the other.
78	
79	### `scripts/*.sh` are wrappers, not implementations
80	
81	`scripts/{add-todo,todo-kanban,promote-todo,sweep-inbox}.sh` are byte-identical
82	three-line shims. The real code is vendored at
83	`.agents/skills/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/<same-name>.sh`, and each
84	wrapper derives its target from `$0`, so adding a new helper only needs a copy
85	of an existing wrapper under the new name.
86	
87	They exist because the skill documents its helpers with cwd-relative paths
88	(`scripts/add-todo.sh`) and that prose was copied verbatim into the guidance
89	block below — where `scripts/` means *this* directory. Fixing the prose instead
90	would not survive, because `project-knowledge-harness` regenerates everything
91	between its sentinel markers. **This note is deliberately above the opening
92	sentinel so regeneration cannot erase it.**
93	
94	Not symlinks — invariant 6 (symlinks/junctions need elevation or Developer
95	Mode on Windows).
96	
97	<!-- project-knowledge-harness:agent-guidance -->
98	<!-- Snippet for the project's agent contract file (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md /
99	     similar). The bundled scripts/init.sh appends this between sentinel
100	     markers; safe to re-run. -->
101	
102	### Long-term backlog → `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
103	
104	When the user surfaces an idea explicitly **not** being implemented this
105	session (signals: "maybe later", "nice to have", "if I'm interested",
106	"工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來"), add an entry to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using
107	the priority + effort tag schema. Do **not** create new `ROADMAP.md` /
108	`IDEAS.md` / `BACKLOG.md` files — `TODO.md` is the single index.
109	
110	The bundled `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` validates the format. Run it
111	(`scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only TODO.md`) after editing so syntax
112	drift is caught immediately.
113	
114	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
115	
116	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
117	
118	   ```
119	   scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
120	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
121	   ```
122	
123	   Inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane and
124	   re-runs the validator. Add `--backlog` to also scaffold
125	   `backlog/<slug>.md` from the bundled template.
126	
127	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
128	
129	   ```
130	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
131	   ```
132	
133	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox", run
134	   `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`. It prompts for the missing fields per loose
135	   line and calls `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs
136	   that only formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
137	
138	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh; run
139	   `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only` afterwards.
140	
141	Add a `backlog/<slug>.md` companion doc when the item meets any of:
142	
143	- carries a `P?` tag (record what was tried so it doesn't need re-investigation)
144	- captures a paused troubleshooting session that you intend to fix later
145	  (preserve the error trace + root cause analysis before context evaporates)
146	- weighs multiple options (record trade-offs, not only the winner)
147	- is `[L]` or `[XL]` (architectural; needs design before code)
148	
149	`[S]` items rarely need a backlog doc — a file path in the `TODO.md` line is
150	usually enough. See [`backlog/README.md`](backlog/README.md) for the full
151	template and "when to add a doc" rules.
152	
153	When implementing a `TODO.md` item, in the same commit:
154	
155	1. Run `scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<what shipped>"`
156	   to move the entry into `## Done` with the dated syntax and re-validate.
157	2. Mark the corresponding `backlog/<slug>.md` (if any) `Status: shipped`
158	   and keep it as a historical record (don't delete — future-you may
159	   revisit adjacent decisions).
160	
161	`backlog/` is excluded from chezmoi (see .chezmoiignore); it
162	is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.
163	
164	### Past pitfalls → `pitfalls/`
165	
166	When you spend more than ~15 minutes debugging something that wasn't
167	googleable and the fix is non-obvious, write a `pitfalls/<slug>.md`
168	capturing:
169	
170	1. **Verbatim symptom** — copy-paste error messages exactly, do not
171	   paraphrase (preserves grep-ability for future-you / future agent)
172	2. **Root cause** — why this happens (with source / docs / upstream issue link)
173	3. **Workaround** — copy-pasteable commands or config diff
174	4. **Prevention** — how to avoid stepping on this again
175	
176	Title the doc by the **symptom**, not the root cause (you'll search by what
177	you're seeing, not by what you eventually learned). See
178	[`pitfalls/README.md`](pitfalls/README.md) for the full template and
179	when-to-add rules.
180	
181	**Pitfall vs Hard invariant**: a pitfall *graduates* to a Hard invariant in
182	this file when it (a) recurs across machines/agents/sessions despite being
183	documented, (b) silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround is non-obvious
184	enough that "remember to do X" isn't safe. When graduating, leave the
185	`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the new
186	invariant.
187	
188	`pitfalls/` is excluded from chezmoi (see .chezmoiignore) and
189	**not** auto-redacted; review for secrets before committing.
190	<!-- project-knowledge-harness:agent-guidance --> (end)

- A valid main model can receive a disabled or picker-hidden role alias.

- Current `@jeffreycao/copilot-api` reduces the immediate exposure by prefiltering disabled and picker-hidden chat models, but it deliberately retains embeddings. Defensive filtering is still needed.

### 2. Smallest reusable PowerShell helper design

Keep `Get-CopilotCatalogIds` as the **raw diagnostic/metadata view**. Add one separate catalog-view helper, conceptually:

```powershell
function script:Get-CopilotSelectableModelIds {
    param($Catalog)

    @($Catalog.data | Where-Object {
        ($_.policy.state -ne 'disabled') -and
        ($_.model_picker_enabled -ne $false) -and
        ($_.capabilities.type -ne 'embeddings')
    } | ForEach-Object { $_.id } | Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object -Unique)
}
```

Use it for:

1. Both automatic pickers.
2. Automatically derived Claude role aliases.
3. Preferably `copilot-model -l`, fzf, and persistent explicit model validation.

Keep the full catalog for `ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel`, because context metadata lookup should not be coupled to picker filtering.

Recommended behavior:

| Path | Catalog view |
|---|---|
| Status, doctor inventory, alias validation | Raw |
| Context-window lookup | Raw |
| Claude `--auto` | Selectable |
| Codex auto | Selectable |
| Automatically chosen role aliases | Selectable |
| `copilot-model -l` / fzf | Selectable |
| Offline static manual list | Existing fallback |
| Explicit Codex `-m` | Preserve current user override |

For selector reuse, extract one within-family selector and let the two public selectors differ only in family order:

- Claude Code: Claude → OpenAI → Gemini → other
- Codex: OpenAI → Claude → Gemini → other

That centralizes known model lists and future fallback policy instead of duplicating them in `Select-CopilotBestModel` and `Select-CopilotBestCodexModel`.

### 3. Exact future-model ordering drift

The current PowerShell Claude picker intentionally splits known flagship and lightweight OpenAI tiers:

- Known flagship/coding models
- Unknown non-lightweight future `gpt-*`
- Known Luna/mini models

See `Copilot.psm1:1959-1970`.

The Unix Claude picker places all known OpenAI tiers, including Luna/mini, before unknown GPTs at `43_copilot_proxy.sh:1951-1967`.

| Catalog vector | PowerShell Claude | Unix Claude | Both Codex pickers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gpt-5.7`, `gpt-5.6-luna` | `gpt-5.7` | `gpt-5.6-luna` | `gpt-5.6-luna` |
| `gpt-5.7`, `gpt-5.4-mini` | `gpt-5.7` | `gpt-5.4-mini` | `gpt-5.4-mini` |
| `gpt-5.7`, `gpt-5.5` | `gpt-5.5` | `gpt-5.5` | `gpt-5.5` |

This policy must be decided before deduplicating the selectors:

- If Unix is normative, move PowerShell Luna/mini into the first known OpenAI list.
- If capability-tier intent is normative, update Unix instead and preserve the distinction explicitly.

Additional future-order behavior shared by both implementations:

- Every named current Claude model—including Haiku 4.5—beats every unknown future Claude ID. Thus `{claude-opus-6, claude-haiku-4-5}` selects Haiku.
- Unknown fallbacks use lexical sorting, not version ordering. Thus `{gpt-5.10, gpt-5.9}` selects `gpt-5.9`.
- Among unknown Claude families, lexical family spelling can beat capability tier.

These behaviors should be locked or deliberately changed with tests rather than left implicit.

### 4. `[1m]` conversion is correct live, but profiles lose offline hints

The normal live conversion matches the gateway:

- `>= 1,000,000` adds `[1m]`
- Lower context removes a stale hint
- Offline conversion preserves an explicitly supplied hint
- Offline conversion does not invent one

See `Copilot.psm1:883-899`.

The profile builder undermines the offline-preservation contract:

```powershell
$raw = Remove-CopilotContextHint $Model
$fableRaw = $raw
$opusRaw = $raw
$sonnetRaw = $raw
$haikuRaw = $raw
```

Therefore an offline profile for `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]` becomes approximately:

- Main: `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]`
- Fable/Opus/Sonnet/Haiku fallback: `gpt-5.6-sol`

The Unix reference has the same issue at `43_copilot_proxy.sh:1982-2031`.

This is visible when:

- `copilot-here on` writes while the proxy is down.
- `copilot-model -c` computes a global profile offline.
- Drift checking runs offline.

`copilot-run` normally auto-starts the proxy first, so it usually repairs the profile from live metadata.

Smallest correction: initialize every fallback role from the normalized `$main`, not suffix-stripped `$raw`; only replace a role when an eligible family-specific candidate is found.

There is also inconsistent manual suffix handling:

- Explicit selection re-appends `[1m]` without consulting live metadata at `Copilot.psm1:2062-2074`.
- A local pin then passes through profile conversion and may remove that hint.
- A global state file stores the explicit hint, while later live environment injection may remove it.

The cleanest contract is metadata-authoritative while live, manual-hint-preserving only offline. Route every branch through `ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel` rather than manually appending the suffix.

PowerShell also casts context directly to `[long]`; malformed nonnumeric metadata can throw. Unix guards nonnumeric values and returns the raw ID.

1713	function codex-copilot-once {
1714	    [CmdletBinding()]
1715	    param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argv)
1716	    codex-copilot @Argv
1717	}
1718	
1719	# --- specstory `-c` passthrough (why the base command must come from config) ---
1720	#
1721	# specstory's `-c/--command` REPLACES the provider's configured command — it does
1722	# NOT append to it. The shipped config says as much: "Use of these is equivalent
1723	# to -c \"custom command\"" — same slot, last write wins. So a hardcoded
1724	# `-c "claude $args"` silently drops every flag in `claude_cmd` the moment
1725	# claude-copilot has args to pass through, which made these two disagree:
1726	#
1727	#   claude-copilot-once             -> bypass-permissions  (no -c branch)
1728	#   claude-copilot-once --resume X  -> ~/.claude defaultMode "auto"
1729	#
1730	# Deriving the base command from the config keeps specstory the single source of
1731	# truth for BOTH branches. `--no-specstory` deliberately does NOT inherit it.
1732	
1733	# Effective `claude_cmd`, honouring specstory's own precedence:
1734	#   project ./.specstory/cli/config.toml > user ~/.specstory/cli/config.toml > `claude`
1735	# Matches UNCOMMENTED assignments only — both shipped configs carry a commented
1736	# `# claude_cmd = "claude"` example, and matching that would re-introduce the very
1737	# bug this exists to fix. Handles TOML's double- and single-quoted strings.
1738	function script:Get-SpecstoryClaudeCmd {
1739	    foreach ($f in '.specstory/cli/config.toml', (Join-Path $HOME '.specstory/cli/config.toml')) {
1740	        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $f)) { continue }
1741	        foreach ($line in (Get-Content -LiteralPath $f -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
1742	            if ($line -match '^\s*claude_cmd\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|''([^'']*)'')') {
1743	                $v = if ($Matches[1]) { $Matches[1] } else { $Matches[2] }
1744	                if ($v) { return $v }
1745	            }
1746	        }
1747	    }
1748	    'claude'
1749	}
1750	
1751	# Single-quote ONE argument for embedding in specstory's `-c` command STRING.
1752	# specstory shell-splits that string honouring quotes, so quoting is both possible
1753	# and necessary — an unquoted join flattens `-p "two words"` into two arguments.
1754	# POSIX escape for an embedded quote: close, \', reopen.
1755	function script:ConvertTo-CopilotShQuote {
1756	    param([string] $Value)
1757	    "'" + ($Value -replace "'", "'\''") + "'"
1758	}
1759	
1760	# --------------------------------------------------------- claude-copilot -----
1761	function claude-copilot {
1762	    [CmdletBinding()]
1763	    param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argv)
1764	    $ss = 'auto'
1765	    if ($Argv -and $Argv[0] -eq '--no-specstory') { $ss = 'never'; $Argv = $Argv[1..($Argv.Count - 1)] }
1766	    elseif ($Argv -and $Argv[0] -eq '--specstory') { $Argv = $Argv[1..($Argv.Count - 1)] }
1767	    elseif ($Argv -and $Argv[0] -in '-h', '--help') {
1768	        Write-Host "Usage: claude-copilot [--no-specstory] [claude args...]"
1769	        Write-Host "  One-off Claude Code session on the Copilot proxy. Sticky: copilot-here on"
1770	        Write-Host "  Runs claude with --dangerously-skip-permissions (hands-off proxy flow)."
1771	        return
1772	    }
1773	    if ($ss -eq 'auto' -and (Get-Command specstory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
1774	        if ($Argv -and $Argv.Count -gt 0) {
1775	            # Rebuild what `-c` clobbers: the configured base command (ITS flags left
1776	            # unquoted so specstory splits them normally) + each of our args quoted.
1777	            $cc = Get-SpecstoryClaudeCmd
1778	            foreach ($a in $Argv) { $cc = "$cc $(ConvertTo-CopilotShQuote $a)" }
1779	            copilot-run specstory run claude -c $cc
1780	        }
1781	        else { copilot-run specstory run claude }
1782	    } else {
1783	        # No specstory on PATH (the Windows default — no native CLI yet): run claude
1784	        # directly, still bypassing permission prompts so behaviour matches the
1785	        # specstory path regardless of whether specstory is installed.
1786	        copilot-run claude --dangerously-skip-permissions @Argv
1787	    }
1788	}
1789	
1790	# --------------------------------------------------- claude-copilot-once ------
1791	function claude-copilot-once {
1792	    [CmdletBinding()]
1793	    param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argv)
1794	    if ($Argv -and $Argv[0] -in '-h', '--help') {
1795	        Write-Host "Usage: claude-copilot-once [--no-specstory] [claude args...]"
1796	        Write-Host "  Pin this project to the proxy, run one session, auto-unpin (even on Ctrl-C)."
1797	        return
1798	    }
1799	    if (-not (Test-CopilotAlive)) {
1800	        Write-Error "claude-copilot-once: proxy not reachable on port $(Get-CopilotPort). Start it: copilot-proxy start"; return
1801	    }
1802	    $wasOn = $false
1803	    if (Test-Path '.claude/settings.local.json') {
1804	        try { if ((Get-Content -Raw '.claude/settings.local.json' | ConvertFrom-Json).env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL) { $wasOn = $true } } catch { $null = $_ }
1805	    }
1806	    if (-not $wasOn) { copilot-here on }
1807	    else {
1808	        # Already pinned here. If the pin drifted from current defaults (model bump,
1809	        # proxy moved, a key added since), offer to refresh it in place; otherwise
1810	        # leave it untouched. Either way it was already ON, so it stays ON on exit.
1811	        $drift = Get-CopilotHereDrift
1812	        if ($drift) {
1813	            Write-Host "claude-copilot-once: this project's copilot-here pin looks stale:"
1814	            $drift | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }
1815	            if (Confirm-CopilotAction '  override with current defaults? (keep = default) [y/N]') { copilot-here on }
1816	            else { Write-Host 'claude-copilot-once: kept the existing pin (stays ON on exit).' }
1817	        } else {
1818	            Write-Host "claude-copilot-once: copilot-here already ON here — leaving the pin in place on exit."
1819	        }
1820	    }
1821	    try {
1822	        claude-copilot @Argv
1823	    } finally {
1824	        if (-not $wasOn) { copilot-here off }
1825	        Write-Host "claude-copilot-once: session ended. Proxy still running on $(Get-CopilotBase)."
1826	    }
1827	}
1828	
1829	# ------------------------------------------------------------ copilot-here ----
1830	$script:CopilotHereKeys = @(
1831	    'ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL', 'ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN', 'ANTHROPIC_MODEL', 'ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL', 'ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL',
1832	    'ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL', 'ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL', 'ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL',
1833	    'CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC', 'CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER',
1834	    'CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION', 'CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AWAY_SUMMARY', 'DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS'
1835	)
1836	
1837	# y/N prompt. Returns $true only on an explicit yes; a non-interactive host
1838	# returns $false — the safe default (keep, don't override). Only called right
1839	# before launching an interactive Claude Code session, so reading input is fine.
1840	function script:Confirm-CopilotAction {
1841	    param([string] $Message = 'Proceed? [y/N]')
1842	    if (-not [Environment]::UserInteractive -or [Console]::IsInputRedirected) { return $false }
1843	    $ans = Read-Host -Prompt $Message
1844	    $ans -match '^\s*y(es)?\s*$'
1845	}
1846	
1847	# Has THIS project's copilot-here pin drifted from what `copilot-here on` would
1848	# write now (default model bumped, proxy moved, a key added since the pin was
1849	# written)? Returns one "  KEY : old -> new" line per drifted key, or nothing.
1850	#
1851	# Drift is defined as "the set of keys `copilot-here on` would actually CHANGE",
1852	# computed by diffing the live file against Get-CopilotEnvBlock — not a hand-picked
1853	# subset (that is how three keys silently went unchecked). The asymmetry is
1854	# deliberate: keys present in the file but absent from the want-set are NOT drift,
1855	# because `on` merges and never removes them (only `off` does).
1856	function script:Get-CopilotHereDrift {
1857	    $settings = '.claude/settings.local.json'
1858	    if (-not (Test-Path $settings)) { return @() }
1859	    try { $obj = Get-Content -Raw $settings | ConvertFrom-Json } catch { return @() }
1860	    # ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is only set while the pin is ON — absent -> nothing to do.
1861	    if (-not $obj.env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL) { return @() }
1862	
1863	    $want = Get-CopilotEnvBlock -Pinned
1864	    $out = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
1865	    foreach ($k in $want.Keys) {
1866	        $cur = if ($obj.env.PSObject.Properties[$k]) { $obj.env.$k } else { '(unset)' }
1867	        if ($cur -ne $want[$k]) { $out.Add("  $k : $cur -> $($want[$k])") }
1868	    }
1869	    $out
1870	}
1871	
1872	function copilot-here {
1873	    [CmdletBinding()]
1874	    param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argv)
1875	    $settings = '.claude/settings.local.json'
1876	    $action = if ($Argv -and $Argv.Count -ge 1) { $Argv[0] } else { 'status' }
1877	    switch ($action) {
1878	        'on' {
1879	            New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path '.claude' | Out-Null
1880	            $obj = if (Test-Path $settings) { try { Get-Content -Raw $settings | ConvertFrom-Json } catch { [pscustomobject]@{} } } else { [pscustomobject]@{} }
1881	            if (-not $obj.PSObject.Properties['env']) { $obj | Add-Member -NotePropertyName env -NotePropertyValue ([pscustomobject]@{}) }
1882	            # Single source of truth, shared with copilot-run and the drift check.
1883	            $envSet = Get-CopilotEnvBlock -Pinned
1884	            $model = $envSet.ANTHROPIC_MODEL
1885	            foreach ($k in $envSet.Keys) {
1886	                if ($obj.env.PSObject.Properties[$k]) { $obj.env.$k = $envSet[$k] }
1887	                else { $obj.env | Add-Member -NotePropertyName $k -NotePropertyValue $envSet[$k] }
1888	            }
1889	            $obj | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 | Set-Content -Path $settings -Encoding utf8
1890	            # Belt-and-braces gitignore via .git/info/exclude (un-anchored **/ form).
1891	            $gitDir = git rev-parse --git-dir 2>$null
1892	            if ($gitDir) {
1893	                git check-ignore -q $settings 2>$null
1894	                if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
1895	                    $exclude = Join-Path $gitDir 'info/exclude'
1896	                    Add-Content -Path $exclude -Value '**/.claude/settings.local.json'
1897	                }
1898	            }
1899	            Write-Host "copilot-here: ON — $settings pins Claude Code to $(Get-CopilotBase) (model: $model)"

```text
1	# copilot-proxy
2	
3	A native PowerShell port of the `copilot-proxy` tool series. It runs the
4	[`@jeffreycao/copilot-api`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@jeffreycao/copilot-api)
5	fork so a **GitHub Copilot subscription** can back **Claude Code** and other
6	Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible clients.
7	
8	The module is deployed to `~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot` and imported by
9	the PowerShell profile. It requires Bun, Node/npm and a Copilot subscription.
10	
11	## Commands
12	
13	| Command | What it does |
14	|---|---|
15	| `copilot-proxy auth` | one-time GitHub device login (`copilot-api auth login --provider copilot`; stores but does not display the token) |
16	| `copilot-proxy start` / `stop` / `restart` | manage the local proxy (port 4141) |
17	| `copilot-proxy status` | show raw served count and Claude availability |
18	| `copilot-proxy doctor [--live]` | diagnose package, auth, proxy, catalog, roles, upstream and Codex Apps |
19	| `copilot-proxy logs [N]` | tail the proxy log |
20	| `copilot-proxy shim [on\|off]` | toggle the throttle shim (port 4142) |
21	| `copilot-proxy whoami` | account / plan / quota |
22	| `copilot-proxy reinstall` | wipe and reinstall the pinned package |
23	| `copilot-run <cmd...>` | run a command with the proxy env injected |
24	| `claude-copilot` | one-off Claude Code session on the proxy |
25	| `claude-copilot-once` | pin this project, run once, then restore it |
26	| `codex-copilot` / `codex-copilot-once` | zero-persistence Codex session on the Responses proxy |
27	| `copilot-here [on\|off\|status]` | sticky project pin in `.claude/settings.local.json` |
28	| `copilot-model [<id>\|-l\|-c\|--auto]` | switch or inspect the complete role profile |
29	| `copilot-embed [TEXT\|-]` | embed text through `/v1/embeddings` |
30	| `semsearch index \| <QUERY>` | semantic search over local text |
31	
32	## Quick start
33	
34	```powershell
35	copilot-proxy auth                 # once
36	copilot-proxy start
37	copilot-model --auto              # select from the live catalog
38	copilot-model -c                   # inspect Main/Fable/Opus/Sonnet/Haiku
39	copilot-here on                    # sticky project; or use claude-copilot-once
40	codex-copilot                     # Codex; live OpenAI-first model selection
41	```
42	
43	Existing global and project pins are deliberately not migrated by `chezmoi
44	apply`. Run `copilot-model --auto` once after this upgrade. When `copilot-here`
45	is active, that command refreshes the local role set; otherwise it updates the
46	global one-line main-model state.
47	
48	## How routing works
49	
50	```text
51	Claude Code --Anthropic /v1/messages--> copilot-api (localhost:4141)
52	                                          | Claude: native Messages path
53	                                          | GPT: Anthropic -> Responses translation
54	                                          v
55	                                  GitHub Copilot API
56	```
57	
58	The default package is `@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0`. For GPT ids it translates
59	Claude Code requests to Responses, including `output_config.effort` to
60	`reasoning.effort`. This is required for GPT-5.6 and Claude Code's `ultracode`
61	effort setting; the old `1.13.14` path could replace the requested effort with a
62	hard-coded fallback.
63	
64	The package is installed once under `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg`. Windows
65	uses `npm.cmd` first because it understands the Azure Artifacts credential
66	provider in `~/.npmrc`; Bun remains the fallback/runtime. Readiness is based on
67	the installed `package.json` name/version, a verified stamp, and a runnable launch
68	path—not merely an old directory or binlink. A failed install cannot restamp or
69	launch stale package contents. `COPILOT_API_PKG` accepts registry package specs
70	(name or `@scope/name` with an optional version/tag/range); npm aliases and
71	local/git/URL specs are rejected before filesystem cleanup. Warm starts do no
72	package network work.
73	
74	On a corporate mirror, `ETARGET` can mean the exact public version has not synced
75	yet. Check the registry that npm is actually using before deleting the working
76	prefix:
77	
78	```powershell
79	npm config get registry
80	npm view '@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0' version
81	# Optional comparison where direct public npm is permitted:
82	npm view '@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0' version --registry https://registry.npmjs.org/
83	```
84	
85	If only the configured mirror is missing the version, wait/request mirror sync or
86	use an approved registry for `copilot-proxy reinstall`. The Windows module also
87	falls back automatically to the exact 2.1.0 runtime files on jsDelivr, verifies a
88	baked SHA-256 for every file, then resolves only its ordinary dependencies through
89	the configured npm registry. This handles a lagging mirror without weakening the
90	pin or bypassing the approved feed for the dependency tree. Do not replace the
91	tested exact pin with `latest`.
92	
93	## Model selection and role profile
94	
95	`copilot-model --auto` requires the live `/v1/models` catalog. It prefers served
96	Claude families (`Fable > Opus > Sonnet > Haiku`), then ranks OpenAI by capability:
97	
98	```text
99	Sol > Terra > GPT-5.5 > GPT-5.4 > GPT-5.3 Codex > Luna > mini > Gemini
100	```
101	
102	Luna follows the older flagships because it is the lightweight tier. This role
103	intent follows OpenAI's [current model guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model).
104	For the normal Claude-less Copilot catalog, the generated profile is:
105	
106	| Claude Code role | Copilot model |
107	|---|---|
108	| Main / Fable / Opus | `gpt-5.6-sol` |
109	| Sonnet | `gpt-5.6-terra` |
110	| Haiku / background / legacy small-fast | `gpt-5.6-luna` |
111	
112	A manually selected OpenAI main remains Main/Fable/Opus; Terra and Luna are used
113	for the lower roles when served. Missing tiers fall back to the selected main,
114	never to an unserved hard-coded id. Native Claude profiles select the strongest
115	served model in each Claude family.
116	
117	The `[1m]` suffix is a Claude Code-only context hint. It is derived from each
118	model's live `max_context_window_tokens` metadata when the value is at least one
119	million. Raw API clients must use the plain id. Offline manual discovery remains
120	available, but offline `--auto` refuses to write a potentially stale pin.
121	
122	Both `copilot-run` and `copilot-here on` inject the same variables:
123	
124	```text
125	ANTHROPIC_MODEL
126	ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL
127	ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL
128	ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL
129	ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL
130	ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL
131	```
132	
133	`CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` is intentionally left unset so workflow/frontmatter
134	routing remains authoritative. Restart Claude Code after changing the profile.
135	
136	## Claude Code feature compatibility
137	
138	The useful boundary is local orchestration versus Anthropic cloud services:
139	
140	| Feature | Through Copilot + GPT | Notes |
141	|---|---|---|
142	| CLI, tools, hooks, skills, memory, plugins, MCP, checkpoints, sandboxing | Yes | Local Claude Code features; GPT behavior may differ after prompt/tool translation. |
143	| Subagents and dynamic workflows | Yes | Role variables are provided without overriding workflow-specific subagent routing. See [workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows). |
144	| `ultracode` | Yes on 2.1.0 | It is xhigh effort plus dynamic workflows, not a separate model. |
145	| Thinking/reasoning | Translated | GPT uses Responses reasoning rather than Anthropic-native thinking semantics. |
146	| Web search, fast/auto mode, MCP tool search | Provider-dependent | Availability depends on the Copilot endpoint and gateway translation. |
147	| Ultrareview, Remote Control, Chrome, cloud Code Review, routines, web/mobile/Slack sessions | No | These require Claude.ai authentication/cloud identity; a local API gateway cannot provide it. |
148	
149	See Claude Code's [feature availability](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/feature-availability),
150	[model configuration](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config),
151	[gateway protocol](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol), and
152	[Ultrareview](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview) references.
153	
154	## Network, entitlement and diagnostics
155	
156	- `COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY=auto` reads the Windows System Proxy or an explicit proxy
157	  environment variable, scopes it to the child and passes `--proxy-env`. Node
158	  otherwise ignores the WinINET system setting.
159	- The proxy refreshes its model cache periodically; a restart forces an immediate
160	  refresh. `COPILOT_PROXY_START_TIMEOUT` defaults to 45 seconds because a
161	  Clash/mihomo hop can make the initial refresh exceed the old 20-second budget.
162	- GitHub can vary the catalog by account, organization policy, rollout and egress.
163	  Claude IDs in `/v1/models` are therefore **advertised aliases**, not proof that
164	  inference is authorized. No Claude IDs is not by itself a broken proxy; use
165	  `copilot-model --auto` when you explicitly want to select another served pin.
166	  There is no automatic Claude-to-OpenAI replay after a failed request.
167	- `copilot-proxy doctor` compares direct and proxied upstream catalogs, validates
168	  the main model plus every role alias, and reports stale local pins. `--live`
169	  also compares direct/proxied reachability of remote ChatGPT `codex_apps`, then
170	  sends one real request to the effective configured main model (or a clearly
171	  labeled catalog fallback when that pin is absent). It never retries another
172	  model. Only this inference request consumes quota; timeout and TLS failures are
173	  reported separately.
174	- HTTP 402 with `billing_not_configured` is account-wide and nonretryable. Select
175	  an organization or enterprise under **Usage billed to** at
176	  <https://github.com/settings/copilot/features>. Model changes,
177	  `copilot-model --auto`, and shim toggles cannot repair that account setting.
178	- `copilot-here` writes only the gitignored `.claude/settings.local.json`, never
179	  committed project settings. `off` removes every env key owned by the helper and
180	  preserves unrelated settings.
181	- `claude-copilot` and `claude-copilot-once` retain the Windows port's trusted
182	  `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and optional SpecStory behavior. Plain `claude`
183	  is unaffected.
184	- The throttle shim remains byte-identical to the macOS/Linux copy and retries
185	  transient 403/429 bursts while limiting concurrent requests. It deliberately
186	  passes HTTP 402 through once; billing configuration is not a throttle failure.
187	
188	State lives under `~/.local/state/copilot-proxy/`; device login stores the GitHub
189	token at `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token` without printing it by default.
190	
191	## Codex through the gateway
192	
193	`codex-copilot` and its identical `codex-copilot-once` alias start the local
194	gateway/shim and pass a `copilot_api` Responses provider through one-invocation
195	Codex `-c` overrides. They do not edit user or project Codex config, so plain
196	`codex` is unaffected. An explicit `-m` / `--model` wins; otherwise the live raw
197	catalog is ranked OpenAI/Codex first (`Sol > Terra > GPT-5.5 > GPT-5.4 > GPT-5.3
198	Codex > Luna > mini`), then Claude, Gemini and other chat models. Disabled and
199	embedding models are excluded.
200	
201	Codex always uses the shim on `localhost:4142`, even when the persisted
202	throttling toggle is off. Besides throttling, that boundary normalizes blank
203	descriptions in Codex `mcp_list_tools` Responses items. GitHub Copilot rejects
204	those with `Invalid 'input[0].tools[0].description': empty string`, while MCP
205	servers and the native Codex path may omit them. The shim fills only those tool
206	definition fields and leaves prompts, schemas, and tool names unchanged.
207	Codex currently zstd-compresses these requests; the shim decodes only the
208	Responses body it must repair, forwards ordinary JSON, and removes the stale
209	`content-encoding` header.
210	
211	This is a separate picker from Claude Code's `copilot-model --auto`: that path
212	remains Claude-first, while only the Codex launcher is OpenAI-first.
213	
214	SpecStory is automatic when installed. The wrapper preserves the effective
215	`codex_cmd` (project config > user config > bare `codex`) before appending
216	provider/model/user arguments; `--no-specstory` runs Codex directly. Claude and
217	Gemini fallback through Responses Lite, which does not support Responses
218	`tool_search`, so native Responses OpenAI models stay ahead of Anthropic.
219	The launcher also enables gateway-backed remote compaction and excludes the
220	`mcp__codex_apps__sites` namespace that depends on unavailable `tool_search`;
221	later explicit `-c` arguments can override either setting per invocation.
222	
223	`codex_apps` itself is not a localhost service and not an Apple-Silicon-only
224	Codex Desktop bridge. It is a remote MCP at
225	`https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/apps`, so startup can fail even while
226	Copilot inference on `localhost:4142` works. Keep Apps enabled and use
227	`copilot-proxy doctor --live` to diagnose that route independently.
228	
229	There is deliberately no Codex equivalent of `copilot-here`: project
230	`.codex/config.toml` cannot override provider definitions, provider selection or
231	auth metadata. The explicit launcher provides project/session scope without
232	changing the user-wide default.
233	
234	### Experimental direct configuration
235	
236	The direct `model_providers.copilot-enterprise` example is documented in the
237	macOS/Linux guide rather than installed. It is not the localhost proxy path, and
238	the pasted `gh auth token` flow is not portable: on the tested EMU account it
239	returned `421`/`403`, while the credential stored by `copilot-proxy auth` plus
240	the normal short-lived Copilot token exchange worked. The supported launcher
241	therefore uses the authenticated local gateway.
242
```

185	`Invalid 'input[0].tools[0].description': empty string` 拒絕請求。shim 只補這些
186	tool definition 欄位，不改 prompt、schema 或 tool name。
187	目前 Codex 會以 zstd 壓縮這些請求；shim 只解壓需要修補的 Responses body，改以
188	普通 JSON 轉送，並移除已不適用的 `content-encoding` header。
189	
190	這是與 Claude Code `copilot-model --auto` 分開的 picker：後者保持
191	Claude-first，只有 Codex launcher 是 OpenAI-first。
192	
193	有安裝 SpecStory 時自動整合。Wrapper 會保留生效的 `codex_cmd`（project config >
194	user config > 裸 `codex`），再附加 provider/model/user arguments；
195	`--no-specstory` 直接執行 Codex。Claude/Gemini fallback 經 Responses Lite，不支援
196	Responses `tool_search`，因此 native Responses OpenAI models 排在 Anthropic 前。
197	Launcher 也會啟用 gateway-backed remote compaction，並排除依賴不可用
198	`tool_search` 的 `mcp__codex_apps__sites` namespace；後續明確傳入的 `-c`
199	仍可在單次呼叫覆寫這兩項。
200	
201	`codex_apps` 本身不是 localhost service，也不是 Apple-Silicon-only Codex Desktop
202	bridge；它是 `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/apps` 的遠端 MCP。因此即使
203	`localhost:4142` inference 正常，它仍可能啟動失敗。保留 Apps 啟用，並以
204	`copilot-proxy doctor --live` 獨立診斷這條路由。
205	
206	刻意不做 Codex 版 `copilot-here`：project `.codex/config.toml` 不能覆寫 provider
207	definition、provider selection 或 auth metadata。顯式 launcher 能提供 project/session
208	scope，同時不改 user-wide default。
209	
210	### 實驗性 direct 設定
211	
212	Direct `model_providers.copilot-enterprise` 範例只記錄在 macOS/Linux 完整指南，
213	不會安裝。它不是 localhost proxy 路徑，而且貼文中的 `gh auth token` flow 不具可攜性：
214	本次 EMU 帳號實測回 `421`/`403`；`copilot-proxy auth` 保存的 credential 加正常短效
215	Copilot token exchange 則可用。因此正式 launcher 使用已認證的本機 gateway。

6	# dotfiles-windows
7	
8	This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** dotfiles repo targeting **native
9	Windows + PowerShell 7**. Packages install via **scoop** (CLI) + **winget** (GUI) —
10	there is no ansible here. Repo: <https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows>.
11	(macOS/Linux/WSL are handled by the separate `daviddwlee84/dotfiles` repo.)
12	
13	## Orientation
14	- Source dir: `chezmoi source-path` — edit there (`cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`).
15	- Preview / apply: `chezmoi diff` / `chezmoi apply` (or `just diff` / `just apply`).
16	- Source of a target: `chezmoi source-path <path>`; render without applying: `chezmoi cat <path>`.
17	- Re-run init prompts: `chezmoi init` (answers persist in `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`).
18	- `docs/**`, `editors/**`, `scripts/**` are chezmoi-ignored (not deployed).
19	
20	## Shell layout (pwsh)
21	- `$PROFILE` (`~/Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1`) is a loader
22	  that dot-sources `~/.config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1` in sorted order, then
23	  `~/.config/powershell/local.ps1` (untracked user override, loaded last).
24	- Fragments: `00_env` (PATH/XDG/env), `10_tools` (starship, zoxide, atuin,
25	  fzf, direnv, tv), `20_aliases` (`ll`/`gs`/`reload`/`cas`/`cau`/`chezmoi-cd`/`run-for`),
26	  `25_herdr` (`hvibe`/`hcode`/`hhere`/`hroot`/`hmark` workspace helpers, gated on herdr),
27	  `30_apps` (`applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/`sysvol`/`sysmute`/`x`), `35_yazi` (`y`),
28	  `40_copilot` (imports the Copilot module), `90_psreadline` (vi-mode gated on `enableVimMode`).
29	
30	## Packages
31	- `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` is the **single source of
32	  truth** for installs, gated by the init toggles. scoop = CLI tools, winget = GUI
33	  apps, npm = AI agents, PSGallery = PSFzf/AudioDeviceCmdlets. Fault-tolerant: one
34	  failed package is collected + reported, never aborts the apply.
35	- Package sources are defined once in `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1` and
36	  reused by the installer and `profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`: managed machines
37	  use company PyPI/npm pull-through registries; otherwise the China-mirror toggle
38	  selects GFW mirrors. Managed-machine policy wins if both toggles are true.
39	- Install ≠ upgrade: `chezmoi apply` only installs what's missing; upgrade via
40	  `just upgrade-scoop` / `just upgrade-winget`.
41	
42	## copilot-proxy
43	- Module at `~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot`. Commands: `copilot-proxy`
44	  (`start`/`stop`/`restart`/`status`/`doctor`/`logs`/`shim`/`whoami`/`auth`/`reinstall`),
45	  `copilot-run`, `claude-copilot`, `claude-copilot-once`, `copilot-here`,
46	  `copilot-model` (incl. `--auto`), `copilot-embed`, `semsearch`.
47	- Needs `bun`. Token: `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`. Ports 4141 (proxy) /
48	  4142 (throttle shim). Default main model `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]`; the OpenAI role
49	  profile maps Fable/Opus to Sol, Sonnet to Terra, and Haiku/background to Luna.
50	  `copilot-here` writes

53	  `COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY` (auto|always|never|URL) controls whether Node fetches the

59	- Windows Terminal `profiles.defaults`, Alacritty (`%APPDATA%\alacritty\alacritty.toml`),

11	#      model has across sources into one key, or the stale-cache diff reports
12	#      false positives on every run:

15	#        proxy alias     : claude-opus-4-8[1m]   (Claude Code-only suffix)

443	# End-to-end against a mock upstream that withholds its response headers the way
444	# copilot-api does while a reasoning model thinks. Guards the four-way split the
445	# keepalive introduced; see pitfalls/copilot-proxy-openai-model-silent-stall.md.
446	@test "shim keepalive fires only on slow streams, leaving fast + non-stream untouched" {
447	  command -v bun >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "bun not installed"
448	  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not installed"
449	  local shim="$SOURCE_DIR/dot_config/shell/copilot-throttle-shim.js"
450	  cat >"$TMP/keepalive.js" <<'JS'
451	const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
452	const up = Bun.serve({ port: 0, idleTimeout: 60, async fetch(req) {
453	  const u = new URL(req.url);
454	  await sleep(Number(u.searchParams.get("delay") ?? 0));
455	  if (u.searchParams.get("mode") === "status")
456	    return new Response('{"error":"nope"}', { status: 400, headers: { "content-type": "application/json" } });
457	  return new Response("event: message_start\ndata: {}\n\nevent: message_stop\ndata: {}\n\n",
458	    { headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" } });
459	} });
460	process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_PORT = "0";
461	process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_UPSTREAM = `http://localhost:${up.port}`;
462	process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_PING_MS = "150";
463	process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_PING_AFTER_MS = "100";
464	process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_STALL_MS = "5000";
465	const { startServer } = await import(process.argv[2]);
466	const shim = startServer();
467	const call = async (q, stream = true) => {
468	  const r = await fetch(`http://localhost:${shim.port}/v1/messages${q}`, { method: "POST",
469	    headers: { "content-type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ model: "m", stream }) });
470	  const body = await r.text();
471	  return { status: r.status, ct: r.headers.get("content-type"),
472	    pings: (body.match(/^: /gm) ?? []).length,
473	    events: (body.match(/^event: (\S+)/gm) ?? []).map((s) => s.slice(7)) };
474	};
475	const out = {

797	# Error bodies appear as direct code/message pairs, error.code/error.message, or
798	# another JSON error encoded inside error.message. Normalize all three shapes.
799	function script:Get-CopilotApiError {
800	    param($Body, [int] $Depth = 0)
801	    $raw = ConvertTo-CopilotCompactText $Body
802	    if ($Depth -gt 4) {
803	        return [pscustomobject]@{ Code = $null; Message = $null; Raw = $raw }
804	    }
805	
806	    $object = $Body
807	    if ($Body -is [string]) {
808	        try { $object = $Body | ConvertFrom-Json -ErrorAction Stop }
809	        catch { return [pscustomobject]@{ Code = $null; Message = $null; Raw = $raw } }
810	    }
811	    if (-not $object) { return [pscustomobject]@{ Code = $null; Message = $null; Raw = $raw } }
812	
813	    $container = $object
814	    if ($object.PSObject.Properties['error']) {
815	        $container = $object.error
816	        if ($container -is [string]) {
817	            $nestedError = Get-CopilotApiError -Body $container -Depth ($Depth + 1)
818	            if ($nestedError.Code -or $nestedError.Message) { return $nestedError }
819	        }
820	    }
821	
822	    $code = if ($container.PSObject.Properties['code']) { [string]$container.code } else { $null }
823	    $message = if ($container.PSObject.Properties['message']) { [string]$container.message } else { $null }
824	    if ($message -and $message.TrimStart().StartsWith('{')) {
825	        $nestedMessage = Get-CopilotApiError -Body $message -Depth ($Depth + 1)
826	        if ($nestedMessage.Code -or $nestedMessage.Message) {
827	            return [pscustomobject]@{
828	                Code    = if ($nestedMessage.Code) { $nestedMessage.Code } else { $code }
829	                Message = if ($nestedMessage.Message) { $nestedMessage.Message } else { $message }
830	                Raw     = $raw
831	            }
832	        }
833	    }
834	    [pscustomobject]@{ Code = $code; Message = $message; Raw = $raw }
835	}

837	function script:Classify-CopilotInferenceError {
838	    param([int] $StatusCode, $Body)
839	    $errorInfo = Get-CopilotApiError -Body $Body
840	    $code = ([string]$errorInfo.Code).ToLowerInvariant()
841	    $detailParts = @($errorInfo.Code, $errorInfo.Message) | Where-Object { $_ }
842	    $detail = $detailParts -join ': '
843	    if (-not $detail) { $detail = $errorInfo.Raw }
844	
845	    if ($StatusCode -eq 402 -and $code -eq 'billing_not_configured') {
846	        return [pscustomobject]@{
847	            Kind        = 'BillingNotConfigured'
848	            Code        = $errorInfo.Code
849	            Message     = $errorInfo.Message
850	            Summary     = "account-wide GitHub Copilot billing is not configured: $detail"
851	            Retryable   = $false
852	            AccountWide = $true
853	            Action      = 'https://github.com/settings/copilot/features'
854	            Guidance    = 'Select an organization or enterprise in GitHub''s "Usage billed to" setting. Changing the model, using --auto, or enabling the shim cannot fix this account-wide failure.'
855	        }
856	    }
857	
858	    if ($code -match '^(model_not_supported|model_unsupported|unsupported_model)$') {
859	        return [pscustomobject]@{
860	            Kind        = 'ModelUnsupported'
861	            Code        = $errorInfo.Code
862	            Message     = $errorInfo.Message
863	            Summary     = $detail
864	            Retryable   = $false
865	            AccountWide = $false
866	            Action      = 'Run copilot-model --auto, or copilot-model -l and select a model advertised by the live catalog.'
867	            Guidance    = $null
868	        }
869	    }
870	
871	    [pscustomobject]@{
872	        Kind        = 'HttpError'
873	        Code        = $errorInfo.Code
874	        Message     = $errorInfo.Message
875	        Summary     = $detail
876	        Retryable   = ($StatusCode -eq 429 -or $StatusCode -ge 500)
877	        AccountWide = $false
878	        Action      = $null
879	        Guidance    = $null
880	    }
881	}

883	# Convert a raw proxy id to the spelling Claude Code should receive. A live
884	# max_context_window_tokens >= 1M earns [1m]. Offline, preserve an explicitly
885	# stored suffix but do not invent one.
886	function script:ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel {
887	    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Model, $Catalog)
888	    $hadHint = $Model -match '\[1m\]$'
889	    $raw = Remove-CopilotContextHint $Model
890	    if (-not $PSBoundParameters.ContainsKey('Catalog')) { $Catalog = Get-CopilotModelCatalog }
891	    if ($Catalog) {
892	        $entry = $Catalog.data | Where-Object { $_.id -eq $raw } | Select-Object -First 1
893	        $context = $entry.capabilities.limits.max_context_window_tokens
894	        if ($context -and [long]$context -ge 1000000) { return "$raw[1m]" }
895	        return $raw
896	    }
897	    if ($hadHint) { return "$raw[1m]" }
898	    $raw
899	}
